Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez reveals desire to join club in future just weeks after Man City transfer
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez reveals desire to join club in future just weeks after Man City transfer

Enzo Fernandez has signalled his intention of returning to River Plate before the end of his playing career.

Fernandez has reached ten appearances for Manchester City since his £125million move from rivals Chelsea in the summer.

2 Fernandez only joined City less than two months ago, but has already eyed a future spell elsewhere Credit: Getty

Viewed as one of the world's best midfielders, the 25-year-old started out in the River Plate academy before featuring for the senior side.

He has since played for Benfica, Chelsea and City, but he has made it clear he intends on a second spell in his native Argentina.

What has Enzo Fernandez said about his future?

"I want to return to River, I've said it a lot of times and every time I have the opportunity," he told Los Edul, as per ESPN. "I would love to and I will return at some point, for sure. It's something I really want."

Fernandez then insisted he won't back down from his claim, adding: "It's OK. I'll take care of the record. If I say it, it's because I feel it.

"I need to return to River to win things and enjoy the River world for more years than I've been here."

Whilst he is eyeing a return to River Plate, the 2022 World Cup winner shut down the idea of it happening soon amid his recent City move.

He stressed: "I'm here, I have a long contract in Manchester, there's a long way to go before that."

Fernandez's career from River Plate to City

At boyhood club River Plate, Fernandez hit 12 goals and ten assists in 53 appearances from 2020 to 2022.

He won the Argentine top-flight title and cup throughout this spell, which also featured a loan to Defensa y Justicia.

There, Fernandez lifted the Copa Sudamericana - the South American equivalent of the Europa League - and Recopa Sudamericana - where the Sudamericana winners face the Copa Libertadores champions.

2 Fernandez has made it clear that he wants to return to River Plate, the first club of his professional career Credit: Getty

Benfica signed him in June 2022, and he was part of their Portuguese league title success in the following season.

However, he left halfway through for Chelsea in a £106.8m move after his excellent performance for Argentina at the World Cup, where he won the Young Player Award.

Fernandez totalled 170 appearances for the Blues with 31 goals and 30 assists, and collected winners' medals in the Club World Cup and Conference League.

Earlier in 2026, he fuelled rumours of a move to Real Madrid, only for the Spanish club to dismiss any plans of bringing him to the club.

City then became interested and completed a signing on the last day of the summer window.

Fernandez has reunited with Enzo Maresca, who was his head coach at Chelsea, and scored his first City goal in the 5-3 Premier League win over Sunderland.

Sports.title: Aston Villa threaten legal action against Jamie Carragher after pundit claimed Unai Emery should replace Michael Carrick at Man United and told fans to 'shut the f*** up'
Sports.content:
Aston Villa last night made the bombshell claim that they intend to take legal action against Jamie Carragher.

In a statement on club channels carrying the name of co-owner Nassef Sawiris, Villa wrote: ‘Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans.

‘Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.’

Television pundit Carragher believes Emery would be the ideal manager of Manchester United if they decided to sack Michael Carrick.

That has prompted a furious response from Villa fans on social media.

Carragher doubled down on his view on The Overlap podcast this week, in which he told ‘Aston Villa fans’ to ‘shut the f*** up.

Aston Villa have decided to launch legal action against Jamie Carragher in a row over his comments about Unai Emery

‘I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year. That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year.

'But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three or four times (Emery has won it five times) surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

‘Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.

'But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.’

Sports.title: 'Divisive' teacher's pet who players roll their eyes at? Or obsessive who truly cares? Man United insiders reveal what Bruno Fernandes' team-mates really think of him - as we reveal Michael Carrick decided to drop captain BEFORE his Como rant
Sports.content:
'Divisive' teacher's pet who players roll their eyes at? Or obsessive who truly cares? Man United insiders reveal what Bruno Fernandes' team-mates really think of him - as we reveal Michael Carrick decided to drop captain BEFORE his Como rant

The expression on the faces of Manchester United’s players turned to shock and shame as they left the pitch at Old Trafford on Sunday and ran the gauntlet of fan anger.

No sooner had head coach Michael Carrick been cheered down the tunnel after a 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth left him on the brink of the sack than supporters rounded on the team and a torrent of abuse rained down from the Stretford End.

‘It was a wake-up for all the players,’ one source told Daily Mail Sport this week.

For captain Bruno Fernandes, it was a particularly painful moment. Fernandes was still in his tracksuit bottoms and hoodie having been dropped to the bench and left there to stew by Carrick as United’s season hit a new low.

He is used to the adoration of fans, but their reaction was muted to say the least when he left the dugout to warm up in the second half.

It was the culmination of the hardest two weeks of Fernandes’ seven-year career at United.

Bruno Fernandes has had the hardest two weeks of his Man United career. The lowest point came when he was hooked off in a 4-1 defeat in Como - then took aim at Michael Carrick in his post-match interview

Fernandes was left on the bench for United's loss to Bournemouth, and didn't receive the adulation he's used to getting from the home supporters at Old Trafford

The 32-year-old was struggling for form and fitness this season long before Carrick replaced him in the 67th minute of the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.

Afterwards, he was accused of throwing his head coach under the bus by publicly blaming the tactics and lack of bravery for United’s worst European defeat in 32 years.

Fernandes was unaware at the time that his family home in Cheshire had been raided by a gang of three burglars during the game, and only found out as United set off for Manchester. Thankfully, his wife Ana and their two children were away on holiday.

It’s understood Carrick had already made the bold decision to drop Fernandes for the first time in five years, and make Harry Maguire captain against Bournemouth, even before hearing about his comments.

Despite liking an Instagram post saying ‘never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care’ after the Bournemouth defeat, Fernandes is said to have taken Carrick’s decision on the chin when the team was named on Saturday, just as he has accepted playing in a wider position over recent weeks while Youri Tielemans has stepped into the No 10 role.

Although Carrick and Fernandes were both at Carrington on Monday as speculation raged over the head coach’s future, the player had left before Carrick turned up just before 2pm. The Portuguese was having treatment on a niggling injury that has troubled him since the World Cup.

Once United had clarified Carrick’s position, the two men met at the training ground and cleared the air on Tuesday.

Carrick has since confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain and is set to lead the side against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge this lunchtime in what is a huge game for United and their manager.

Others have been less forgiving. Jamie Carragher branded Fernandes’ comments in Como ‘disgraceful’, while Alan Shearer believes he has tarnished his legacy at Old Trafford.

Carrick and Fernandes have cleared the air at Carrington and Fernandes will remain as United's captain, starting at Chelsea today

But the Portuguese's actions have reignited the debate over whether Fernandes is too emotional to wear the armband

The controversy has reignited the debate over whether Fernandes is too emotional to wear the armband. Former United boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer said so in a video clip that resurfaced last week, explaining why he preferred Maguire.

That was put to Carrick, who was part of Solskjaer’s coaching team at the time, and he said: ‘There are different personalities, characteristics and ways to lead.

‘The questions get asked, and I understand why you're asking them now. He cares deeply about this football club and about the team and he's desperate to do well.’

It is a view backed up by some sources who describe a football obsessive who takes United’s problems to heart and feels the pain of the alarming slump this season just as keenly as the fans. While other players have distractions away from the pitch (too many in Gary Neville’s opinion), they say Fernandes can find no escape.

He is understood to have been worn down by yet another United crisis just when it seemed the good times were coming back under Carrick. Inevitably, that has taken its toll and has not been helped by worries over his future at Old Trafford as talks over a new contract drag on.

Insiders describe him as ‘an emotional metronome’ who sets the mood around the club, both good and bad. They say he bonds the dressing room together, and question who else in the United squad should wear the armband.

However, some of Fernandes’ team-mates in recent years have seen him as a more divisive figure whose close relationship with Ruben Amorim was viewed with suspicion.

‘The players can be quite dismissive of him,’ said a source close to one. ‘Sometimes they roll their eyes when he’s talking.’

Not surprisingly, Fernandes’ form has suffered this season with his four goals and one assist coming in United’s only two wins against Ipswich Town and Sabah – months after he picked up the Premier League Player of the Year award for his nine goals and Premier League record 21 assists last term.

He brought his trophy into Carrington and posed for individual pictures with staff from the treatment room to the canteen to thank them for the part they played in his success.

‘The players can be quite dismissive of him,’ said a source close to one of Fernandes' team-mates. ‘Sometimes they roll their eyes when he’s talking’

Insiders describe him as ‘an emotional metronome’ who sets the mood around the club, both good and bad

‘He has been the club's best player over the past few seasons and we need to get the best out of him for this team to succeed,’ legendary United captain Bryan Robson told Daily Mail Sport.

‘I have always thought a captain should be a centre back or deep-lying midfielder so they can see the game and spot things when they go wrong.

‘The trouble for Bruno is he is playing in a more advanced position because we have no centre forward. He's constantly looking over his shoulder and not necessarily expending his energy in the right way.

‘He gets how important it is to keep the group together. I know he has been instrumental as captain in organising bonding dinners and days out. That helps, but he also must know the importance of keeping things in the dressing room.’

With the Como controversy behind him, Fernandes is said to have returned to being the best version of himself during what has been a turbulent week for everyone at United.

Stung by the reaction from fans on Sunday, he has taken what is described as ‘direct action’ to lift the rest of the players and confront the crisis, as a captain should. Now another test of his leadership awaits at Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Why Burnley gambled on Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss inspired by Che Guevara who boxes, dances and was an electrical engineer, to spark their season back to life - and why his new players are already worried about him
Sports.content:
Why Burnley gambled on Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss inspired by Che Guevara who boxes, dances and was an electrical engineer, to spark their season back to life - and why his new players are already worried about him

Not many football managers have a tattoo of Che Guevara, dance in their free time and speak five languages.

But they are just three quirks which add to the layers of intrigue around Burnley's new boss Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss tasked with saving the Clarets from double relegation and dropping into the third tier for the first time since 2000.

After four wins in the last year, with morale in the gutter, Burnley announced Celestini as Nicky Hayen's successor on Wednesday. Many fans will have dropped their marmalade. Who? Celestini's CV is promising but this is an almighty gamble and they cannot afford for things to go wrong.

The Clarets sit 22nd in the Championship and have won just one home game inside 90 minutes in 2026. Their summer was an unmitigated disaster – they had woeful pre-season results, went 71 days without a manager, sold last campaign's top scorer Zian Flemming on deadline day with no replacement, and their chief executive, James Holroyd, walked out in September after difficulties working alongside chairman Alan Pace.

The club is in £142million of debt, according to their latest accounts, with £13m in cash in the coffers. The phrase 'basket case' comes to mind.

Celestini's appointment falls squarely on the shoulders of new chief football officer Diego Lopez, another stranger to English football, and it is one Burnley's players are unsure about.

Fabio Celestini is facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation with Burnley, who sit 22nd in the Championship

Belgian boss Nicky Hayen lasted just 12 league matches - and won only once

Burnley have not been in the third tier since 2000 but are staring down the barrel of a second successive relegation

Daily Mail Sport understands that some members of the squad have reservations about Celestini's style of play – he has favoured a possession-based 4-2-3-1 throughout his career, a system which Hayen tried and failed to implement during his time in charge.

Many clubs have turned to outsiders and succeeded – just look at table-toppers Middlesbrough under Kim Hellberg – but the lack of Championship experience in Burnley's management structure leaves Celestini to navigate a steep learning curve without much support.

On the bright side, Celestini inherited a similarly shambolic case at Basel in October 2023 and thrived. The Swiss giants were bottom of the table and had had to cancel their goal of the month award, because they hadn't scored any. Celestini saved them from relegation, restored the feel-good factor by re-signing club legend Xherdan Shaqiri, and won them the league and cup double the following season.

The 50-year-old former Switzerland midfielder – who won 35 caps for his country and played against England's Golden Generation at Euro 2004 – also has a promotion on his ledger from his time at Lausanne and a Swiss Cup with Luzern. He also led Lugano into Europe and managed Sion.

'Celestini is a determined, ambitious personality, but he can also be a stubborn coach and that has caused issues at several clubs,' Swiss football expert Craig King (@FootballSwissEN on X) tells Daily Mail Sport.

'He is capable of providing clubs with a short-term bounce before it eventually deteriorates. He has strong ideas, but his stubbornness often tends to rub people the wrong way.

'It seems that inevitably, he loses control of his teams somewhere along the way and can never get them back on track.'

His time at Russian giants CSKA Moscow, last season after he left Basel, followed that trend. He had found out about their interest on a holiday with his dancer wife, Fanny, in the Seychelles, and took the plunge, rocking up with a Spanish-speaking coaching coterie. He even appointed his wife to help edit video clips for analysis and support in aspects of communication, a club source tells Daily Mail Sport.

He enjoyed a strong start at CSKA – he won the Russian Super Cup in his first match and they led the Russian Premier League after 11 games. Going into the winter break, they were just four points off top in fourth.

'Fabio has done a tremendous job,' the club's general director Roman Babaev said during that hiatus. 'There was beautiful football.'

By the end of Celestini's tenure in May, Babaev was describing a 'lack of self-confidence and a lack of belief in their ability to turn the situation around'. He added: 'We agreed that things could only get worse – the head coach doubted the team was listening to him.'

Celestini won 35 caps for Switzerland and appeared against England at Euro 2004

Burnley are Celestini's eighth club as a manager, having left CSKA Moscow by mutual consent in May

What changed? Reports in Russia claimed that over the winter break, players had been unimpressed with the lack of physical and defensive work, with too much emphasis on attacking and set-pieces. They lost their first three games back after the break, suffered a humbling 4-0 thrashing by Krasnodar in the Russian Cup, and went winless in Celestini's final five matches in charge.

In the space of two months, everything had unravelled. After defender Moises was sent off in the drubbing at Krasnodar, Celestini reprimanded the player in the dressing room – but the Brazilian hit back, questioning his manager's competence in front of the team. Moises was subsequently suspended and the club took Celestini's side.

'I felt like something was missing, I wasn't feeling well, something wasn't right. Other players started saying they weren't feeling well,' Moises later reflected in the documentary We Are CSKA. 'To become a champion, you need to cleanse yourself of all dirt. I blurted it all out because I knew what was simmering inside us all.'

Celestini is still well thought of at CSKA and was always willing to take accountability rather than criticise his players publicly. Former manager Viktor Goncharenko claimed that he ultimately failed because he 'didn't find common ground with the CSKA veterans', such as legendary goalkeeper Igor Akinfeev, and didn't have enough Russian coaches. He left with the club sixth in the table.

Celestini's task now is to turn around a flailing Burnley. His first assignment will be on Saturday at Turf Moor against in-form Portsmouth. Based off how he describes himself, he does not come across as a disciplinarian. Celestini says he does not like implementing fines and is not a fan of throwing things across a dressing room.

'This kind of half-time behavior might only work once a season,' he once said. 'It's like an electric shock.'

At his heart Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana.

His tattoo of Cuban revolutionary Guevara cost 180 Swiss francs (£163). He has lost count of his tattoos by now, also inking his kids and a depiction of good triumphing over evil.

Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana

Daily Mail Sport understands some Burnley players have reservations about Celestini's possession-based 4-2-3-1, a system which Hayen failed to implement

'I started reading about (Guevara), studying him. My tattoo depicts him without his military beret. There are no political references,' he said. 'What attracts me to him is that he fought his whole life for those who had nothing to do with him, and I've also fought a lot in my life, so I decided to get it.'

Another of his heroes is Nelson Mandela: 'He also dedicated his entire life to his ideas. Anyone who fought for their ideals is important to me. I admire people who take the time to help others. I don’t consider myself a good person, but I’m not a hypocrite.'

Away from football, Celestini – who speaks Italian, French, Spanish, German and English – also dances with his wife and enjoys boxing. A former electrical draughtsman, he has a good work ethic and, we hear, made a strong push for the Burnley job.

A source at the Clarets, who were also interested in Rob Edwards and Carlos Corberan, insists that Celestini was their first choice. Now they are counting on him to deliver a minor miracle.

Sports.title: RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: Here's what I've heard privately about Max Dowman that proves he will come out of Mikel Arteta scolding a stronger player - and why he'll have dealt with far worse already
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta didn’t require the hysteria of the past week to know a thing or two about dubious reactions. Before we get onto his reaction to Max Dowman’s reaction, or the wider reaction to those reactions, we might revisit something that happened in November 2010.

That’s a long journey into the past, but the episode tells us a little about Arteta’s feelings for opponents who took liberties with his shins. The abbreviated version: violence would be returned with spectacular amounts of interest.

The longer telling revolves around a match between Arteta’s Everton and West Brom. To rewatch some of the footage now, we would say Gonzalo Jara brought it upon himself after 58 minutes, when in a mad passage he elbowed Leighton Baines and then barged shoulder-first into Steven Pienaar in the same scramble for a loose ball.

The defining act came next – Arteta stepped in to retrieve possession, but was clattered by Jara with one of those nasty scissor-motion tackles that could break the standing leg. If that sounds familiar, it’s because the challenge was near-identical to the lunge by Fleetwood Town’s Harrison Neal that provoked Dowman on Tuesday night.

But Arteta didn’t kick Jara, as Dowman did Neal. No, he stomped on his leg. Twice, actually. And with venom in each.

Arsenal's 16-year-old Max Dowman gets an earful from his manager Mikel Arteta after the attacker was sent off on Tuesday night against Fleetwood

It was a frustrating night for Dowman who failed to live up to the excitement that surrounds him

Dowman was around 11 months old when this happened, so he’ll have no idea about all that. And besides, he’d probably be wise to avoid bringing it up. Aged 16, his sense of which battles to pick will be growing by the hour.

But Arteta was 28 when he turned vigilante against West Brom. And it wasn’t quite an isolated incident.

Seven months earlier, Morten Gamst Pedersen stepped on Arteta’s ankle in a game against Blackburn and the Spaniard didn’t like it. His response? He poked Pedersen in the eye and got a yellow.

So let’s offer a couple of conclusions at this point.

One is about Arteta – if he wishes to present himself as a poster boy for the zen state and self-control in football matches, then he might need to torch a few archives. The two yellow cards he has collected on the touchline this season would suggest his own journey to enlightenment is ongoing.

The second, more meaningful conclusion centres on the general theme that Dowman should have been preserved from a few chilly words and a colder stare from his manager.

In the aftermath of Arsenal’s defeat at Fleetwood, that peculiar stance has been propagated by Paul Merson and Gabby Agbonlahor, who were among the vocal cohort that bristled and recoiled at the sight of a young pro being sent to the dressing room without a cuddle. The backlash against Arteta almost sounded as if he had abdicated a duty of care. Of all the reactions in this saga, I found that the strangest.

When Arteta addressed the matter on Friday, his justification felt far closer to the mark: ‘You have to understand the context. We’re not in Disneyland, we’re in the Premier League.'

If Arteta wishes to present himself as a poster boy for the zen state and self-control in football matches, then he might wish to explain why he gets booked so often

Morten Gamst Pedersen is left reeling after a clash with Arteta in his Everton days. A few years later Arteta would poke Pedersen in the eye during a game at Ewood Park

A hypocrite on the subject of retaliations? Yes, we can go with that. Wrong in his handling of a young player who lost his cool? No. Definitely not.

At 16, we can say Dowman meets the legal definition of a child, and a bloody talented one at that, but he’s not a kid. Kids don’t get into the Arsenal first team. Kids wouldn’t survive the hothouse of a Premier League academy.

To understand why that might be, it is instructive to look back to an update on the Arsenal website from the summer. On June 4, as they do every year, they put out a few words to detail which of their Under 18s and Under 21s had not made the grade, which was a list that included the names of Harrison Dudziak, Seb Ferdinand, Cam’ron Ismail, Will Sweet and Josh Nichols.

As very good players, they were all in the Arsenal Under 19s squad in 2024, when Dowman, aged 14, became the youngest scorer in the UEFA Youth League's history against Atalanta.

Of the starting XI that day, only four remain at Arsenal, and the point is this – Dowman has lived through the brutalities of that whittling process every summer and he will have been friends with those who had their dreams ended.

He will have been hardened by their traumas and solidified by knowing what it takes to stay standing in that world.

In short, when we attempt to imagine his position, and wonder how a cold shoulder might feel to a Gen Z child in the Arsenal team, we do so without the relevant context.

Because Dowman was never in Disneyland. A Premier League academy, even an excellent and caring one like that at Arsenal, will inevitably be more like a trip to the Hunger Games. Dowman has been there since he was five, so let’s assume it will take more than a mildly disappointed manager to hurt his feelings.

An incensed Dowman grapples with the Fleetwood Town players just before being sent off on Tuesday night

Dowman has not appeared flustered while he has passed milestones at breakneck speed in his short career so far

Based on everything I’ve heard privately and publicly about Dowman, his reaction to the reaction chain will go the other way. He’s a tremendously promising player and has a strong mind with good people behind him – it’s why he has not been flustered by any of the milestones he has passed at breakneck speed.

The wobbles, like the one at Fleetwood and shortly before that with England Under 19s, are few. But they are also useful, based on the truism that we all learn more when things go wrong. Viewed through that lens, Arteta’s worst possible response would be to indulge a blip or pretend it never happened. As an excellent manager, he hasn’t done that.

It is too early to say how far Dowman will go in his career. Likewise, we have no idea if he will shape into the kind of player who jabs a finger into the occasional eye or plants studs in any thighs. His reaction to Neal on Tuesday was certainly at the Disney-end of that scale.

But Dowman’s chances of succeeding will only be increased by learning where the margins exist. As with a few other facets of his game, he is ahead of the curve.

Does Mbappe really need China's money?

A confession: I find the Kylian Mbappe ‘dictator’ memes funny. If you haven’t seen them, the gist is pretty simple – someone once decided that he carries himself like a dictator and subsequently imposed his head on the bodies and uniforms of a few notorious figures from history.

One of those was Chairman Mao Zedong and Mbappe’s own amusement at that fact is why he was forced onto the journey of 1,000 apologies this week.

In China, where it remains taboo to query Mao’s actions in any way, Mbappe has since had multiple sponsorships cancelled and a diplomatic row has swirled, with the upshot that a state-controlled broadcaster is now refusing to screen his matches.

The space here is too short to relitigate the deaths of millions of people under Mao’s reign, but Mbappe might have cause to wonder if he ever really needed Chinese money that badly.

Kylian Mbappe got himself into hot water this week by finding a Chairman Mao meme amusing. He has now had sponsorship deals in China canned

Welcome back, Sergio!

With a tail tucked between his legs, Sergio Garcia has announced his return to the DP World Tour after the demise of LIV.

Aside from saying he is ‘proud’ to be going back, Garcia adds that he is ‘excited’ to ‘strengthen personal relationships’ with those he left behind in 2022.

Based on multiple conversations I have had with leading players from the Tour, including a well-known name who has regularly described Garcia as a ‘total a**e’ since his defection, that excitement is remarkably one-sided.

Sports.title: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson SPLIT: NFL icon, 74, and cheerleader girlfriend, 25, have 'called it quits... and she already has a new man'
Sports.content:
Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson SPLIT: NFL icon, 74, and cheerleader girlfriend, 25, have 'called it quits... and she already has a new man'

NFL legend Bill Belichick and his cheerleader girlfriend Jordon Hudson have called it quits and are no longer dating, according to a bombshell new report.

In fact, TMZ claims the high-profile pair called time on their age-gap romance late last year – and Jordon has even begun dating new men.

The outlet reports that they are 'still close friends and remain committed to their business partnerships,' despite their secret split.

The legendary former New England Patriots coach, 74, started dating the cheerleader, 25, back in 2022, after they first met on a flight from Boston to Florida.

They were first pictured together in January 2023, before finally going public with their relationship in June 2024.

They have since been on a whirlwind and often controversial romance, which resulted in them living together between North Carolina, where Belichick is currently coaching the UNC football team, and Nantucket.

Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson secretly ended their age-gap relationship last year, per TMZ

The pair were spotted beaming on the sideline of a UNC game as recently as this month

Hudson has been an ever-present at Belichick's side despite reports of their romance ending

A source close to Hudson told TMZ that the pair quietly ended their relationship 'late last year,' though it is unclear who exactly pulled the plug.

It is also being reported that Hudson has been 'seeing other people' since her romance with Belichick, who is 49 years her senior, came to an end.

The Daily Mail has reached out to the pair for further comment.

It is extremely surprising that the news wasn't made public any earlier, especially given Hudson has been a constant presence on the sideline at UNC games this season – and as recently as last weekend against Syracuse in Chapel Hill.

A week earlier, she was alongside her now-ex-boyfriend for the road game against Duke, with the pair beaming as they left the field together.

It remains to be seen whether Hudson will resume her role on the sideline in the wake of their split becoming public knowledge, with UNC at home against No 1-ranked Miami in Chapel Hill on Saturday night.

Bizarrely, the pair were also seen holding hands during a public appearance at the Kentucky Derby in May, after which Hudson posted a photo with the caption: 'Not the first time we’ve trudged through the mud together,' with a love heart.

Hudson and Belichick are regularly at each other's sides despite reports of a secret split

While it is reported they split last year, the pair held hands at the Kentucky Derby in May

That trip came months after their reported split at the end of 2025.

During the course of their romance, Hudson amassed an impressive $9 million property portfolio, as first reported by the Daily Mail.

She has snapped up at least four properties, including one worth $3 million, which were all purchased after she met the former New England Patriots coach.

Even more impressively, she has also paid off the mortgages on each of the homes, with her primary residence listed as a two-bedroom cottage in Cape Cod.

Records also show that she has registered 18 companies – several with names that suggest she had, or has, some control over Belichick's affairs.

She had been operating as Belichick's de facto manager during their relationship, and it appears she is still involved with him from a business perspective if not a romantic one.

Her control of his affairs hit the headlines most notably during a CBS Sunday Morning interview back in April 2025.

Belichick celebrates with his UNC players after winning on the road against Duke on October 17

Hudson, sitting out of shot, muscled in on reporter Tony Dokoupil's line of questioning about how the pair met, shouting out: 'We're not talking about this.'

CBS broadcast the multiple interruptions made by Hudson throughout the interview, with TMZ later reporting that she 'walked out and delayed filming by 30 minutes' and at one point even corrected Belichick while he was discussing football.

More recently, Belichick was forced to deny that Jordon has been 'trying to control UNC's football program,' calling the claims 'ridiculous' in an interview with the Wall Street Journal in September.

To reports she is involved in virtually everything he does, Belichick responded that that is a 'flat-out lie.'

Prior to his relationship with Hudson, Belichick was married to his ex-wife Debby for 30 years, before they separated prior to the 2004 NFL season.

He was then in a long-term relationship with girlfriend Linda Holliday for approximately 16 years, from 2007 to 2022.

Sports.title: Fallon Sherrock BEATS Luke Littler to win £501k in Netflix challenge: 'Queen of the Palace' holds back tears after winning in front of her son - seven years on from fairytale World Championship run
Sports.content:
Fallon Sherrock BEATS Luke Littler to win £501k in Netflix challenge: 'Queen of the Palace' holds back tears after winning in front of her son - seven years on from fairytale World Championship run

Fallon Sherrock made more history on Friday night as she defeated Luke Littler to take home a life-changing £501,000 on Netflix's Beat Luke Littler.

It took Sherrock, who has won two matches at the World Championship previously – her first win seeing her become the first female player to win at the tournament – 14 darts to claim victory, and her son rushed onto the stage to embrace her and her new fortune.

'It's insane,' she said, fighting back the tears. 'I can't put into words how much this means. And having my son, the first time he's ever been to anything, and he saw me win.

'It was lovely. Sorry, I'm lost for words. It was a great moment and I'll remember it forever. Give me an opportunity and I'll take it every time. I'm really proud of myself right now.'

Littler said: 'That's what one person had to do. I wanted her to give me a chance, and she didn't.

'I've enjoyed every minute of it. It's been good.'

The moment Fallon Sherrock hit a 180 before going on to #BeatLukeLittler and win £501k! pic.twitter.com/jrpkPvWBFw — Netflix UK & Ireland (@NetflixUK) October 30, 2026

Luke Littler was defeated on Netflix on Friday night as Fallon Sherrock claimed £501,000

Sherrock needed just 14 darts to beat the two-time world champion and take home the prize

It was first assumed that the common man or woman would be taking on Littler for the chance at life-changing money. Netflix's  featured people lining up to audition that no one had ever seen before.

More than 3,000 people auditioned in London and Manchester to take on The Nuke. Hopefuls travelled from far and wide, queuing from the early hours of the morning.

And so fans were left puzzled when the line-up was announced. Among them were semi-pro stars, upcoming hotshots, and even players who have competed at the World Championship before.

Queen of the Palace Sherrock, six and soon to be seven-time Ally Pally participant, once reaching the last-32 in 2019; Wee Sox Mitchell Lawrie, the reigning World Darts Federation Youth champion and World No1; Fierce Pearse Mackle, who has played youth darts for Ireland; Young Gun Jayden Walker, 14, who has played Littler before - and he wasn't the only one. Others who have played at semi-pro level.

'I don't need the money,' Sherrock told Daily Mail Sport at the London auditions. 'But I have always said I would like more opportunities to promote the women's game, and this is the perfect opportunity to do it. Why wouldn't you?

'I do speak to Luke. I know him, I know his mum, his dad, Faith, and they are lovely, genuine people.'

Some felt short-changed. Some have indeed come from nowhere – a teacher, a Nando's restaurant manager and a business adviser were all featured – but the selection process hardly went down as Netflix would have hoped.

Littler 'put his reputation on the line', Gary Lineker told us as the show started.

Up to 20 hopefuls would be given the chance to face Littler, with Sherrock compeititor No 15

On the punditry team, alongside darts player and analyst Laura Turner was Richard Osman, Littler's friend Angry Ginge and comedian Lee Mack. We then saw Joe Marler and Josh Denzel. Darts.

Qualifiers were ranked and put into pots. Sixteen players were seeded, then others were wildcards who the public would vote for in a one-off contest.

Mack, frankly, had no idea. He asked if anyone had played at a high standard. What happened if Littler was beaten early. Said that more Professional Darts Corporation matches should bull up. They do.

Cheerleaders followed Littler to stage, which was where he stayed for the duration of the night. A hug for girlfriend Faith. Were the nerves starting to hit?

First up was 16-year-old Kasey Smith. Or 'Katie', according to Lineker. Smith was left stranded on 261, but did herself no shame. One down.

Tony Cole had never played against anyone before. He got closer, but not really close at all. Two down.

The major disadvantage that the challengers had was that Littler was regularly winning the bull, meaning he threw first in the leg. Playing against the darts is always a challenge – it's worse when facing the best in the world.

Zach the professional jockey – who entered with a horse – fell short despite putting up a solid competition. Olly Murs was then interviewed. Again, darts.

Sherrock's family celebrated in the crowd and would eventually join her on stage in Manchester

She was presented with a cheque - having previously told Daily Mail Sport she 'doesn't need the money'

Jayden Walker could have provided serious competition up next. He has broken some of Littler's youth records and got the better of Luke Humphries before. Here, he had no answer as Littler pinned his first 180 and checked out 158 to win.

The first wildcard selection felt awkward. Two hopefuls stood at the end of the walk-on – one, decided by a live viewer vote, walked forward. The other headed backstage. What a waste of time.

And 18-year-old bin man Taylon Forrester came close. The crowd began to boo Littler's throw. He came through his toughest challenge yet as his opponent got down to a finish.

The next, Mackle, had a dart at the bull. His life flashed before his eyes. Netflix were more interested in getting Olly Murs on screen than actually filming the dart, but he missed. Littler didn't. 'I'm happy enough with that,' Mackle said. The closest we'd come by far.

Fifty-seven-year-old Mark Pooke hit a 12-dart leg in the auditions. He won the bull, but then threw away the advantage and seemed to lose his bottle. Stone faced, but Littler prevailed against the No2 seed.

Littler's average at this point had dropped into the 80s. Though a second ton-plus out shot took him to ten wins.

'It's tough when it's constant,' Littler said. 'Anyone can cause me bother.'

Littler hit only two 180s. He wasn't good enough, or he didn't need to? Pick your narrative.

Sherrock won the bull as challenger number 15. The trebles started to come. She left 43. Littler a mile away.

The roof came off the place. Fallon Sherrock made history again. Her son rushed onto stage. She may not be the best player – or even the best female player – but she has a habit of making history.

And so Littler was beaten by Sherrock, who, for some reason Lineker said at the close 'arrived as a hairdresser from Milton Keynes'.

'Let's do it again next year,' The Nuke said. It's back to making the millions for him now.

Sports.title: Emiliano Martinez reveals his finger 'won't ever return' to normal after injury left him playing like  a 'zombie' during World Cup: 'I cried every day'
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez reveals his finger 'won't ever return' to normal after injury left him playing like a 'zombie' during World Cup: 'I cried every day'

Emiliano Martinez has revealed his finger will never return to normal after he played through injury to represent Argentina at the World Cup.

Martinez broke and dislocated a finger in the warm-up before playing for Aston Villa in their Europa League final triumph over Freiburg in May.

The 34-year-old told Argentine journalist Gaston Edul’s YouTube channel that he cried after seeing x-rays having feared he would be ruled out of Argentina's World Cup title defence.

After receiving support from Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni, Martinez explained a decision was taken to avoid undergoing surgery that would have ruled him out of the tournament.

Martinez was instead provided with a special glove from Adidas to protect the injured finger, which he admitted meant he could not grasp the ball properly.

'It will never go back to how it was,' Martinez said. 'I am still playing with pain.'

Emiliano Martinez has revealed his finger will never return to normal after he played through injury to represent Argentina at the World Cup. Source: YouTube/Gastón Edul

Martinez sustained a broken finger before playing for Aston Villa in the Europa League final

The shot stopper wore a special glove from Adidas to protect his injured finger to ensure he could play at the World Cup, but admits he will need surgery in the future

'The day before Algeria I was diving with one arm, diving like a zombie.

'If I put my hand down I was seeing stars. It was brutal. Every single night I was crying because my finger looked like a sausage.

'But these are the risks you take for the national team, I’d do it again.'

Martinez added that a summer transfer to Italy – with Juventus having targeted the star – ultimately collapsed as a direct result of the injury.

'I got an x-ray and it was broken again,' Martinez said. 'That is when a transfer to a club fell through because of the finger.

'They said it was possible for me to play like that, that I needed surgery, but Chelsea didn't, they didn't care. One day I will need surgery.'

Martinez, who joined Chelsea for £7.5million in the summer, is currently recovering from a broken jaw sustained in their victory over Everton earlier this month.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hits back at Gary Neville after his former Man United team-mate accused players of being unprofessional - and opens up on crunch meeting with struggling stars
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has rejected claims that his Manchester United stars have been unprofessional, and vowed to stand by them in the face of fierce criticism from pundits and fans. Carrick’s former teammate Gary Neville accused some players of not going to bed at the right time or keeping to a healthy diet, while Wayne Rooney said they need ‘a firework up their a**e’ for the performances that have left their head coach fighting to save his job. United fans turned on the team following Sunday’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford, applauding Carrick down the tunnel before immediately venting their anger at the players. Asked if he has encountered the unprofessional behaviour insinuated by Neville, Carrick said: ‘No, I haven’t. Gaz says a lot things!’ After United decided to give their head coach more time to turn the season around, he met with the players when they returned to Carrington on Tuesday and spoke about the backlash from fans. ‘Just to be clear, it was more for them to understand that I'm right in there with them. There's no way that I'm separated from that,’ said Carrick ahead of Saturday's crucial game at Chelsea. Gary Neville (left) said Man United players were 'unprofessional' but Michael Carrick (right) insists he is standing by them in the face of criticism

Your browser does not support iframes.

‘As much as I totally respect and appreciate the response from the supporters, I'm right there with them and we'll go through this together. ‘It was mixed feelings for me. To have the appreciation from the supporters and that connection and that respect is something I feel strongly about. ‘It wasn't a nice situation, but to feel that was important, of course. But it didn't make me feel better in the fact that I'm with the players 100 per cent. ‘We're all in it together and I've told the players that. I'm happy to say that. I didn't feel comfortable being separated from that in any way, shape or form. ‘That's my group, they're my players and this is my football club, so we have to all be in it together. ‘That includes the supporters. As hard as it is at the moment, I totally get that. I get their feelings. When we get through this, we'll be a lot stronger as a whole. ‘We need to play better and we need to show certain things better. But the connection with us is as strong as ever.’ The fans also targeted United’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as well as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. On his meeting with the players, Carrick added: ‘It's pretty clear. It's not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that's between me and the players, whether that's between me, Jason or Omar or the owners. It's the hard truth at times and it's what we need to move forward.’

Sports.title: Tyson Fury dealt major blow by Oleksandr Usyk's latest decision
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury dealt major blow by Oleksandr Usyk's latest decision

Usyk gave up his heavyweight world titles last year but was still expected to campaign in the division and had set his sights on Deontay Wilder

View Image Oleksandr Usyk has made a big decision (Image: PA)

Oleksandr Usyk will return to cruiserweight next year - ending Tyson Fury's hopes of a trilogy fight.

‌



‌



Usyk gave up his heavyweight world titles last year but was still expected to campaign in the division. He had set his sights on a final bout with Deontay Wilder next year but talks fell through. The Ukrainian also expressed a desire to face Fury for a third time despite beating the Brit twice in 2024.

‌



Fury has always insisted he should have won those fights and has demanded the chance to set the record straight. But while he faces Anthony Joshua in Cardiff in December, Usyk has decided to return to cruiserweight and target a second resign as the undisputed champion.

‌



Anthony Joshua told he won't last 10 minutes against Tyson Fury READ MORE :

"Oleksandr aims to return to cruiserweight in 2027 and become undisputed again," Usyk team director Sergey Lapin told Casinostugan. "First, we are looking at a fight for a vacant world title. Then, the goal is to face David Benavidez to unify all the belts and become undisputed cruiserweight champion.

"We see 2027 as the final chapter of his career. He wants to finish as undisputed champion in the division where he first won all the belts. If we’re going to do this, we need to take a comprehensive approach. The first fight for a world title, the second for the undisputed championship.

‌



"Usyk has never been a natural heavyweight. Cruiserweight is his home. He loves a challenge, so he moved up, cleaned out the heavyweight division, and now he is coming home to restore order."

Fury most recently called out Usyk while claiming Joshua would not go through with their £150million mega-fight. He said: “You got the decisions last time; fair play to you. Good luck to you; let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court... do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits? Let me know because I am now looking for a new opponent.”

Article continues below

Usyk was last in action in May when he scraped past kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven. Having struggled against the Dutchman, the fight was stopped in the 11th round to ensure Usyk remained unbeaten.

Sports.title: Should Michael Carrick recall Bruno Fernandes with his Man Utd job on the line?
Sports.content:
Should Michael Carrick recall Bruno Fernandes with his Man Utd job on the line?

HAVE YOUR SAY: Michael Carrick chose to drop Bruno Fernandes last weekend but, with it job on the line and private talks held, should the Manchester United boss bring his captain back into the starting picture

View Image Michael Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for last weekend's defeat (Image: Getty)

The image of Bruno Fernandes glued to the Manchester United bench last Sunday said a lot. It was undoubtedly a power play from Michael Carrick, who must've thought he'd led his former side for the last time.

‌



‌



In the six days since he's been backed by those above him, but with the caveat that things need to improve and fast if he is to remain long-term. Carrick and Fernandes have also held talks to clear the air.

‌



The Portugal star was scathing about Carrick in the aftermath of the loss at Como, and clearly the United boss felt he needed to make a statement, even if that meant leaving out his best player.

‌



And whilst Fernandes may be United's best player, he's hardly been playing at his optimum this season. Carrick will also know that, with his job on the line, he may need his players to dig deep and commit to him. It is also worth noting that Fernandes was, supposedly, dropped for football reasons. Have those reasons really changed in the space of a week?

Even after discussing any differences with Fernandes, questions have to be asked over whether the Portuguese playmaker will truly buy in for his manager, who needs a win more than ever.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua's coach responds to Tyson Fury's "traitor" accusation
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua's coach responds to Tyson Fury's "traitor" accusation

Anthony Joshua has reunited with Ben Davison for his mouthwatering all-British heavyweight showdown with Tyson Fury later this year

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua face off (Image: Getty Images)

Ben Davison has played down Tyson Fury's 'traitor' jibe after the boxing trainer teamed up with Anthony Joshua for a second time.

‌



‌



Davison famously corned Fury for five fights - including his historic draw with Deontay Wilder back in 2018. He also played a vital role in helping the former two-time heavyweight world champion out of his drink-and-drug fuelled depression and back to the ring.

‌



The pair split in December 2019 - just weeks before his rematch with Wilder. Nearly four years later, Davison joined forces with 'AJ' and helped him prepare for his win over Otto Wallin as well as his destructive knockout win over Francis Ngannou in March 2024.

‌



However, they parted ways after Joshua was knocked out by Daniel Dubois in front of over 90,000 fans at Wembley Stadium in September 2024. 'AJ' enlisted the help of Oleksandr Usyk's team for his two recent wins - back-to-back knockout victories over Jake Paul and Kristian Prenga.

But the 37-year-old will now work alongside Davison for his all-British mega-fight with Fury - which is scheduled to take place on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. And prior to their dust-up, Fury rather playfully labelled Davison a "traitor" for reuniting with Joshua.

James DeGale breaks down as he discusses retiring from boxing READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

‌



Reacting to the comments, Davison told Playbook Boxing, powered by Betway: "I think it's tongue-in-cheek. I'll be honest, I don't think he cares who works with AJ. But I think most importantly, I spent a lot of time with him and I think deep down he knows what type of person I am. I think he would say, "I know Ben's a good guy."

"He's smart enough to understand that boxing is a business and hopefully he feels the same way I do where it doesn't have an impact. Like I say, he could say whatever it is that he wanted to, call me this, call me that, whatever. It wouldn't change how things are because deep down I have the same, where I know he's a good guy.

‌

"I never fell out with any ex-fighters that I've worked with, and it's important to me that stays the same. But at the same time, I've got a fantastic relationship and a lot of love for AJ as well."

Article continues below

Despite his loyalties lying with Joshua currently, Davison admits he still won't give the British brawler any tips on how to beat Fury in their heavyweight showdown. "Not really. I think Tyson's developed as a fighter," he said. "There's nothing that I would know about him that you couldn't see by watching one of his fights - in terms of boxing.

"Outside of that, I think that's something that AJ respects. I never go to AJ and talk to him about Tyson. I think that's something that he can see. There's a level of integrity there."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Ronald Araujo transfer update issued as Jamie Carragher makes bold claim
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Ronald Araujo transfer update issued as Jamie Carragher makes bold claim

Liverpool are in the ascendancy after winning five matches on the bounce since their 3-0 defeat to Manchester City earlier this month

View 3 Images A Ronald Araujo transfer update has been issued (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Things are going well for Liverpool at the moment. The Reds have won five games on the trot - albeit one via a penalty shootout - and now have their eyes set on a Premier League title challenge.

‌



‌



Andoni Iraola's tenure began with a bit of a whimper and things looked bleak when they were beaten 3-0 by Manchester City earlier this month. But the response to that setback has been impressive.

‌



In the weeks since, Liverpool have sealed victories over LASK, Brentford, Villarreal, Brighton and Chelsea, scoring 15 goals to boot. Their latest triumph - beating Chelsea on penalties on Wednesday - booked the club's place in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals.

‌



Now though, attention turns back to the Premier League, with a blockbuster clash with champions Arsenal to come on Sunday. With that in mind, here are the latest Liverpool-related headlines.

5 Brazilian wonderkids Liverpool's new transfer chief may attempt to sign READ MORE :

Liverpool open talks over January transfer as clear leader in Alex Scott race emerges READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Carragher makes bold claim

Jamie Carragher has reversed his initial stance on Liverpool's Premier League title chances.

‌



Earlier this season, the legendary Reds defender said it would take time for Iraola to turn his former team back into title contenders after a disappointing 2025/26 campaign under Arne Slot. But now, Carragher thinks Liverpool will be Arsenal's closest challengers.

"I count myself as one of those on a journey with Iraola from initial scepticism following his appointment towards cautious optimism having seen his vision starting to take shape," he wrote in his column for The Telegraph. "My fear at the start of the season was that Liverpool employed a manager who had never won a trophy, nor managed in European competition.

‌



View 3 Images Jamie Carragher has changed his mind about Liverpool's title credentials (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

"These did not strike me as solid credentials for a job of such stature. It felt like a gamble to opt for someone who would have to learn how to manage a big club rather than arrive ready-made."

‌



However, as the campaign has unfolded, Carragher has changed his position. "There are several reasons why there are those who believe Iraola's side might push Arsenal closer than anticipated," he explained. "First and foremost, the guilty verdict in the Manchester City case has altered the complexion of the season, and emboldened those who want to seize the initiative.

"Now we expect City to be punished soon. Given the nature and severity of their misdemeanours it is inconceivable they will be a title contender if that happens. The door is open for those in the chasing pack with the capacity and will to walk through it."

‌



Araujo transfer update

Ronald Araujo's agent says it's "too early" to talk about the Uruguayan's future beyond this season but insists his client is happy at Anfield.

Araujo joined Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona in August and has impressed fans with his performances. Many are now urging the club to sign the 27-year-old permanently but Araujo's agent, Edoardo Crnjar, has played down talk of a permanent transfer, at least for now.

‌



View 3 Images Ronald Araujo has been impressing at Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

"Ronald is performing well. We're very pleased with what he's bringing to the team, but it's still too early to talk about his future," he said.

‌



"He's feeling great. He's happy to be playing for Liverpool and to be helping the club and his team-mates, just as he's said before."

Araujo has made over 200 appearances for Barcelona, but has never been a guaranteed starter at the Camp Nou. Since joining Liverpool, he has featured in all 13 of the club's opening matches, starting 11 of them.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Gunners target 'extraordinary' £58m talent as Mikel Arteta urged to 'move on'
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Gunners target 'extraordinary' £58m talent as Mikel Arteta urged to 'move on'

Arsenal are looking to get back on track with a tough away trip to Liverpool on Sunday afternoon

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta will be hoping to put Arsenal's Carabao Cup exit behind him this weekend (Image: Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images)

Arsenal will have to do without Max Dowman against Liverpool on Sunday afternoon after his red card appeal was rejected. The Gunners winger was sent off for retaliation against Harrison Neal of Fleetwood Town during the side's shock Carabao Cup defeat on Wednesday.

‌



‌



Dowman was forced to watch from the changing rooms as his team were dumped out at the fourth-round stage on penalties, with the League Two outfit recording a famous win over the reigning Premier League champions. Mikel Arteta was left incensed by the teenager's actions, making his thoughts perfectly clear post-game.

‌



He said: "When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate. It was very clear."

‌



During his pre-Liverpool press conference, the Spaniard reflected on his reaction to Dowman, where he seemed to shout his frustration at the teen. He said: "My reaction [during the match against Fleetwood] was in the heat [of the moment] and of frustration as I know the consequences for that and especially for Max.

Mikel Arteta doubles down on Max Dowman anger and reveals new disappointment READ MORE :

"It's something we discussed just before we went out because it's not the first time it's happened as it happened earlier this month with England. It will continue to happen with the way he plays and the way he attracts opponents. We have to be protective of him as he is 16 but also very straight with him about what to expect from him towards the team and the club."

Here, Mirror Football has the latest news coming out of the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Gunners target 'extraordinary' £58m talent

Reports in Italy claim that Arsenal are showing a 'serious interest' in RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa. The winger, who is valued at £58million, has been touted with a move to north London as Tutto Mercato reports that the Gunners are confident they could land his services.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is reportedly keen on Antonio Nusa (Image: Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Roma are also reportedly interested in the 21-year-old, who already has 10 goal contributions in 12 appearances so far this season. Rival striker Erling Haaland has previously sung Nusa's praises, calling him "something extraordinary."

‌



Following a 4-1 win over Slovenia in 2024, in which Nusa scored a brace and Haaland also found the net, the Norway international and Manchester City star said: "He's something extraordinary. He's delivering at a high level, he's a great talent and he simply has to keep going."

Mikel Arteta urged to 'move on'

Micah Richards has urged Arteta to "move on" from Viktor Gyokeres and search for a replacement in January. The Swede has scored just once in 11 appearances this season and looks to be cutting a frustrated figure in front of goal.

‌



Speaking on The Rest Is Football podcast, Richards believes the 28-year-old should leave Arsenal to allow "top cover" to arrive in the next transfer window. He said: "I think one of the major talking points as well is Gyokeres. When he first arrived at Arsenal, I was saying to the Arsenal fans, ‘Don’t expect him to be scoring 25 and 30 goals.'

View 3 Images Arsenal have been urged to move on from Viktor Gyokeres (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



"What I really liked about him, he was good at running in behind, but he stopped doing the things that he’s really good at. He sort of looks like he has no confidence. I don’t know if the reports in the summer that they tried to get rid of him [were true] or not, but essentially he’s had enough game time to show what he can do now at Arsenal and it’s just not happening for him.

"I think in January, because of the injuries, I definitely think they should go back into the market, and find top cover around."

‌



Richards continued: "Because the way Arsenal play, and everyone talks about they need this player, they need that player, but the reason why they’re so good is what the front players do off the ball… so, Saka and Madueke work hard in a system that works for Arsenal.

"Obviously, losing Trossard was a big miss for them in terms of what he does off the ball and how clinical he was with the opportunities given to him. But I think if they want to compete and then, say, dominate, then 100 per cent, I think they need more firepower in that forward area, for sure.

‌



"There are so many times where Gyokeres gets in really good positions, and I don’t know if he doesn’t back himself, I don’t know if it’s confidence, I don’t know if the team doesn’t back him to score, but he just, he doesn’t put the ball away. So, then it becomes a problem. And I just feel like he needs one of those opportunities where he plays 90 minutes, he scores, he builds confidence, and it goes from there. Otherwise, you know, they’re going to have to look to move him on."

Sports.title: Aston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher after 'unacceptable insults'
Sports.content:
Aston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher after 'unacceptable insults'

Jamie Carragher took aim at Aston Villa fans this week after facing backlash for suggesting Unai Emery could head to Manchester United - with the club now hitting back

View 2 Images Aston Villa's chairman has responded to comments made by Jamie Carragher

Aston Villa have confirmed that they will take legal action against Jamie Carragher "for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans".

‌



‌



The Premier League club made the statement on their social media on Friday night, which was signed off by their chairman, Nassef Sawiris.

‌



Villa don't make specific reference to particular comments made by Carragher, but the Sky Sports pundit did make headlines this week when he took on Villa fans who had taken issue with him hinting that Unai Emery could be the man to take over at Manchester United if they made a managerial change.

‌



He explained his reasons on Stick to Football and finished by saying: "So shut the f*** up Villa fans."

The club, without making clear what insults, said in a statement: "Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans. Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football."

Emery has been at Villa Park since 2022 and has overseen their rise from a side who were in the bottom half to one that have played in the Champions League in two of the past three seasons and also won the Europa League.

‌



The Spanish boss has done so whilst constantly having to rejig his squad with the club sanctioning the British record sale of Morgan Rogers to Chelsea this summer. In the same window they also saw Emi Martinez head to the Blues whilst Ezri Konsa headed to Arsenal.

Carragher, during his address earlier this week, commented: "I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year. That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year.

‌



View 2 Images Jamie Carragher's comments this week could be the subject of legal action (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

"But the reason I'm going to go back at Villa fans is I can't believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you'd won the Europa League three of four times surely you'll then want to go for the Champions League.

Article continues below

"Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn't do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that's because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing. But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not."

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or scores published as Harry Kane's slender winning margin revealed
Sports.content:
Ballon d'Or scores published as Harry Kane's slender winning margin revealed

Harry Kane claimed the Ballon d'Or on Monday night but the Bayern Munich star's margin of victory was a minor one as he edged out Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe

View 2 Images Harry Kane won his Ballon d'Or by just 28 points (Image: Jeff Spicer - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by just 28 points with his narrow margin of victory over Kylian Mbappe being published.

‌



The Bayern Munich ace won the individual accolade for the first time in his career on Monday and also ended a 25-year wait for a English winner as he scooped the gong in his hometown, London.

Heading into the ceremony there was talk of a unique three-way battle for the award as Kane, Mbappe and Lamine Yamal all had genuine cases to claim the Ballon d'Or. Kane would win ahead of the Frenchman, but the contest was particularly close. Kane amassed 1,055 points with Mbappe just behind on 1,027.

For all the talk of a three-way battle, Yamal was a distant third with 881 points. The World Cup winner's exploits were not enough to see him claim the award.

It is worth noting that the journalists who represented Spain and Germany both handed their vote to Mbappe - not the players who play in their domestic league.

For Mbappe it was the best showing of his career to date. He'd previously finished third in 2018 following his World Cup victory with France, but topped that after delivering the best goalscoring season of his career - leading charts in La Liga, the Champions League and at the World Cup.

His trophyless season may well have counted against him with Kane helping Bayern continue their German dominance - winning the league and cup double. He also got the better of Mbappe when England beat France to third at the World Cup.

From third to tenth the margins were relatively comfortable with few players close to going up or down the rankings. Rodri in fourth, Lionel Messi in fifth and seventh-placed Ousmane Dembele are the last three winners of the Ballon d'Or.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe narrowly missed out on the Golden Ball

Kane said after his victory: “Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year. Some of the incredible players I was up against, some of my team-mates and world-class players in the room tonight, so thank you to everyone who voted for me.

"Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees tonight - an impressive showing of what determination and hard work can really achieve, so well done."

Ballon d'Or top 10

1. Harry Kane, 1,055 points

2. Kylian Mbappé, 1,027 points

3. Lamine Yamal, 881 points

4. Rodri, 726 points

5. Lionel Messi, 612 points

6. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, 541 points

7. Ousmane Dembélé, 418 points

8. Erling Haaland, 378 points

9. Michael Olise, 296 points

10. Fabian Ruiz, 201 points
