Sports.title: Bottas ‘needs to do’ more weekends like Austin to keep Cadillac seat – Budkowski | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac team principal Marcin Budkowski explained what Valtteri Bottas needs to do to keep his seat at the team as test driver Colton Herta becomes eligible for a superlicence.

The team confirmed Sergio Perez will continue as one of its drivers next year. It is yet to confirm whether Valtteri Bottas will also get a second season.

Budkowski said the team extended Perez’s contract because he’s “been overall the quicker and the better driver this year.” He said Bottas needs to consistently perform at the level he demonstrated in Austin last weekend.

“He’s done a really good race in Austin,” Budkowski told Sky. “He was strong in qualifying, he was strong at the race. That’s what he needs to do, race in, race out.”

Bottas has been puzzled by his inability to match Perez’s pace in some races, says Budkowski, who admitted the difference could be down to the preparation of their two cars.

“It’s actually the question we’re asking ourselves collectively with Valtteri and with the engineering team, because some races we don’t actually see a reason for it in the data,” he said. “Valtteri doesn’t see a reason either in terms of the fact there’s no big issue in the car.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“He’s an experienced race driver, he knows what he can extract from a race car and what he can’t, and he just says ‘I can’t extract more pace from this car’.

“But let’s face it, we’re a new team, this car is not a perfect car. The car has been put together in a very short period of time by a team of people who have never worked together before and from a white sheet of paper.

“We have to accept that we’re not giving these guys the best possible equipment and we don’t have as a team enough strength and depth to have full certainty that the equipment we have is perfect. So we’re looking at it together, from the team’s side and from the driver’s side and that’s also why we’re taking the time to try to understand exactly what’s going on.”

2026 Mexican Grand Prix

Sports.title: Leclerc puts Ferrari on top in practice again in Mexico | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc started the Mexican Grand Prix on top by setting the fastest time in the opening practice session.

It was the fourth consecutive practice session headed by a Ferrari, after the team led all three sessions in Austin a week ago.

The two Mercedes drivers came next, Andrea Kimi Antonelli leading Frederik Vesti, who took over from George Russell. Vesti lapped within a tenth of a second of the driver who can clinch the world championship on Sunday.

The majority of teams ran junior drivers in the opening practice session. Behind Lewis Hamilton, Ayumu Iwasa set the quickest time by any driver who did not use the soft tyres. Isack Hadjar in the other Red Bull ended the session outside the top 10 after being delayed by a power unit problem.

Pierre Gasly took sixth while Fernando Alonso put his Aston Martin much further up the times sheets than usual with the seventh-fastest time.

Oscar Piastri, the quickest McLaren driver, was only eighth. Leonardo Fornaroli, replacing Lando Norris for this session, struggled to brake as aggressively as he needed to at turn one, running wide during his soft tyre run.

Oliver Bearman and Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10. Formula 2 driver Nikola Tsolov became the first Bulgarian driver to participate in an official practice session and impressed by lapping a tenth of a second slower than the team’s regular driver.

Other newcomers had less smooth sessions. Audi sent Freddie Slater out of the garage with a fan assembly in his right-hand sidepod. He had to pit to have it removed, then return to the garage for a longer stay due to overheating. The stewards are investigating the team’s unsafe release of the car.

Jak Crawford, driving Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin, parked up with a technical problem after leaving the track at turn one.

Colton Herta ended the session at the bottom of the times but passed an important milestone. Completing 30 laps ensured he will reach the 40 superlicence points he needs in order to be allowed to race in Formula 1.

Sports.title: ‘There’s no pay drivers now’: Alonso’s rivals reject his criticism of ‘one-third’ of the grid | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso’s rivals do not share his view that one-third of the Formula 1 grid has “very low” driving standards.

The Aston Martin driver’s comments were prompted by his first-lap tangle with Alexander Albon in the United States Grand Prix last week. “I think the bottom third of the grid, the quality of the drivers is very low at the moment,” the two-times world champion remarked.

Albon initially tried to downplay his rival’s comments as being made “in the heat of the moment” after the race. But Alonso stood by his criticism of the Williams driver’s first-lap lunge, saying he didn’t understand why Albon thought his attempt to pass on the inside of turn 11 would work.

However Albon maintained he disagreed with Alonso and defended the standard of driving in F1, claiming it is higher now than in past seasons when more drivers bought their way onto the grid.

“I have huge respect for Fernando,” said Albon. “I looked up to him a lot growing up as a kid.

“Obviously, it’s not nice to hear those comments in many ways. You’re racing someone that you looked up to, but at the same time, I don’t agree. It’s as simple as that.

“I think the level is strong up and down the grid. Ten or fifteen years ago, the back half of the grid wasn’t the way it is now. You don’t have pay drivers anymore. It is what it is, hopefully we don’t cross paths in the race this weekend.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Pierre Gasly, who is in his tenth season in F1, agreed the standard of driving has improved.

“You have to love Fernando for the statements he makes out there,” said the Alpine driver. “I have so much respect for the driver he is, and at the same time, he’s very vocal.

“I’m not too sure – I haven’t seen his race, I’m not too sure what he referred to – but I think I would agree. I will say that the level on the grid is probably one of the highest, considering all the drivers we have now, from what I’ve seen over maybe nine years. I’ve seen some wild driving approaches when I joined compared to what I see now.”

Oliver Bearman, who is 13th in the championship, said those in the bottom half of the field need to take more risks to stand a chance of scoring points.

“Luckily, I’m just about in the middle third, not the bottom one, so I get away with it,” he said. “But no, I think that’s a slightly harsh conclusion.

“I agree with Pierre that the level is very high on this current grid. With the gaps that we face this year, you have to be very opportunistic at times, and that can end in disaster, like it did for me last week with myself and Pierre.

“So I wouldn’t say it’s a question of quality. It’s a question of trying your very best and trying to make something happen, which is very challenging when the top eight positions are pretty much all filled by the top four teams.”

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder And Jai Opetaia Agree To Fight
Sports.content:
Jai Opetaia is taking a dangerous route toward a potential David Benavidez fight, with a deal reportedly agreed for him to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard. Wilder offers the Australian a recognizable name and access to Netflix’s audience, but his right hand could wreck those plans.

The heavyweight bout is not signed, according to Dan Rafael, who reported that the sides have reached an agreement. Fury and Joshua headline December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, giving Opetaia an opportunity to introduce himself to viewers who have never followed his cruiserweight career.

“Per source, while it’s not signed yet, deal is agreed to for Wilder-Opetaia to be on the #FuryJoshua card,” Rafael wrote on X.

That represents progress from the earlier discussions. Dana White had previously confirmed that Wilder was among the opponents being considered for Opetaia, while identifying Benavidez as the fight his cruiserweight star wants.

There is an obvious commercial reason to take this detour. Another cruiserweight victory might strengthen Opetaia’s standing among dedicated boxing followers without doing much to expand his audience. Wilder’s name could help him reach casual viewers, particularly on a card built around two of Britain’s most recognizable fighters.

The sporting reward is less clear. Wilder has won his last two fights, but his latest victory was a narrow split decision over Derek Chisora in April. Before those wins, he lost four of five bouts, including three defeats by stoppage. Opetaia would be facing a former champion whose recent results have diminished the value of beating him.

That leaves Opetaia in a tough position. Outboxing Wilder would invite the response that the American was already well past his best. Getting caught by him could cost Opetaia far more than a defeat at cruiserweight, because it would damage the unbeaten record helping sell a Benavidez fight.

Wilder does not need to rediscover everything he once had to make this dangerous. Opetaia still has to close the distance, land his combinations, and get out without leaving an opening for the right hand. Moving up in weight gives him less room for a mistake against a puncher of Wilder’s reputation.

There is also a difference between keeping active and taking a heavyweight fight before returning to cruiserweight. Even a victory could come with an injury or a hard enough night to complicate the timing of his next bout. Until Wilder is beaten and Opetaia comes through healthy, the Benavidez fight carries an extra obstacle.

For Wilder, the attraction is clear: beating an unbeaten cruiserweight star would give his career a substantial lift. For Opetaia, the calculation is tougher. He needs Wilder’s recognition, but he also needs enough of a performance to make viewers remember the winner rather than dismiss the opponent.

Netflix could give Opetaia the audience he has been missing. Whether that exposure is worth putting a potential Benavidez fight at risk is what makes this more than a routine undercard addition.

Sports.title: Keyshawn Davis Leaves Top Rank, But Will Zuffa Pay?
Sports.content:
Keyshawn Davis is officially free from Top Rank, paving the way for Zuffa to sign him and jump-start talks for a clash with Richardson Hitchins. Still, switching promoters will not automatically fix the persistent hurdle stalling Davis through his recent negotiations: agreeing on purse money.

Tim Bradley addressed the split once Bob Arum confirmed Davis received an early release. Hitchins, who already signed with Zuffa, claimed Davis priced himself out of their bout by demanding $6 million. While that number is strictly Hitchins’ version of events, Davis previously turned down the financial package to challenge Devin Haney, proving money remains the sticking point.

Having both men under the Zuffa umbrella clears a major promotional hurdle, yet it guarantees nothing. Shakur Stevenson’s inability to finalize an in-house bout with Rayo Valenzuela serves as a clear warning that shared promotional backing cannot force fighters to sign off on numbers they dislike.

Bradley pushed that point on his YouTube channel, questioning Davis’ market value.

“Keyshawn ain’t worth no $6 million. Sorry, he not,” Bradley said on his channel. “The last time you fought at home, you didn’t even sell out the arena.”

That critique highlights Davis’ real test. Ring talent alone does not guarantee pay-per-view buys or live gates. Unless a promoter is willing to absorb a financial loss, Davis must align his demands with what the event actually earns.

Bradley made clear he views this purely as business rather than intimidation.

“I don’t think Keyshawn is scared of Hitchins,” Bradley said. “He wants what was promised to him. That’s it.”

Bradley did not cite evidence of an explicit promise, and he openly noted that his speculation about Davis possibly paying a buyout fee was just personal opinion.

Keyshawn now controls his promotional future. Going to Zuffa might make a Hitchins bout simpler to stage, but if his payout demands do not budge, his new team will run into the exact same dead end that Top Rank just walked away from.

The chances of Zuffa signing Davis are real simply because Dana White wants elite, recognized talent to build the promotion’s roster alongside guys like Shakur Stevenson and Richardson Hitchins. But signing him and actually getting him into a ring without losing their shirts are two completely different problems.

Keyshawn’s self-valuation has completely detached from his real-world box office metrics. Turning down a mandatory shot at Devin Haney for the WBO welterweight belt because a $2.14 million purse bid split felt “embarrassingly low” was telling enough.

Demanding $6 million to fight Hitchins, when Keyshawn’s career-high payday sits around $1 million, and he struggled to pack his hometown arena in Norfolk, shows he’s not in tune with his worth.

Zuffa has deep pockets, but Dana White did not build an empire by letting unproven ticket sellers dictate vanity purses. The entire UFC/Zuffa operational model relies on cost control, leverage, and making matches on company terms.

If Bob Arum and Top Rank, who developed Keyshawn from day one, decided letting him walk out of his contract early was better than dealing with his price tags, Zuffa is stepping right into that same situation.

If Zuffa signs him, it only works under two scenarios: Zuffa pays him a flat, inflated signing guarantee up front to lock him down, only to watch negotiations stall when they try to schedule Hitchins or Haney and realize Keyshawn refuses to budge on bout fees. Shakur Stevenson’s standoff over Rayo Valenzuela already showed that bringing guys into the same stable does not magically make contracts get signed.

Or Zuffa gives him a dose of reality. If Dana and company offer him standard market numbers tied strictly to live-gate revenue and pay-per-view incentives, Keyshawn might quickly discover that free agency does not mean a blank check.

Unless Zuffa is willing to burn millions just to stage Hitchins vs. Davis, Davis will either have to adjust his expectations or sit on the shelf.

Sports.title: Ducking Yoenli Hernandez Was Bentley’s Smartest Business Decision
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley no longer owns the WBO middleweight belt, but picking Shane Mosley Jr. over Yoenli Hernandez makes total sense for his career. Getting stripped of a world title is never an ideal situation.

Still, surrendering the hardware outside the ring sure beats taking a beating inside it against Hernandez. Bentley was simply not going to beat that guy.

By ducking Hernandez and sacrificing the WBO title, Bentley walks into an immediately winnable booking against Mosley Jr. instead. Dan Rafael reported that the WBO Grievance Committee officially dismissed Bentley’s appeal on Friday in a massive twenty-eight-page resolution. His November 7 bout can still proceed, yet he will enter the arena without his championship.

Dropping the belt hurts his prestige, but sharing twelve rounds with Hernandez would have extracted a much steeper toll. The Cuban amateur star operates as the real power at 160 pounds right now. Stepping into that mandatory test right as his promotional tenure began would have been sheer recklessness, especially with Hernandez likely stopping him early.

Mosley Jr. gives Bentley the perfect opening platform to look good under his new banner. Nobody should treat Mosley as a complete walkover, but that pairing remains manageable compared to facing the most lethal threat in the entire division.

The real prize sits just over the horizon. Should Bentley take care of business against Mosley, he immediately positions himself for massive in-house unification opportunities. Zuffa Boxing controls both IBF champion Aaron McKenna and WBC titlist Carlos Adames. A single victory over Mosley puts Bentley in prime position to challenge McKenna or Adames for their titles, completely bypassing the Cuban buzzsaw while fighting for even bigger gold.

Hernandez gets what he deserved anyway with an unblocked route to the vacant WBO strap. For Bentley, giving up the belt preserves his market value, protects his health, and sets up a direct line to brand-new world titles down the road.

Sports.title: Will Christian Mbilli Send Canelo Into Retirement?
Sports.content:
The former two-time undisputed super-middleweight world champion Saul “Canelo” Alvarez (63-3-2, 39 KOs) is a legend and a future Hall of Famer, but on Saturday night, October 31st, will the WBC champion Christian Mbilli send Canelo into retirement?

This world title bout is an intriguing matchup because it features Canelo’s skill set versus Mbilli’s work rate. The action is set to take place at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, airing live on DAZN PPV.

Back in June 2025, Christian Mbilli stopped Maciej Sulecki in the first round and won the WBC title. Three months later, Mbilli was involved in a hard-fought battle as his bout against Lester Martinez resulted in a split draw.

Going into this fight, the defending champion Christian Mbilli is the underdog. Despite the odds being against him, Mbilli has the opportunity to defeat the great Canelo Alvarez and send him into retirement.

Losing a fight is rare, but it’s not new to Canelo. What would be new is for him to lose this upcoming bout because it will mark the first time Canelo ever suffered back-to-back losses.

Suffering consecutive defeats could push Alvarez towards retirement. It’s a bold statement, and due to the statement, one would ask: what is Christian Mbilli’s path to victory?

Christian Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KOs) is a determined, physical, and hungry world champion. He’s facing a tall task, but his path to victory is his aggression and his punch volume.

The 31-year-old Mbilli has incredible endurance, which allows him to constantly press forward and attack the body and head of his opponent. Alvarez has experienced stamina issues in the past, so outworking and outlasting Alvarez is Mbilli’s clear path to victory.

On the flip side, if the 36-year-old Canelo Alvarez has anything left in the tank, then this bout could be tailor-made for him due to the fact that Mbilli will be standing right in front of him.

In the past, Alvarez has done really well against opponents who lack movement and footwork. With Mbilli posting up in a neutral position and constantly in attack mode, Canelo will have many counterpunching opportunities.

Canelo will have his chances in regards to landing the left hook, the uppercut, and shots to the body. Speaking of body punches, those types of shots are a big part of Mbilli’s arsenal, and it will be interesting to see if he can consistently land shots to Canelo’s body.

Styles make fights, and that’s why the Canelo vs Mbilli fight will be an action-packed event. However, the question is, on Halloween night, will Canelo be sent into retirement, or will he take a step towards one last run at becoming undisputed once again?

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Must Demolish Inexperienced Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia cannot just settle for a win on Saturday; he needs to dominate. His opponent, Nikita Zon, has never boxed past eight rounds, yet finds himself stepping into a full twelve-round battle for the WBA super middleweight title in Riyadh.

On the scales, they matched up evenly, with Munguia clocking in at 167.4 pounds to Zon’s 167.5, but championship pedigree sets them worlds apart.

Zon brings an undefeated record, yet staying unblemished against modest competition is completely different from surviving world-class firepower. He stepped onto the stage looking like a man who knows exactly what he signed up for and wishes he hadn’t. That dead-eyed, heavy-footed demeanor on the scales says everything about where his head is at.

“This is his first scheduled twelve-round fight. Only fought three scheduled ten-round fights. Never fought longer than eight rounds,” Chris Mannix said on DAZN’s weigh-in broadcast. “Looks the part. Big, tall guy at 168 pounds. But this is a big, big challenge for Zon against Munguia.”

Those missing rounds matter when the fight goes deep. Zon will have to find out how his stamina holds up while taking heavy punishment from someone who practically lives in championship rounds. Looking cut on the scale does nothing to prove you can survive that furnace.

That puts the pressure squarely on Munguia to deliver a statement. He owns every edge needed to punish Zon to the body, test his gas tank early, and drag him into uncharted waters. Giving the challenger room to breathe would simply waste the advantages built up over years at the elite level.

There was plenty of talk about Munguia using extra footwork in his last outing, but staying on his toes against an overmatched opponent is not what fans want to see. Zon could theoretically shock everyone if he raises his game under pressure, since unbeaten fighters sometimes tap into another gear when everything is on the line. Still, a clean record cannot replace the stamina built from real championship rounds.

Munguia owns the title, the resume, and the edge. Now he just has to go out there and prove it. If he is serious about staying relevant at the absolute top of 168 pounds, he cannot mess around and box cute. He needs to walk Zon down and get him out of there fast.

With Munguia, there’s no such thing as a sure-thing win. We saw that in 2024 when he was knocked out by unknown Bruno Surace. That Surace disaster exposed the fatal flaw in treating any world-level booking as an easy night. Munguia walked into that ring looking right past an unheralded opponent, forgot his defense entirely, and paid for it by getting stretched out cold.

When a frontrunner fights down to the level of his competition or assumes a showcase win is guaranteed, disaster is always waiting. Zon is practically built in the exact same mold: obscure, fighting outside his home turf, possessing zero marquee names on his record, but completely free from the weight of expectations. All the pressure sits squarely on Munguia.

If he fights lazy, gets reckless, or leaves his chin hanging out like he did against Surace, even an inexperienced challenger can land the one punch that completely derails his career.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Gives Floyd Mayweather February 6 Ultimatum
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia wants Floyd Mayweather to stop talking and commit to February 6, but the bigger sales job is convincing fans that beating the retired star would carry championship value. Mayweather’s name can sell the event. His unbeaten record gives Garcia something even easier to advertise.

Garcia says Mayweather called him about the fight, and he is now demanding action. His latest post presents February 6 as a date he intends to keep, whether Floyd takes the offer or another opponent gets it.

“You called me and wanted this fight and I agree this is a big fight. But I am fighting FEB6th regardless so unless you actually make this happen then this fight is gone,” Garcia said on X. “You can go fight whoever but this is for a championship. I will TAKE you 0 with pleasure. Final warning no more games let’s make it happen.”

That unbeaten record is the prize Garcia keeps pointing toward. Taking Mayweather’s first professional defeat would generate enormous attention, but it would not mean Garcia had beaten the fighter who once ruled the sport. Floyd would enter February 6 at 49, approaching his 50th birthday.

Garcia is entitled to chase the biggest commercial fight available. Fans are equally entitled to distinguish between beating a famous former champion and beating an elite opponent in his prime. Putting a championship belt into the promotion does not erase that distinction.

Teofimo Lopez has also been mentioned for Garcia’s February return, giving this public ultimatum another purpose: pressure on Mayweather to commit while Garcia advertises that he has alternatives. February 6, 2027, was already being discussed before this latest post.

Ryan’s message establishes what he wants, rather than what both sides have signed. There is no completed agreement announced in the post, and his account of Mayweather’s call remains his account.

The demand is clear enough. Garcia wants Floyd’s name and unbeaten record on the contract. Until that happens, threatening to take the zero is promotion for a fight still waiting to become real.

It looks bad no matter how you view it. A prime fighter holding a major belt trying to strong-arm a fifty-year-old pensioner with a fake deadline is embarrassing theater. Giving Mayweather an ultimatum, as if Ryan is the A-side dictating terms to an icon old enough to be his father, makes Garcia look ridiculous rather than intimidating.

The optics are awful on every level. Floyd has not taken a genuine professional punch since Barack Obama was in the White House. His last legitimate pro test was an already-diminished Pacquiao over a decade ago, and his official retirement bout was a glorified sparring session against a debuting MMA fighter. Everything since has been low-effort exhibitions against kickboxers, reality stars, and YouTubers where nobody gets hurt.

Now you have Ryan, sitting in his physical prime, strutting around like he is doing the boxing world a favor by offering to beat up an inactive senior citizen. Demanding that Floyd hurry up and sign before February 6 only proves Ryan is desperate for the biggest possible check with the lowest possible threat level.

If Ryan really wanted to act like a world champion, he would be issuing ultimatums to Teofimo Lopez, Jaron Ennis, or the killer sharks at 140 and 147. Instead, he is publicly hounding a retired hall of famer to step into the ring so he can cosplay as the guy who conquered Mayweather’s record. Fans see right through it, and issuing a countdown clock to a grandfather only underlines how paper-thin the bravado is.

Sports.title: Oleksander Usyk Weight Cut Excuse Ready For Benavidez Bout
Sports.content:
David Benavidez spent years chasing Canelo Alvarez without ever landing the opportunity. Oleksandr Usyk could hand him the defining blockbuster that eluded him. Usyk takes on the physical risk, stepping down to 200 pounds after a long reign at heavyweight to face a younger, relentless pressure fighter built to break down tired opponents.

Usyk wants a return to cruiserweight for his next outing to target Benavidez, according to advisor Serhii Lapin speaking to Mike Coppinger of The Ring. Benavidez must handle business first against Michal Cieslak on December 5 in Glendale, Arizona, with three cruiserweight belts on the line. The potential clash with Usyk remains an ambitious goal instead of a signed deal.

The appeal for Benavidez stretches far past picking up more hardware. Taking down Usyk offers massive historical prestige, plus the distinct advantage of meeting him at cruiserweight instead of stepping up into heavyweight territory.

Usyk deserves credit for entertaining the idea. Past brilliance at 200 pounds offers no guarantee that his body responds well to another cut. He sits at 39 and turns 40 in January. Dropping weight after so long at heavyweight brings real volatility that glossy promotional hype easily ignores.

In top condition, Usyk possesses the foot speed and angles to keep Benavidez resetting, off balance, unable to plant his feet for heavy combinations. A sharp Usyk can disrupt incoming fire, spin his man, reset the pocket.

Trouble starts if cutting weight robs Usyk of his legs or tank. Benavidez thrives on grinding opponents down, making every exchange costly with dedicated work to the body through the championship rounds. Nobody can call Usyk depleted right now, but assuming the cut goes smoothly is just as reckless.

The built-in weight excuse angle is hard to ignore for Usyk, especially in modern boxing where fighters guard their reputations with an iron fist.

If Usyk drags Benavidez up to heavyweight and gets caught, battered, or outworked by a younger man, there is no safety net. He would lose as a heavyweight champion in his own division, full stop. By dropping to cruiserweight, his camp instantly constructs a built-in narrative cushion: he is almost 40 years old, he gave up size, he sacrificed his body to squeeze back down to 200 pounds for the fans, and he was depleted.

If he wins, he looks like an immortal wizard who conquered two divisions back and forth. If he loses, the media immediately frames it around the brutal weight cut rather than Benavidez simply beating him.

The physical reality makes the cruiserweight decision even more absurd. Benavidez has spent his entire career boiling down from heavyweight proportions. He rehydrated into the 180s and 190s just to bully super middleweights, and at cruiserweight he walks around comfortably above 215. Usyk weighed in the mid-220s for his heavyweight fights.

There is zero reason this fight could not happen at heavyweight, or at least a sensible catchweight, other than the tactical gamesmanship of the narrative.

Benavidez also plays along because he wants no part of heavyweights right now. Facing Usyk at 200 gives Benavidez the biggest brand name in the sport without having to step into the heavyweight ring against giant punchers. It lets Benavidez bypass the true divisional ruler, Jai Opetaia, avoid the terrifying risk of prime cruiserweights, and cash in against a depleted legend.

Both camps know exactly what they are doing. It provides Benavidez a shortcut to a massive scalp and gives Usyk a pre-packaged alibi if his legs fail him down the stretch.

Jai Opetaia belongs in this conversation too. The Ring previously reported Benavidez might target their cruiserweight champion after Cieslak. Moving toward Usyk creates a massive spectacle, yet it sidelines the most dangerous active force currently ruling the division.

Toppling Usyk creates an incredible legacy moment. It still leaves questions about true cruiserweight supremacy if Opetaia stays undefeated on the sideline.

Benavidez gets a crack at an all-time great. Usyk wagers his body can handle the scales without losing the stamina needed to survive deep water. That specific tension turns this matchup into must-see theater.

Ghana News.title: NACOC destroys cannabis farms in Nadowli District
Ghana News.content:
The Upper West Regional Command of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), in a joint operation with officers of the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS), has destroyed several cannabis farms at Siiru, a community in the Nadowli District of the Upper West Region.

The operation followed intelligence gathered by officers of the Ghana Immigration Service, which led the joint team to suspected cannabis cultivation sites in the community, located near the Black Volta.

During the exercise, the team identified several locations where cannabis was being cultivated. Some plants had already been harvested, while others were at various stages of maturity and nearly ready for harvest.

Further searches uncovered cannabis farms in incomplete buildings, in front of residential properties and alongside maize farms, suggesting that the illegal cultivation was taking place in different parts of the community.

The identified cannabis plants were subsequently destroyed by burning.

Following the operation, officers engaged community members in an education and sensitisation exercise on the dangers and consequences of cannabis cultivation and substance abuse.

The team urged residents to support efforts to combat illicit drug cultivation and distribution by providing timely information to the relevant authorities.

Ghana News.title: NAIMOS not adequately equipped to fight galamsey – Awula Serwah
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of EcoConscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, has raised concerns about the operational capacity of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), questioning whether it has the necessary equipment and logistical support to effectively combat illegal mining.

She believes the resources available to the anti-galamsey task force are inadequate to match the scale of illegal mining activities across the country.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 31, she questioned whether NAIMOS, the Forestry Commission and other stakeholders in the fight against galamsey on the ground had access to essential protective equipment, including bulletproof vests, particularly when some illegal miners were reportedly armed and equipped with similar protective gear.

She also raised concerns about the logistical capacity of these task forces, questioning whether their personnel had the necessary resources to sustain operations in areas affected by illegal mining.

"It is difficult to understand that two years into the administration, the situation does not appear to be improving. And I would also say that if we want to avert the catastrophe, we need to better equip our duty bearers. If you look at the Forestry Commission, for instance, the forestry guards who are supposed to be protecting our forests do not even have bulletproof vests; two of them have been shot, and I believe one of them is dead"

"And then we look at NAIMOS, do they have the resources they need to do the work they are mandated to do? Do they have speedboats? How do they pursue those on our water bodies?"

"The situation is dire," she added.

Despite these concerns, Ms Serwah acknowledged the efforts of NAIMOS, saying she believed its personnel had done their best under the circumstances.

"NAIMOS is doing a very good job with the limited resources they have. But you have to look at the scale of the problem," she noted.

She maintained that strengthening the task force's operational capacity would be critical to improving the fight against galamsey.

Ghana News.title: Galamsey fight remains ineffective despite NAIMOS arrests and seizures – Awula Serwah
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of Eco-Conscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, says Ghana has made little meaningful progress in the fight against illegal mining, warning that the country remains at risk of an ecological catastrophe.

She argues that despite government announcements of arrests and the confiscation of mining equipment, illegal mining activities continue to threaten rivers and other natural resources.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 31, she questioned whether politically connected individuals involved in illegal mining were being arrested and prosecuted.

“We talk about arrests, but how many politically connected persons or so-called high fliers have actually been arrested and prosecuted?” she asked.

Ms Serwah also expressed concern that chanfang machines and excavators continued to find their way onto water bodies and into mining areas, despite the government's enforcement operations.

She further questioned the effectiveness of the planned reclamation of degraded lands, insisting that the government must demonstrate how its interventions are producing lasting environmental improvements.

“So from where we are sitting and our activists up and down the country, we cannot say that things have become better and we still face a national emergency, and we are still on the verge of an ecological catastrophe,” she said.

Her comments come amid renewed government efforts to intensify the fight against galamsey. President John Dramani Mahama has disclosed that more than 8,200 items used in illegal mining, including 135 excavators and nearly 200 firearms, have been confiscated. He has also announced plans to reclaim 5,000 acres of degraded land from 2027, with GH¢200 million allocated for the exercise.

However, Ms Serwah's assessment raises questions about whether enforcement, equipment seizures and reclamation plans are sufficient to dismantle illegal mining networks and protect Ghana's water bodies and forests.

Ghana News.title: Galamsey: Ghana still faces national emergency, says Awula Serwah
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of Eco-Conscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, has warned that Ghana remains in a national emergency over illegal mining, arguing that current interventions have yet to deliver the environmental progress needed to protect the country's natural resources.

She said that despite government claims of arrests, equipment seizures and plans to reclaim degraded lands, illegal mining continued to threaten rivers, forests and farmlands across the country.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 31, Ms Serwah questioned the impact of enforcement measures, particularly the prosecution of influential individuals allegedly connected to illegal mining.

“We talk about arrest, but how many politically connected persons or so-called high fliers have actually been arrested and prosecuted?” she asked.

She also expressed concern that chanfang machines remained on water bodies while excavators continued to enter and leave the country, raising questions about the effectiveness of efforts to prevent illegal mining operations from resuming.

Ms Serwah further questioned the government's proposed land reclamation programme, asking what reclamation would entail in practical terms and whether it would result in lasting environmental recovery.

“From where we are sitting and our activists up and down the country, we cannot say that things have become better and we still face a national emergency and we are still on the verge of an ecological catastrophe,” she said.

Her concerns come after President John Dramani Mahama announced that more than 8,200 items linked to illegal mining had been confiscated, including 135 excavators and nearly 200 firearms.

The President has also outlined plans to reclaim 5,000 acres of degraded land from 2027, with GH¢200 million allocated to the exercise. The plans also include expanded river protection operations and sustained enforcement in areas cleared of illegal miners.

However, Ms Serwah said the continued destruction of water bodies and other ecosystems meant Ghana could not yet declare victory in the fight against galamsey.

She is calling for stronger accountability and evidence that government interventions are producing sustainable results.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t wants to use Traffitech-GH to extort money from drivers while traders take over spaces – GPRTU
Ghana News.content:
Commercial transport operators have accused the government of seeking to use the planned rollout of the Traffitech-GH system to extort money from drivers through traffic fines while allowing traders to occupy designated bus stops and pedestrian walkways.

The operators say it is unfair to subject drivers to camera-based traffic enforcement when the authorities have failed to clear the spaces they are legally expected to use for picking up and dropping off passengers.

They have consequently threatened to suspend public transport services nationwide from Sunday, November 1, when Traffitech-GH is scheduled to become operational, unless their concerns are addressed.

The ultimatum was issued in a statement dated October 31 by the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), the Commercial Transport Operators of Ghana and the Concerned Drivers Association of Ghana, operating under the Joint Transport Front.

The statement was signed by Samuel Amoah, National Deputy Public Relations Officer of the GPRTU of TUC; Asonaba Nana Owiredu, National Chairman of the Commercial Transport Operators of Ghana; Paa Willie, National Chairman of the Concerned Drivers Association of Ghana; David Agboado, National PRO of the Concerned Drivers Association of Ghana; and Yaw Barimah, National PRO of the Commercial Transport Operators/True Drivers Union.

The groups said they had earlier given the government and the Ghana Police Service until October 20 to enforce Regulation 142 of L.I. 2519 by removing traders from bus stops and pedestrian walkways before the introduction of the new traffic enforcement system.

However, they claimed that the deadline had passed without any meaningful action by the government, the Ministry of Local Government or the police.

“This shows clearly that the government wants to use TRAFFITECH-GH to extort money from innocent drivers while leaving traders to take over our legally designated spaces,” the statement said.

Bus stops remain occupied

The operators cited Kaneshie, Circle, Madina, Kasoa and Kejetia among areas where they claimed traders continued to occupy designated bus stops.

They said the situation would expose drivers to fines and harassment by traffic cameras for offences arising from the authorities’ failure to keep the designated spaces accessible.

“We cannot allow our drivers to be fined and harassed by cameras for offences created by the government's own failure to clear the roads,” the groups stated.

They maintained that the authorities should first address the alleged encroachment on bus stops and pedestrian walkways before enforcing the new system against commercial drivers.

Nationwide shutdown threat

The groups said their leadership had resolved to direct drivers across the country to park their vehicles and suspend operations once Traffitech-GH became operational on November 1.

“We will not operate under an unfair and unjust system. You cannot digitalise illegality,” they declared.

They also appealed to commuters to take notice of the planned action and make alternative transport arrangements from Sunday, warning that the suspension could disrupt travel across the country.

“The government will be fully responsible for any inconvenience this action will cause,” the statement added.

The latest warning follows a joint press conference held on October 13, during which the operators called on the government and the police to clear traders from bus stops and pedestrian walkways ahead of the system's introduction.

Ghana News.title: Transport operators threaten nationwide strike as Traffitech-GH begins on Nov 1
Ghana News.content:
Commercial transport operators have threatened to suspend services nationwide on November 1, when the Traffitech-GH system is scheduled to become operational, accusing the government and the police of failing to clear traders from designated bus stops and pedestrian walkways.

The operators, led by the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), the Commercial Transport Operators of Ghana and the Concerned Drivers Association of Ghana, say they will direct their members to park their vehicles if the authorities proceed with the rollout without addressing their concerns.

In a statement dated October 31, 2026, the groups said they had given the government and the Ghana Police Service until October 20 to enforce Regulation 142 of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2180), which they cited as the legal basis for clearing traders from bus stops and pedestrian walkways.

The latest statement was signed by Samuel Amoah, National Deputy Public Relations Officer of the GPRTU of TUC; Asonaba Nana Owiredu, National Chairman of the Commercial Transport Operators of Ghana; Paa Willie, National Chairman of the Concerned Drivers Association of Ghana; David Agboado, National PRO of the Concerned Drivers Association of Ghana; and Yaw Barimah, National PRO of the Commercial Transport Operators/True Drivers Union.

They said the deadline had passed without the action they were demanding.

According to the operators, bus stops in areas including Kaneshie, Circle, Madina, Kasoa and Kejetia, as well as those in other major towns, remained occupied by traders.

The groups argue that introducing camera-based traffic enforcement while designated stopping areas remain obstructed would expose drivers to penalties for circumstances they say are beyond their control.

Operators accuse the government of unfair enforcement

The transport groups contend that the authorities should address the occupation of bus stops before using the new system to enforce traffic regulations.

They accused the government of seeking to impose fines on drivers without first resolving what they described as the failure to protect legally designated spaces for loading and unloading passengers.

“This shows clearly that the government wants to use TRAFFITECH-GH to extort money from innocent drivers while leaving traders to take over our legally designated spaces,” the statement said.

The operators said they would not accept a system they considered unfair, warning that drivers should not be penalised for stopping or operating in areas where traders had allegedly taken over designated transport spaces.

“We will not operate under an unfair and unjust system. You cannot digitalise illegality,” they declared.

Travelling public warned

The groups said they would direct drivers to suspend operations as soon as Traffitech-GH became operational on November 1.

They also urged commuters to make alternative transport arrangements from that date, warning that the planned action could disrupt movement if the dispute remained unresolved.

“The government will be fully responsible for any inconvenience this action will cause,” the statement added.

The proposed shutdown follows an earlier joint press conference on October 13, during which the operators said they had called on the government and the police to clear traders from bus stops and pedestrian walkways before the system's introduction.

The government, the Ministry of Local Government and the Ghana Police Service are yet to respond to the allegations in the statement.

Ghana News.title: Akim Swedru MP supports 145 traders, apprentices and artisans
Ghana News.content:
The Member of Parliament for Akim Swedru, Kennedy Osei Nyarko, has provided financial and skills development support to 145 constituents as part of efforts to promote entrepreneurship and vocational training.

The beneficiaries comprise 50 petty traders, 60 prospective apprentices and 35 newly graduated apprentices, who received assistance to strengthen their businesses, acquire vocational skills or establish themselves in their chosen trades.

The 50 traders received financial assistance to support their business operations and improve their income-generating activities.

Another 60 young people received support to undertake apprenticeship training, allowing them to acquire practical skills for employment and self-employment.

The remaining 35 beneficiaries, who had completed their apprenticeships, were provided with tools and equipment to enable them to begin practising their trades and build their own livelihoods.

The intervention, carried out during the week, is intended to address some of the financial and practical challenges facing small-scale business owners, young people seeking vocational training and artisans transitioning into independent work.

Ghana News.title: ‘We cannot feed our families’ — 170 college staff withdraw services
Ghana News.content:
About 170 staff of the Savannah College of Education at Daboya in the Savannah Region have withdrawn their services over delays in migrating them onto the government payroll, more than a year after the institution was absorbed into the public Colleges of Education system.

The teaching and non-teaching staff say they will not return to work until concrete steps are taken to place them on the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department payroll, describing their continued exclusion as financially unbearable.

In a joint press conference in Daboya in the Savannah Region, members of two local associations at the Savannah College of Education, namely, the Colleges of Education Teachers Association of Ghana [CETAG] and the Colleges of Education Non-Teaching Staff Association of Ghana (CENTSAG) said the transition of the college into the public system can not be deemed complete while staff continue to work without government-paid salaries and a clear roadmap for their migration.

"Our concern is not to undermine government efforts or disregard the progress made since the college became a public institution. Rather, we seek to draw attention to the unresolved issues surrounding staff remuneration, recruitment and migration onto the government payroll, which continue to threaten staff and the smooth administration of the college," they indicated.

The college was absorbed into the public system in March 2025, but the staff say none of them has been migrated onto the government payroll since then.

Jacob Kotochi, a lecturer at the institution, said staff had continued working in anticipation of a resolution, despite mounting financial difficulties.

He said the government had honoured its commitment to pay student allowances but had yet to address the employment and salary concerns of the college’s workforce.

“The government fulfilled one side, which was to pay the student allowances, but staff were still left out. And I can tell you that since March 2025 to now, no single staff member from the college has been put on any payroll,” he said.

Staff struggle to support families

Mr Kotochi said the delay had placed considerable pressure on staff who had families to support, particularly amid rising living costs and expenses associated with working away from home.

He said the allowances currently available to staff were inadequate, with the highest-paid personnel receiving less than GH¢2,000 and some receiving as little as GH¢500.

“How much more to feed a family with GH¢1,800?” he asked, describing the situation as unbearable.

The staff say their financial difficulties have persisted despite the college’s transition into the public education system, leaving them uncertain about when they will receive regular salaries through the government payroll.

Appeals yield no results

Mr Kotochi said the decision to withdraw services followed several attempts to resolve the matter through engagements with stakeholders, including traditional authorities and regional officials.

He said the staff had pursued different channels in the hope of securing a solution but had yet to see any meaningful outcome.

“We didn’t just get up out of the blue to embark on this industrial strike. We have tried several times to meet all relevant stakeholders. Management even led us; they went to the paramount chief in Daboya. We’ve been told that the overlord, we went; I think the regional minister, all the key holders we went, we engaged them, and still we are not seeing any result,” he said.

He insisted that the withdrawal of services would continue until the staff’s migration onto the public payroll was secured.

The action puts the spotlight on the unresolved employment and remuneration concerns at the college following its absorption into the public Colleges of Education system in March 2025.

The staff are demanding concrete action to regularise their employment and provide them with a reliable salary arrangement.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Dead dolphins, naval mines: Russia-Ukraine war destroys the Black Sea
World.content:
Russia’s war in Ukraine is devastating Black Sea marine life, killing more than 120,000 dolphins and causing ecological damage.

Kyiv, Ukraine – Fishers and poachers along the Black Sea coast often find suffocated dolphins entangled in their nets,

They release them by cutting off their fins and dropping them in the sea. Their bodies, with net marks on their skin, are often washed ashore.

Fishing and poaching in littoral Black Sea nations plummeted because of Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion, as Moscow strove to occupy all of Ukraine’s Black Sea coast.

It failed – but the ongoing hostilities have been killing “hundreds times more” bottlenose and short-beaked dolphins and harbour porpoises, according to Ivan Rusev, head researcher at the Tuzly Lagoons national park in southern Ukraine.

In 2022 alone, some 50,000 dolphins died this way, and by 2026, the number exceeded 120,000, or one in four cetaceans in the Black Sea, Rusev told Al Jazeera.

Dolphins are apex predators, and their decimation further ruins the Black Sea’s ecosystem already affected by chemicals from munitions, spills of oil, fuel and vegetable oils from dozens of sunk or damaged warships, tankers and freighters.

Many dead dolphins still have their fins, but look starved.

Explosions, launches of cruise missiles from warships, and military sonar systems confuse them, deafening their primary survival tool, echolocation, and making them unable to navigate, communicate and hunt.

“If a dolphin can’t fish, it loses weight fast,” said Rusev, whose park covers 280 square kilometres (108 square miles) of salty lagoons that serve as a stopover and breeding site for migratory birds.



The dolphins switch to consuming their blubber that has already accumulated pollutants from wastewater, agricultural runoff, microplastics and antibiotics.

The self-poisoning incapacitates their immune system, and they succumb to lethal respiratory tract infections caused by the so-called morbillivirus.

The Black Sea is one of the world’s youngest – some scholars hypothesise that it was a freshwater lake until about eight millennia ago, when the Bosporus Strait burst open, causing what may have been the biblical Great Flood.

The sea’s waters lack oxygen and support no fauna or flora below 50 to 100 metres.

The chronic environmental damage from the war was aggravated by another shock: the 2023 destruction of the giant Kakhovka dam on the Dnipro River, releasing most of its 18 cubic kilometres (4.3 cubic miles) of water contaminated with fertiliser runoff, heavy metals and machine oil.

Fish species such as mullet and bluefish have become scarce, even though fishing in Black Sea nations has been affected by restrictions, bans and naval mines that were spotted near Istanbul.

The changes inevitably affect the dolphins.

“With dolphins at the top of the food chain, everything from zooplankton to fish reaches them,” Rusev said.

Environmentalists from other Black Sea nations – Bulgaria, Romania, Turkiye – also reported a spike in dolphin deaths, even though the cause of their death couldn’t always be established.

“Most of the stranded dead cetaceans are usually in an advanced state of decomposition, making detection of net marks and other marks almost impossible,” Dimitar Popov of Green Balkans, Bulgaria’s oldest nature conservation group, told Al Jazeera.

He agrees with Rusev that “sonar systems of warships and submarines definitely affect cetaceans and their echolocation and hearing abilities”.

Meanwhile, Russian environmental monitors blamed the dolphin deaths on “parasites” and “virus infections” without any further explanation.

And even though only a tiny percentage of dead dolphins are washed ashore, their appearance horrifies Ukrainians already unnerved by nearly daily drone and missile attacks.

In August, Tetiana Smolchenko enjoyed a seaside stroll with her eight-year-old son Oleh in the southern city of Odesa – until the child spotted an emaciated, decaying dolphin.

“I nearly threw up,” the 33-year-old, whose husband serves in the military and whose apartment building has been damaged by a Russian drone twice, told Al Jazeera.



“We’re so used to human deaths now, but seeing these creatures die because of the war is no less horrifying,” she said. “We both wept.”

What looks like a military triumph could become a heavy blow to the marine ecosystem.

Since 2022, Ukrainian sea and airborne drones have sunk two submarines and three dozen Russian warships, including the Black Sea Fleet’s flagship, the Moskva (Moscow) guided missile cruiser.

They were all loaded with toxic fuel and other chemicals.

Even though Ukrainian drone operators attacking Russian “shadow fleet” tankers are instructed to specifically target their engines, oil and fuel spills continue to happen.

Oil molecules form a film that coats seaweed, poisoning molluscs and fish, especially sturgeons that die in droves.

Every explosion deafens and kills fish, and the sound, coupled with flying drones, startles birds migrating back and forth between Northern Europe and the Middle East.

“And when a bird can’t find enough food, doesn’t have ‘fuel,’ it can’t reach the destination where it winters or nests,” Rusev said. “It will affect the number of certain bird populations for years.”

Startled by the blasts, flamingoes, who only started nesting in his park years ago, are leaving their hatches, and seagulls immediately eat the eggs, he said.

The war’s only silver lining for wild nature around the sea is that the number of boars, roes, foxes, jackals, hares and badgers has risen because hunting and poaching nearly stopped, he said.

And the ecosystem’s post-war recovery is going to be uneven.

While the number of insects and small mammals should return to normal within years, the dolphin population’s recovery will take decades.

“We estimate that it would take 30 to 50 years to renew the population of cetaceans, so that the sea ecosystem becomes more or less normal,” Rusev said.

World.title: RSF senior commander defects, accusing Sudan group’s leadership of nepotism
World.content:
Siddiq Ander has accused RSF leader Hemedti of running the paramilitary group like a family business and suppressing dissent.

Senior commander Siddiq Ander says he has defected from Sudan‘s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), according to exclusive video footage obtained by Al Jazeera.

The footage, published on Friday, shows Ander accusing relatives of RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemedti”, of tightly controlling the group’s finances, weapons, troop movements and military promotions.

Ander’s exit follows a string of high-profile defections this year, with some commanders leaving alongside hundreds of fighters.

“It has become clear to us beyond any doubt that we were serving a purely family-based project controlled by Hemedti’s relatives in every aspect, money, weapons, fighters’ movements and the granting of ranks,” Ander said.

“Anyone who speaks out and tells the whole truth faces expulsion, imprisonment or a hidden death.”

Hemedti’s brother, Abdul Rahim Hamdan Dagalo, serves as the RSF deputy commander.

Senior commanders break ranks

A wave of defections has seen several senior RSF commanders leave the group this year, including Lieutenant Colonel Mohammed Azraq al-Fanjari, who announced on October 8 that he was leaving, along with 300 officers and soldiers and 30 military vehicles.

Al-Fanjari also urged other fighters to abandon the RSF, expressing regret over the suffering caused by the war.

His announcement came after the September 25 defection of Al-Tayeb al-Wahidu, who joined the enemy Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) with 50 fighters in Omdurman, across the Nile from the capital, Khartoum, according to The Sudan Tribune.



Al-Wahidu cited abuses within the RSF as his reason for leaving.

Earlier, in May, Brigadier Ali Rizqallah, known as Savannah, announced his departure.

Yet another senior commander, Major General al-Nour Ahmed Adam, known as al-Qubba, joined the SAF in April and was publicly welcomed by Sudanese leader and military chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.

Al-Qubba’s departure followed disagreements over military appointments within the RSF leadership, the Tribune reported.

Sudan’s war erupted in April 2023 after a power struggle between the army and the RSF, including disagreements over plans to integrate the paramilitary group into the regular military.

The conflict has since displaced about 13 million people and pushed parts of the country into famine.

The latest defections come as both sides increasingly use drones in attacks that have caused mounting civilian casualties.

On October 26, strikes hit a market and residential area in Nyala, an RSF-controlled city in South Darfur.

Emergency Lawyers, a Sudanese rights group, reported more than 100 deaths, although other medical organisations recorded lower figures.

The United Nations says drone strikes have become the leading cause of civilian deaths in Sudan’s war.

World.title: Are Houthis using Russian satellites as Saudi Arabia fends off strikes?
World.content:
Analysts say the seizure of state arsenals, external backing and extensive military evolution has enabled the Houthis to build a powerful arsenal.

Share Are Houthis using Russian satellites as Saudi Arabia fends off strikes? on social media

An investigation has revealed that Russian satellites are assisting the Iran-aligned Houthis to strike Saudi Arabia’s military and energy infrastructure, further upending global energy markets amid the US war on Iran.

Hostilities between the internationally recognised Yemeni government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia, and the Houthis have been ongoing since July and escalated in September when the rebel group seized full control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast.

Last month, the Houthis also carried out a precision strike on pumping stations on Saudi Arabia’s most important oil pipeline, the East-West pipeline. An investigation by Geneva-based private firm AURORAH GeoSignal Intelligence revealed that Russian satellites had been surveying the region days in advance to gather intelligence about the pipeline.
