World.title: Atiku accuses INEC of shielding officials behind voter register fraud
World.content:
Atiku Abubakar

By Luminous Jannamike

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of concealing evidence and shielding officials implicated in irregularities in the voter register, warning that the scandal threatens the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

Atiku said INEC’s admission that AI-generated images and other irregularities had entered the register through registration officers exposed a grave failure of leadership and safeguards at the electoral body, raising fresh questions about the integrity of the database on which millions of Nigerians depend to exercise their franchise.

In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded the identification and prosecution of officials involved, full disclosure of evidence and an independent forensic audit of the voter register.

He described INEC’s explanation of how the register was compromised as an attempt to evade responsibility.

“That is a disgraceful evasion, not an answer. Even ordinary WhatsApp, Facebook and email accounts appear to have stronger security safeguards than those INEC’s ICT director described on national television. How can the database holding the votes of millions of Nigerians be less secure than a personal social media account?” he asked.

Atiku said the Commission must disclose how the register was compromised, identify every officer involved and explain why those implicated had not been suspended or prosecuted.

“Amupitan cannot admit the misconduct, withhold the perpetrators’ identities and expect Nigerians to accept ignorance as an excuse. He must account for this failure now,” he said.

The former vice president also demanded an independent forensic audit, citing allegations that more than 20 million AI-generated images may have been involved.

He warned against any attempt by INEC to quietly remove disputed records without preserving evidence of how the irregularities occurred.

“Preserve every voter record, image file, access log and audit trail. Let accredited independent experts, political parties, civil society and credible international observers examine the evidence. No disputed record should be certified until the audit is complete,” he said.

Atiku further accused INEC of ignoring opposition parties’ demand for disclosure of companies contracted to produce sensitive election materials, insisting that secrecy over the contractors and their operating protocols was incompatible with a credible election.

He demanded that the Commission publish the contractors’ identities and explain the safeguards governing their work, arguing that opposition parties deserved the same information available to the APC-led Federal Government.

The former vice president threatened legal action if INEC failed to disclose the information and account for the alleged misconduct.

“If INEC refuses to disclose the truth, we will go to court and compel it. Every official found to have tampered with the register must be prosecuted,” he said.

Atiku also urged opposition leaders and the international community to demand full disclosure, an independent audit and accountability, accusing President Bola Tinubu’s government of enabling the crisis by allowing INEC to evade scrutiny.

He said the Commission could not demand public trust while withholding evidence and shielding those responsible.

“Name the culprits, expose the contractors and submit the register and election materials to independent scrutiny. Until then, its assurances are worthless. The credibility of the 2027 election is on the line,” he said.

World.title: Senegal kicks off Youth Games, Africa’s first ever Olympics
World.content:
Senegal’s Influencer and TikToker Khaby Lame carries the Youth Olympic Flame on the eve of the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on October 30, 2026. Over the course of two weeks some 2,700 athletes aged 17 or younger are expected to compete across 25 sports, including Russians who are returning to the Games following a ban. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking will be held across eight venues in three locations (Photo by PATRICK MEINHARDT / AFP)

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, open Saturday in the Senegalese capital marking an historic moment for the continent.

Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are abundant across Dakar, which is hosting some 2,665 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world.

The event marks the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events.

“We’ve got people from around the world that maybe had a very different idea about Africa and they’re going to leave, hopefully, with something really positive in mind”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Thursday during a press conference in Dakar.

“I think that is really important for our continent”, she said.

Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations.

Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events.

– Sports culture –

An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games.

A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event.

The west African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene.

Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or weekends on the beach or in village squares.

And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise.

While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics have struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal.

Many are more concerned with the high cost of living, unemployment and economic hardship.

“Once the youth Olympic Games in Senegal begin, Dakar will become the capital of African youth,” Senegal Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo said in an interview with AFP this week.

“Africa hosting the (Youth) Olympic Games, it’s a symbol”, he said.

– Russian athletes –

With the IOC effectively lifting the Russian Olympic Committee’s (ROC) suspension in July, the Youth Games will mark the first Olympic competition since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 in which Russian athletes are allowed to compete under their own flag and colours.

According to the ROC, 13 Russian athletes will participate and 10 coaches will accompany them to Senegal.

“The kids are excited, it’s good news that our legitimate right to participate with the national anthem and Russian flag has been restored”, Anzor Gaunov, who coaches Anastasia Dobrovolskaya in judo, told AFP earlier this month in Moscow.

However, it is up to each sport’s international federation whether to authorise the Russian athletes’ participation.

The Dakar Youth Games will also welcome a refugee Olympic team, composed primarily of athletes based in Africa.

The IOC has called the Dakar Games an important milestone for the continent and an opportunity to showcase Senegal’s cultural richness and Africa’s growing role within the Olympics.

South Africa could potentially become the first African nation to host the Olympic Games, having already paved the way by hosting the men’s FIFA World Cup in 2010. The country is officially in the running for the 2036 Summer Olympics.

AFP

World.title: US judge issues restraining order against Justice Dept over election directives
World.content:
Election in United States of America. Voter holds envelope in hand above vote ballot. USA flags in background. Democracy concept.

A US federal judge temporarily blocked on Friday the Justice Department from threatening state and local election officials with criminal prosecution if they fail to comply with its directives on processing ballots.

The order by Judge Trina Thompson in the Northern District of California deals a setback to Trump administration efforts to restrict voting by people it says might not be US citizens in the November 3 midterm elections.

The harshly worded temporary restraining order was issued in response to a case brought by labor union and civil rights groups against the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security.

“Defendants shall not threaten, intimidate or coerce state or local elections officials or workers to demand that they halt processing the ballots of any registered voter solely on the basis that the ballot belongs to an individual alleged by Defendants to be ineligible to vote,” Thompson wrote.

The judge also ruled that Justice Department officials “shall not threaten state or local election officials and workers with criminal prosecution for failure to comply” with such demands.

President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is at risk of losing its control of Congress in next Tuesday’s elections, and critics have accused his administration of trying to cast doubt on electoral results.

On Wednesday, a federal judge rejected the Justice Department’s efforts to set aside the ballots of more than 20,000 California voters it said might not be citizens, slamming the move as brazen pre-election “interference.”

In Friday’s ruling, Thompson said that a restraining order, which expires on November 16, was justified “given the fast-approaching date of the Election” and because the plaintiffs “have demonstrated that they will likely succeed on the merits of their claims.”

Thompson described the “intimidation” and threats of criminal prosecution of election workers as “contrary to law” and “arbitrary and capricious.”

In a wide-ranging order, the judge said the defendants shall not demand the removal of specific registered voters from voter lists, nor refuse to issue ballots to specific voters nor demand ballots not be counted because of alleged ineligibility to vote.

For months, Trump — who has never acknowledged his own election defeat by Joe Biden in 2020 — has been claiming that there will be fraud in this year’s midterms.

Studies repeatedly show that while rare cases of voter fraud exist, such incidents are minuscule and do not influence US election results.

AFP

World.title: Police confirm rescue of 3 kidnapped Zamfara Islamic clerics
World.content:
The Zamfara Commissioner of Police, CP Muhammad Bello, has confirmed the rescue of three of the six Islamic Clerics (Imam) kidnapped on September 12, while travelling to Talata Mafara, Zamfara.

Bello gave the confirmation in an interview with some select reporters on Friday in Gusau.

He said the rescue followed a multi-agency collaboration and seamless synergy between the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), the Department of State Services (DSS) and police operatives.

The CP said security tactical operations remained ongoing in full force, leveraging real-time intelligence supplied by local community members to track down the remaining armed bandits and ensure the safe rescue of the three clerics still in captivity.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the ONSA, in a high-stakes intelligence-driven collaboration with the DSS and the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), rescued the three Islamic clerics kidnapped while en route to a special prayer session for President Bola Tinubu in Talata Mafara, Zamfara.

NAN also reports that the victims were part of a group of six Islamic clerics abducted on Sept. 12, when heavily armed bandits intercepted them around 11:30 a.m. on the Dakko-Damri feeder road near Sububu Forest in Bakura Local Government Area.

The clerics, identified as Imam Yahuza, Magawata Abdullahi, Malam Shehu Dakko, Imam Bala Fagon and Na’ibi Tasi’u, were travelling to Talata Mafara to attend a special prayer gathering to seek divine favour for Tinubu’s administration.

Their abductors had reportedly demanded N30 million ransom for their release.

A senior security operative involved in the extraction also confirmed that the three clerics were rescued unhurt following meticulous, intelligence-led manoeuvres.

NAN learnt that the clerics are said to be in stable condition after receiving medical evaluation and expert debriefing.

The security operatives confirmed that the three clerics were slated for formal handover to the Zamfara Government to reunite them with their families.

The Police command assured that operational leads would continue, urging the public to maintain a vigilant flow of timely, actionable information to help flush out terrorist elements across the region.

(NAN)

World.title: Sowore, police differ over attack in Ekiti
World.content:
Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), and the Ekiti State Police Command have given conflicting accounts of an incident at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, on Friday.

While Sowore insisted that he and members of his team were violently attacked, the police described the incident as an altercation with some individuals, saying the activist sustained a minor injury.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, said the command received an alert that Sowore was having issues with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti and immediately deployed operatives to the scene.

Abutu said the operatives rescued the AAC presidential candidate and took him to the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti, where he was receiving treatment.

However, Sowore, in a statement published on his social media accounts, rejected the police description of the incident as an “altercation”.

“There was no altercation! We were attacked!” he declared.

He accused the Ekiti State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) of attempting to suppress evidence relating to the incident.

Sowore alleged that security operatives seized CCTV footage from the restaurant where the incident occurred, claiming that the attackers were captured on camera and accusing the agencies of attempting to shield those responsible.

He also faulted the state Commissioner of Police, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, for describing the incident as an altercation, saying the police commissioner had visited the scene and seen the injuries sustained by the victims but subsequently played down their severity.

Sowore further alleged that DSS operatives had been trailing and harassing him since his arrival in the state on Thursday.

He claimed that the operatives also threatened the manager of a restaurant where he and his team had earlier eaten, warning him against allowing them to use the premises again.

He said the attack occurred shortly after he concluded an interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 in Ado-Ekiti on Friday.

Sowore also alleged that some of the attackers came from the Ekiti State Government House and received operational support from DSS operatives.

Police Response

The police, however, denied reports that the activist was kidnapped, following a social media post claiming that he had been seized by armed thugs and his whereabouts were unknown.

Abutu said in a statement that the command wished to clarify that Sowore was not kidnapped but was rescued by police operatives after they received information about the incident.

“The command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, following which the police were immediately alerted.

“Upon receiving the report, police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. He, however, sustained a minor injury and is currently receiving medical attention at the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti,” the statement read.

The police spokesman said the Commissioner of Police, Michael Falade, had ordered a discreet investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, identify those involved and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice.

The command urged members of the public to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information capable of creating panic and tension.

World.title: Rev360: Reimagining Tax Administration for a Digital Nigeria
World.content:
By Emmanuel Jonathan

For many taxpayers, the true measure of an effective tax system is not the complexity of its laws or the sophistication of its technology, but a much simpler question: how easy is it to comply?

This question is central to the Nigeria Revenue Service’s (NRS) ongoing transformation of tax administration through Rev360, its next-generation digital tax administration platform.

Since its go-live on 30th April, 2026, Rev360 has marked an important milestone in the Service’s transition towards a more integrated, intelligent and taxpayer-centric system. Building on previous advances in digital tax administration, the platform is designed to simplify compliance, improve service delivery, strengthen transparency and support more efficient revenue administration.

As implementation progresses, attention is increasingly shifting from the introduction of the platform to its adoption, operational effectiveness and the tangible improvements it delivers for taxpayers and other stakeholders.

More Than a Digital Platform

Rev360 comprises an interconnected digital architecture designed to serve different participants in the tax ecosystem.

The Unified Revenue Collections Workspace (URCW) is the internal workspace for NRS personnel. It provides staff with a digital environment for administering revenue and managing taxpayer-related processes and information.

The Taxpayer Self-Service Portal (TSSP) is the principal digital channel for taxpayers. It enables taxpayers to access tax services and interact with the NRS without depending entirely on physical offices and manual paperwork. Through the TSSP, taxpayers can undertake key compliance activities and access relevant services digitally.

The Tax Consultants’ Portal (TCP) provides a dedicated channel for tax consultants and professionals who assist taxpayers with their obligations. It gives them a structured digital interface through which they can support their clients.

The Government Tax Portal (GTP) is designed for Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), extending the digital tax environment into government institutions and supporting their interaction with tax administration.

The Developers’ Portal provides a connection point for third-party software developers and supports interoperability between external technology solutions and the wider Rev360 ecosystem.

The significance of these channels lies not merely in the existence of separate portals, but in their connection within a broader digital tax administration environment. Taxpayers, tax professionals, government institutions, NRS personnel and technology developers can therefore engage with the Service through channels designed around their respective roles.

What Rev360 Means for Taxpayers

For taxpayers, however, the technology behind Rev360 matters less than the experience it creates.

The important questions are practical: Can a taxpayer register more easily? Can returns be filed without unnecessary complications? Can payments be made conveniently? Can compliance issues be resolved more efficiently? Can taxpayers obtain assistance without repeated visits to tax offices?

The TSSP is particularly significant because it creates a direct digital channel between taxpayers and the NRS, providing access to services such as tax filing, payments, tax clearance, assessments and other taxpayer services.

The Tax ID also plays an important role in the wider digital tax administration framework by providing a basis for identifying taxpayers and supporting access to tax services. However, the Tax ID framework should be distinguished from Rev360 itself. The NRS Tax ID service states that the Tax ID is jointly issued by the NRS and the Joint Revenue Board in accordance with Nigerian tax laws.

For businesses, predictable processes and easier access to tax services can reduce the administrative burden associated with compliance.

The objective, therefore, is not simply to digitise existing procedures but to make the overall experience of dealing with the tax authority more convenient, accessible and predictable.

From Implementation to Adoption

Since its introduction, Rev360 has progressed through a phased implementation process designed to support an orderly transition for taxpayers and other stakeholders.

Beyond the deployment of technology, the NRS has prioritised stakeholder sensitisation, user training, technical support and continuous engagement to facilitate adoption and address implementation challenges.

The early implementation period is naturally one of adjustment. Taxpayers, professionals, government institutions and NRS personnel have to become familiar with the digital environment and adapt to processes that may differ from previous ways of working.

The success of Rev360 will ultimately be determined by measurable improvements in taxpayer experience, service reliability, processing efficiency, accessibility and voluntary compliance.

As implementation progresses, user feedback and operational performance data will remain essential to identifying opportunities for improvement and ensuring that the platform delivers on its objectives.

Turning Data into an Advantage

Another important dimension of digital tax administration is data.

Tax administration generates enormous amounts of information. When that information exists in disconnected systems, its usefulness can be limited. When appropriately integrated, it can provide a clearer picture of taxpayer behaviour, compliance patterns and revenue trends.

Rev360’s digital architecture is intended to support greater integration of tax administration processes and information. Such integration can help reduce duplication, improve coordination and strengthen the Service’s ability to use data in administering tax obligations.

The potential benefits extend beyond revenue collection. Reliable tax data can support economic planning and policy decisions by providing government with a stronger evidence base on economic activity.

This makes the digital transformation of tax administration relevant not only to taxpayers and the revenue authority but also to the wider economy.

Connecting to Global Tax Practice

Rev360 is being implemented at a time when tax administration globally is becoming increasingly digital.

Businesses increasingly operate across borders, while tax authorities are relying more heavily on digitalisation, data integration, transparency and information exchange.

Nigeria therefore needs a tax administration capable of operating effectively within this changing international environment.

A modern digital tax ecosystem can improve domestic administration while strengthening the country’s capacity to respond to developments in international taxation and cross-border economic activity.

Rev360 consequently represents an important stage in Nigeria’s continuing transition towards a more connected and digitally enabled tax administration.

Adoption Will Determine Success

Technology alone cannot guarantee transformation.

Nigeria’s taxpayer population is diverse, ranging from large corporations to medium-sized businesses, entrepreneurs, professionals and individual taxpayers. Their levels of digital literacy, access to technology and familiarity with tax processes vary.

This makes communication, taxpayer education and user support essential to the success of Rev360.

Users need clear information about which channel applies to them, what services they can access, how to use those services and where to obtain assistance when problems arise.

The success of digital tax administration will therefore depend not only on the technology itself but also on the ability of taxpayers and other stakeholders to understand, trust and effectively use the system.

As implementation continues, sustained engagement, responsive support and attention to user feedback will be critical to ensuring that the benefits of digitalisation are experienced across different categories of taxpayers and stakeholders.

The Real Measure of Transformation

The significance of Rev360 extends beyond the tax office.

Nigeria needs stronger domestic revenue to finance infrastructure, public services and development. At the same time, businesses need a tax environment that provides greater certainty, accessibility and predictability.

A more efficient digital tax administration can contribute to both objectives by making compliance easier for taxpayers while providing the revenue authority with more effective tools for administering the tax system.

The transformation of the NRS under the leadership of Executive Chairman Dr Zacch Adedeji reflects a broader effort to reposition tax administration around technology, data, efficiency and improved taxpayer experience.

But the real measure of that transformation will not be the sophistication of the technology or simply the number of digital channels created.

It will be whether taxpayers experience a meaningful difference.

Can taxpayers register and access services more easily? Can businesses file and pay with fewer complications? Can tax consultants manage their clients more efficiently? Can government institutions interact more effectively with the tax authority? Can NRS personnel work with better-integrated information? And can the Service use reliable data to improve compliance and revenue administration?

These are the questions that will increasingly define the success of Rev360.

Nigeria is moving from a tax administration shaped largely by physical processes towards one increasingly built around digital connectivity, integrated information and self-service.

Rev360 provides an important architecture for that transition.

Its ultimate achievement, however, will not be measured by technology alone. It will be measured by whether taxation becomes simpler for taxpayers, more efficient for government, more transparent for stakeholders and more predictable for the Nigerian economy.

*Emmanuel Jonathan, a Communications Expert and Manager with the Nigeria Revenue Service, writes from Abuja.

World.title: Obafemi Hamzat And ‘The Lagos Promise’
World.content:
By Mobolaji Sanusi

“The visionary starts with a clean sheet of paper, and re-imagines the world.”—Malcolm Gladwell

In my part of the world, one familiar cliché routinely finds its way into everyday conversations: “a promise is a debt.” It is an expression so frequently invoked that it has almost become an accepted principle of social interaction. But when it comes to the official conduct of public affairs in this part of the world, a fundamental question arises: Is a promise truly a debt, and can those who make promises in the political arena be held to account for fulfilling them?

Under the law of contract that applies across legal jurisdictions, an exchange of promises is generally recognised as legally binding and enforceable, except where it constitutes a nudum pactum, which means a bare agreement unsupported by consideration. In its everyday usage, Wikipedia defines a promise as “a commitment by someone to do or not to do something.” This also finds further expression in the universal Latin legal maxim, pacta sunt servanda, which states that agreements must be kept. The principle is not restricted to private contractual relationships; it also offers a compelling moral and political standard against which public commitments, including socio-political agreements between elected leaders and their constituents, ought to be measured.

As the 2027 general elections draw closer, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, the cerebral incumbent Deputy Governor of Lagos State and gubernatorial candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has taken a significant step towards establishing such a relationship of accountability with the people of Lagos. He has emerged as the first major gubernatorial contender across Nigeria to publicly present a concrete and actionable manifesto that he titles: “The Lagos Promise — Ìlérí Èkó.” The document, which he unveiled on Friday, sets out specific deliverables his administration intends to pursue when elected and inaugurated on May 29, 2027.

Hamzat’s firm grasp of the substance of the manifesto was evident even before its formal public unveiling. In his continuing engagements with stakeholders within and outside Lagos State, he has demonstrated a clear command of the policy direction and priorities that would shape his administration. During a recent visit to the President and Senior Chiefs of the Association of Lagos Titled Chiefs, preceding the public presentation of his manifesto, he demonstrated this grasp by extemporaneously outlining its seven pillars, 31 chapters, and 100 pledges.

In the presence of his hosts, including business tycoon Chief Kessington Adebutu and other prominent leaders, Hamzat offered an important clarification about the nature of the pledges contained in the document. He explained that 87 of the 100 pledges are commitments, while the remaining 13 are aspirations. This distinction, he maintained, was necessary because “government also has limits,” particularly in view of the constitutional delineation of powers and responsibilities among the judiciary, the Federal Government, and state governments.

His clarification is significant. It reflects an understanding that responsible leadership is not merely about making attractive promises to secure electoral support; it is also about recognising the constitutional, institutional, and empirical boundaries within which government must operate. Indeed, the credibility of a political manifesto should not be measured by the sheer volume of promises it contains, but by the realism of its commitments, the clarity of its implementation framework, and the capacity of its authors to translate policy intentions into measurable outcomes. This is the manifest difference between Hamzat’s “The Lagos Promise — Ìlérí Èkó” and the hitherto verbose compilations that other politicians across the country seeking elective positions call manifestos.

Yours sincerely believes that Hamzat’s institutional experience gives above proposition considerable weight. Having served in virtually every administration that has governed Lagos State, with the exception of one, he possesses an unusually deep understanding of the state’s governance architecture, administrative machinery, and development priorities. His accumulated experience is a significant advantage in his stated ambition to deliver on the commitments contained in “The Lagos Promise — Ìlérí Èkó.” It provides him with an appreciation of what works, what requires reform, and, perhaps more importantly, what is realistically achievable within the constitutional and operational confines of state governance.

His wealth of administrative experience is further complemented by his formidable political family pedigree, which provides an additional foundation for navigating the complex political terrain of Lagos State.

The inimitable sage, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, must have had someone of Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat’s stature in mind when he declared that, “Experience is a commodity that cannot be purchased in an open market; you must go through it.” Having traversed the demanding terrain of successive administrations and managerial governance since the time President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, as Governor of Lagos State, persuaded him to leave a prestigious professional engagement in the United States to serve his state, Hamzat has accumulated a wealth of experience and an impressive public service record that places him above other contenders in the 2027 Lagos governorship race. He’s certainly the next Lagos governor that is waiting to be crowned and this shall eventually come to pass, God willing.

Lagosians are indeed fortunate to have a potential governor with such rich and enduring political and administrative credentials. More importantly, they have standing before them a candidate with a clear vision, a firm grasp of the state’s challenges, and a genuine commitment to improving the lives of its people.

Despite widespread confidence in his competence, capacity, and electoral prospects, Hamzat is leaving no stone unturned as the 2027 election approaches. His campaign’s strategic leadership team, headed by noteworthy Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, a capable and tested veteran of many political battles, as Director-General, with the consistently dependable and seasoned political strategist, Honourable Rasak Ajala as Deputy Director-General, is already working assiduously to secure a resounding victory. The team, alongside other dedicated members of the campaign structure, operates under the strategic guidance of the respected Governor’s Advisory Council (GAC), led by our revered Baba Tajudeen Olusi.

The campaign has set an ambitious target of securing a victory margin of at least three million votes for Hamzat and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR. Yet, rather than rest on his widespread goodwill and confidence, Hamzat remains relentless in his pursuit of this objective.

He is approaching the campaign with the determination and energy of someone starting from ground zero, personally engaging critical stakeholders across the state. His consultations have extended to religious leaders in churches and mosques, social organisations, community influencers, political leaders, and even members of the opposition parties. His message is consistent: to present his programmes, communicate his vision for Lagos, and secure the trust and support of the electorate.

Equally central to his message is the importance of continuity in governance and the need for Lagosians to participate actively in the electoral process by coming out en masse to vote for him and return President Tinubu to office. For Hamzat, the task is not merely about winning an election; it is about sustaining the progress of Lagos while building on the foundations already laid.

Indeed, listening to Hamzat articulate his vision and mission for his beloved Lagos State leaves little doubt about his appreciation of the responsibilities and opportunities before him. His disposition aptly reflects the timeless observation of Joel Barker when he said: “Vision without action is merely a dream. Action without vision just passes the time. Vision with action can change the world.” Hamzat appears determined to translate this philosophy into practical governance by combining a clearly defined vision with purposeful and people-oriented action. His aspiration is to build a Lagos that works better for everyone, particularly law-abiding residents whose hopes and expectations he promised will remain at the centre of his government’s policy agenda.

“The Lagos Promise — Ìlérí Èkó,” Hamzat’s publicly unveiled social contract with Lagosians, is his commitment that should resonate with inhabitants of the state across ethnic, religious, social, and economic divides. Young and old, women and men, professionals, artisans, entrepreneurs, and ordinary residents all have a stake in his promises and commitments.

Hamzat understands the needs of the people and amongst his key priorities are improved road infrastructure, a more effective and sustainable environmental management system, better access to quality healthcare and education, a responsive and humane security architecture, an affordable and realistic housing system, redressing the trend of current elusive portable water for all, and creation of a business environment that encourages investment, innovation, enterprise, and job creation. These are not merely campaign talking points; they are critical pillars upon which a more prosperous, inclusive, and liveable Lagos will be built under Hamzat’s leadership.

Ultimately, the credibility of any political vision lies in its implementation. Lagosians should therefore engage with “The Lagos Promise — Ìlérí Èkó,” examine its commitments, and hold its proponents accountable for delivering on them. Once again, Hamzat’s experience, administrative pedigree, and understanding of the state’s governance architecture provide a compelling basis for believing that he has the capacity to translate these aspirations into tangible outcomes.

Yours sincerely believes that Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat’s emergence as the next Governor of Lagos State and Princess Damilola Sonayon-James as his deputy would mark another significant chapter in the state’s remarkable evolution. With the right blend of experience, vision, strategic leadership, and purposeful execution, Lagos can move beyond being an empire of the mind to becoming a true future empire of Nigeria and Africa, to borrow, with due apologies, from the words of Winston Churchill. The opportunity before Lagos is not simply to choose another governor; it is to choose the experience, vision, and capacity required to consolidate its achievements and boldly shape its future.

Hamzat is obviously at the moment the best choice to translate Lagosians’ desires into reality. Other candidates in states across the country need to learn something about prepared leadership from his starting point on Friday. With his clean sheet of paper containing his achievable promises, reimagining the future of Lagos is a foregone conclusion.

On this note, I hereby rest my case for the week.

•Sanusi, former MD/CEO of Lagos State Signage and  Agency, is currently Managing Partner at AMS RELIABLE SOLICITORS. (WhatsApp only: 07011117777).

World.title: NDLEA: No Payment Required for Drug Integrity Test by Interior Ministry Recruits
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has warned applicants undergoing recruitment into four agencies under the Ministry of Interior against making payments for the mandatory Drug Integrity Test (DIT).

The agency said the Ministry of Interior had already made bulk payment to cover the testing of new intakes into the Nigerian Correctional Service, Nigeria Immigration Service, Federal Fire Service and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.

NDLEA, in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja by its Director, Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, stressed that no candidate or personnel would be required to pay for the exercise.

It consequently advised all participating agencies and their personnel not to make payments to NDLEA officials, testing centres or through any other payment channel in connection with the exercise.

According to the agency, arrangements have been concluded for the conduct of the mandatory test as part of the recruitment process.

It explained that candidates would be required to access the NDLEA Drug Integrity Test portal through designated links or access points to be provided on the respective institutional portals.

The candidates would then complete the necessary registration and documentation on the NDLEA platform before proceeding for the test.

The agency said the arrangement was designed to ensure a seamless and orderly testing process without additional financial obligations for applicants.

NDLEA appreciated the cooperation of the Ministry of Interior and reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring a transparent and efficient implementation of the exercise.

World.title: How To Harness Gains Of AI For Devt, By Olaopa
World.content:
The Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission (FCSC), Prof. Tunji Olaopa, has proposed measures that governments could deploy in order to harness the gains of Artificial Intelligence ( AI) for development.

Olaopa spoke on Thursday in Abuja on “Media And Information Literacy, AI And Youth Creativity” during a stakeholders’ dinner organised by the International Media and Information Literacy Institute (IMILI) in partnership with UNESCO to mark the 2026 Global Media and Information Literacy (GMIL) Week

According to Olaopa, through a proper understanding of Media & Information Literacy (MIL), various competences are being developed for the proper deployment of AI tools . He referred to educational models that help in source

evaluation and fact-checking and AI literacy and integration that lead to responsible generative AI use that paves the way for empowered youth creativity, ethical content creation, and

innovative problem solving.

To Olaopa, when generative AI tools are integrated into literacy curricula, they hold the potential of considerably reducing the cognitive load for younger learners, making complex research and information synthesis more accessible.

According to him, MIL equips youth with the capacity to detect automated text or graphics, and to set strict boundaries, cross-examine outputs, and counter hidden AI biases.

“Thus, a mastery of the dual disciplines of MIL and AI rescues technology from the trap of being an automated shortcut. It rather becomes a path for multi-faceted development”, he said.

He said that to get the best of media, information literacy, AI and youth creativity, the educational system should be reworked to reflect learning models that align with contemporary technological reality.

He said that this should lead to reviewing policy frameworks to formally blend data literacy and AI ethics into mainstream school systems.

Stressing the need for institutional hubs like academic libraries and community media networks that should be empowered to ensure basic AI literacy for marginalized youth, he said this should lead to bridging the infrastructural gap. He decried a situation where while advantaged youth are familiar with even the advanced world of media and AI, there are disadvantaged youth without access to the basic knowledge of media and AI tools, let alone information literacy.

” Such youth need access to the Internet and AI tools in their local settings for their creativity to flourish”, he said.

But to Olaopa, while AI and modern media have opened possibilities in youth creativity, workplaces and democratised information that is essential for the protection of democracy as a counterweight to tyranny as demonstrated in the. Arab Spring and ENDSARS, there is the need to reckon with their bleak implications for humanity.

He said that the late scientist Stephen Hawking was so concerned about the impact of fast-paced technological development on humanity that in 2015, alongside more than 1,000 other experts and researchers, especially in robotics and artificial intelligence, wrote an open letter presented at the International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Argentina.

He said that it was borne out of a collective concern about the possibility of AI — and especially the dangers inherent in “a military artificial intelligence arms race” — being humanity’s “biggest existential threat” and the possibility of this translating into “the end of the human race.”

He said that Hawking wondered if the human race could survive the next 100 years. He said that the anxiety of Hawking was not misplaced amid a world in which machines are increasingly taking over almost every sphere of human life.

“Robotics and intelligent machines have taken over the workplace. They are even taking over the the role of a wife or husband. With their dominance at home, and thus replacing a human wife or husband, Hawking’s prediction might after all not be a ruse but a dark reality awaiting humanity”, he said.

Consequently, he stressed the necessity for MIL that would enable humanity to profitably navigate the technological reality of the modern world.

“Since human beings were responsible for the creation of AI as they were responsible for the creation of the atomic bomb and the Holocaust, it should not be taken for granted that they know how to tame AI. Rather, humanity should step forward and make a determined effort to stop AI from running amok. It is only through that we can enjoy the possibilities in media, information literacy, AI and youth creativity”, he added.

World.title: Tinubu Appoints Prof Ahmad As UDUTH CMD
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved the appointment of Professor Murtala Muhammad Ahmad as the seventh substantive Chief Medical Director (CMD) of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH), Sokoto.

In a statement by the Head, Public Affairs, UDUTH, Mansur Wadata, the appointment is for an initial term of four years with effect from October 20, 2026, and was conveyed in a letter signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate.

Professor Ahmad succeeds Professor Anas Ahmad Sabir, who successfully completed his two-term tenure in May this year.

The statement further stated that while congratulating him on the appointment, Professor Pate reminded him of the heavy responsibilities of his new office and the yearnings of Nigerians for an effective and responsive healthcare delivery system.

He urged the new CMD to justify the confidence reposed in him by Mr. President by working collaboratively with all stakeholders to ensure that the hospital continues to deliver quality healthcare services to Nigerians.

Professor Ahmad becomes the second alumnus of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University to lead the Teaching Hospital as Chief Medical Director, marking a historic milestone for the institution.

With over two decades of experience in Paediatrics and Child Health, Professor Ahmad brings a robust blend of clinical expertise, university teaching, and hospital administration to his new role.

He earned his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree from the Usmanu Danfodiyo University, followed by a Fellowship of the West African College of Physicians (FWACP) in Paediatrics and a Professional Diploma in Education from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. He also holds specialized certifications in paediatric electroencephalography, health leadership, management, and public administration from the University of Cape Town, University of Washington and Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON) respectively.

Before his elevation, Professor Ahmad built an impressive administrative track record within both the university and the teaching hospital, steadily climbing the academic ladder from Lecturer I to Senior Lecturer, Reader, and ultimately Professor of Paediatrics.

He previously served as Deputy Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee (Training) at UDUTH for four years, where he brought impactful transformation to the administration of residency and training in the hospital. He also held key roles as Deputy Director of the Institute of Child Health and Faculty Examinations Officer in the Faculty of Clinical Sciences, alongside representing the faculty on the University Senate, and stepped in as Acting Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee and Acting Chief Medical Director on multiple occasions.

Beyond institutional management, Professor Ahmad has been at the forefront of public health service and specialised medical research in Sokoto State and across Nigeria, with active involvement in maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response, and as a national trainer on the management of severe acute malnutrition. As a prolific researcher, he has published widely in peer-reviewed journals focusing on child health, child neurology, epilepsy, and broader paediatric health concerns, while actively mentoring the next generation of medical professionals and postgraduate students.

World.title: Ondo APC Presidential Campaign Council Inaugurates Eight Media Subcommittees

World.title: Otemu Foundation Expands Scholarship Scheme To 9 States In Niger Delta
World.content:
The Otemu Educational Foundation (OEF), founded by former Delta State Governor, Chief James Ibori, has announced plans to expand its scholarship programme to cover all nine states of the Niger Delta.

The scheme which started in Delta State will now empower brilliant young minds in Abia, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa,Cross River, Delta, Edo, Imo, Ondo and Rivers.

The announcement was made on Friday during the foundation’s second Beneficiary Induction Programme (BIP 2.0), held at the Auditorium of Western Delta University, Oghara, Delta State, where 42 newly selected beneficiaries under Cohort Beta were formally inducted into the scholarship scheme.

The expansion marks a new phase in the foundation’s commitment to widening access to higher education and empowering young people across the Niger Delta.

Speaking at the event, Ibori, founder and chairman of the foundation, said the decision reflected its determination to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent talented young people from accessing quality education.

“What began as a vision to support deserving young people within Delta State is gradually evolving into a platform for regional transformation. We believe that talent knows no geographical boundaries, and we remain committed to building a scholarship programme that continues to transform lives across the Niger Delta for generations to come,” he said.

Ibori described the induction ceremony as more than a ceremonial gathering, noting that it represented the formal entry of the beneficiaries into a community built on excellence, leadership, discipline and service.

He observed that although talent, ambition and potential were widespread across society, access to opportunities remained uneven.

“Talent is everywhere. Potential is everywhere. Ambition is everywhere. But opportunity is not,” he stated.

The 42 beneficiaries were selected through what the foundation described as a rigorous and merit-driven process and have commenced their academic studies at Western Delta University under its full undergraduate scholarship programme.

Ibori charged the newly inducted scholars to approach their academic journey with discipline, purpose and a strong commitment to personal excellence and service to society

The ceremony also celebrated the achievements of Cohort Alpha, the foundation’s pioneer group of beneficiaries, many of whom have successfully completed their first academic year and continue to record encouraging academic performances.

A major highlight of the event was the presentation of a commemorative artwork titled The OEF Tree of Impact to Ibori in recognition of his vision, leadership and commitment to creating educational opportunities for young people.

The artwork featured 55 leaves, representing the total number of scholars across Cohorts Alpha and Beta.

Speaking at the ceremony, the OEF Programme Coordinator, Isioghene Eyikimi, described the induction as a celebration of possibility and purpose.

“Today is not simply about welcoming new scholars. It is about reaffirming our belief that when potential is identified, nurtured, and supported, excellence becomes inevitable. We are incredibly proud of what our beneficiaries have achieved thus far, and even more excited about what lies ahead,” she said.

The event attracted stakeholders from the education and development sectors, including the management of Western Delta University, parents, supporters of the foundation, members of Friends of OEF, and beneficiaries from both cohorts.

Since its establishment, the Otemu Educational Foundation has focused on expanding access to higher education through scholarships, mentorship, leadership development and youth empowerment initiatives.

With the induction of Cohort Beta and the announcement of its regional expansion plan, the foundation said it was positioning itself to play a broader role in developing the next generation of leaders across the Niger Delta.

The event ended with expressions of optimism from beneficiaries, parents, university officials and other guests over the potential impact of sustained investment in education on individuals, families and communities.

World.title: Debt Worse Than Leprosy, Destroys Generations, Says Obasanjo
World.content:
•⁠ ⁠Warns AI may be another booby trap of the West against developing countries

James Sowole in Abeokuta



Former President Olusegun Obasanjo yesterday declared that debt was worse than leprosy because while leprosy destroyed only one person, debt destroyed generations.

He made the remark while questioning how Nigeria accumulated its debt and the impact of the country’s economic decisions over the years.



“And for anybody to say that debt is no leprosy is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person, whereas debt destroys generations,” he said.



“How did we get ourselves into this trap? Can AI help us?”

Obasanjo also warned that Artificial Intelligence (AI) might be another booby trap of the West against developing countries.

The former president stated this while speaking at the Ajibosin 3.0 Symposium, held at the Olusegun Obasanjo Presidential Library, Abeokuta, Ogun State.



The symposium, with the theme, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”, drew speakers from academics, policymakers, politicians and other stakeholders, and featured discussants who warned Nigerians against uncontrolled exposure to AI applications.



Obasanjo, who specifically picked on the lead presentation of the Convener and Founder of the League of Northern Democrats (LND), which dwelt on historical perspectives of AI, admitted that he did not know too much technically about the subject.

He said, “I don’t know too much technically about AI, but I know that anything that is not under your control can be abused against you. You can therefore understand why, in his statement, Dr. Umar Addo approached the subject from a historical perspective.”



Quoting Ardo, Obasanjo said, “Look, these things they call AI, I am looking at them from a historical point of view. Everything that has been packaged and nicely presented to us from the West has always turned out to be a booby trap.

“He was not discussing what AI is or what it is not. Others had spoken about that. His point was that we have seen this pattern before. We have been packaged as commodities.



“First, there was the slave trade. Then they came back and introduced what they called legitimate trade. That was colonialism. After that came foreign direct investment, accompanied by the requirement that we pay for technology transfer. But what exactly is technology transfer? Who transferred technology to them, and what did they pay for it?

“Then came globalisation, which, in practical terms, meant that we opened our doors, they took everything in our houses, and then closed their own doors.



“At another point, they came back and told us that we could not do anything without certain conditions. I believe the World Bank introduced it. Yes, Structural Adjustment. We did not have the necessary structures, yet they came up with structural adjustment.

“Now, consider these things. I once sat with someone like the former Prime Minister of Britain, James Callaghan. He was a sheep farmer and received four euros per annum for every sheep he owned. Yet we were told that we must never subsidise agriculture.

“We were warned that if we subsidised agriculture, we would not receive loans from the World Bank or the IMF.

“The World Bank and the IMF were not designed for us. They were established before we became independent. Yet these are the institutions that determine what we should do.



“We have brilliant young men and women who attended Ivy League universities, Oxford, Cambridge and other prestigious institutions. My children attended some of these universities too. One went to Cornell, one of the Ivy League universities.

“But how can someone who has not managed a home tell me how to run mine?

“These brilliant young men and women package their ideas in impressive academic language, present them to us, and we accept them lock, stock and barrel. We then proceed to implement them.



“In a country of 250 million people, we allow young men and women who may not even be married, let alone have experience managing a household, to tell us how to manage our people and our country. We swallow their prescriptions, and in the process, we destroy ourselves.



“When I started my farm 47 years ago, one naira was worth 1 dollar and 85 cents. That was 47 years ago. What has Nigeria done in those 47 years that has brought us to a situation where one dollar is now worth 1,500 naira?

“What have we done? What do our leaders know, and what do they not know? Of what they know, what can they actually do for us?

“We have 24 million Nigerian children who should be in school but are not. If you are looking for the disasters of tomorrow, these children represent one of them.



“What can AI do for us in this regard? Can AI help us identify the types of food and crops we should produce and ensure that we produce them adequately and in sufficient quantities to achieve food and nutrition security?

“Can AI help us improve healthcare delivery? Can AI help us in the production of drugs?

“I believe these are the kinds of questions we should be asking. We want AI to help us at the grassroots level.



“And I believe that if we are masters of our own homes, particularly in matters concerning AI, we will be able to make AI do for us what we want it to do.”

World.title: First electric MyCiTi buses arrive in Cape Town: Which routes will they serve?
World.content:
Cape Town is acquiring 38 electric buses for the expansion of its MyCiTi service. Image: MyCiti/ Facebook

Cape Town’s first batch of battery-electric MyCiTi buses has arrived, marking another step towards a cleaner public transport fleet.

Seven e-buses arrived from Johannesburg earlier this week, where their bodies are being manufactured. Another 13 are expected next month, with a further 17 due between January and March 2027.

The City of Cape Town is acquiring 38 electric buses for the expansion of its MyCiTi service to the metro-south east.



Which MyCiTi routes will get the electric buses?

If all goes according to plan, 21 of the electric buses will initially operate on the N2 Express service.

The route runs along the N2 highway and serves commuters travelling from Mitchells Plain and Khayelitsha.

The City says other routes could also be considered. This will depend on available capacity and commuter demand.



The remaining buses will bring the electric fleet to 38 once all deliveries are complete.

What do we know about Cape Town’s new FLEET?

The fleet consists of 12-metre Volvo BZRLE battery-electric buses. They can accommodate 59 passengers each.

They are also the first MyCiTi buses with bodies designed in South Africa and manufactured locally in Gauteng.



The City previously received a prototype electric bus in July. It was tested on various routes to assess its performance on steep inclines, downhill stretches and in heavy traffic.

City Mayco Member for Urban Mobility, Rob Quintas, welcomed the latest delivery.

“Given the steep diesel prices in particular, we cannot wait to see the difference the e-fleet will make in the operational expenditure where these buses operate,” he said.



He added that electric buses could deliver significant savings.

“Some countries operating e-buses have noted a reduction of up to 70% in operating costs,” Quintas noted.

The City also hopes the fleet will support a more sustainable and resilient public transport system.



However, further electric bus purchases will depend on the availability of funding from National Government.

World.title: WHY it’s not only SA questioning 10-year Rwanda F1 deal
World.content:
A new 10-year Rwanda F1 deal is drawing criticism the world over. Not just from South Africa. Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

A new 10-year Rwanda F1 deal to bring top-flight motor racing back to Africa for the first time in three decades has drawn strong criticism. First, from human rights organisation Amnesty International, which described it as a ‘sportswashing prize’ for Rwandan authorities.

Then there’s the human rights backlash over war in neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). As such, DRC Foreign minister, Therese Kayikwamba Wagner, has been even more direct in her condemnation of the 10-year Rwanda F1 deal …

10-YEAR RWANDA F1 DEAL

She recently told The Athletic: “Giving Paul Kagame this platform would help to polish the reputation of an authoritarian leader whose government has contributed to fuelling a devastating war in our country.”



She also added that successive wars “have claimed the lives of millions of our people.” And she alleges that minerals extracted from the DRC are smuggled back into Rwanda to help sustain the conflict. Human Rights Watch has also raised concerns about repression, media freedom and Rwanda’s alleged role in the conflict in eastern DRC.

SOUTH AFRICA SENT TROOPS TO DRC

SA sports minister is adamant South Africa’s bid is not dead yet after naming of 10-year Rwanda F1 deal. Image: File

Moreover, South Africa actually deployed about 3 000 soldiers to the conflict zone back in December 2023. This formed part of a Southern African Development Community (SADC) peace mission. However, the operation faced intense fighting when M23 rebels advanced on Goma in January 2025. 14 South African soldiers were killed, with more wounded.

The deployment ended after SADC terminated the mission in March 2025, amid the rebels’ territorial gains. At the time, many believed the war would hurt any potential Rwanda F1 deal. However, that clearly wasn’t the case. In fact, many of F1’s biggest names are defending Formula 1’s decision to bring Rwanda onto the calendar.



RWANDA F1 HAS ‘LEGITIMATE PLACE’ ON CALENDAR

One such voice is Dr. Helmut Marko, who told RTL that Rwanda F1 has earned a legitimate place on the calendar. “Formula 1 was in South Africa for a long time, and Kyalami, near Johannesburg, was a very popular race. But Rwanda is an emerging country, and it’s simply a fact that different political laws apply there. And as long as sportswashing doesn’t get out of hand, it is a World Championship, after all. That means, of course, that all regions of the world should be included,” concluded Marko. – with GMM

But what do you think? Do you think it’s good that Rwanda F1 will be a genuinely African race? Or are you sad South Africa is missing out? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: SASSA grant money siphoned off, victims demand answers
World.content:
More and more beneficiaries are reporting SASSA grant money missing at the start of every payment cycle. But why? Image: File

We’re regularly contacted about missing SASSA grant money by readers. Dave Marie, for example, said on The South African this week:

“The problem and question I have, is why my SASSA payment only R1 730 and not R2 400 as promised? That is a massive difference of R670.”

He described the situation as a ‘disgrace.’



Earlier this month we also reported on the 80-year-old Gogo who had not received her SASSA grant money in months. Meanwhile, the agency confirms she is still on the database, with monthly payments rolling off as usual but not getting to her …

SASSA GRANT MONEY SIPHONED OFF

Perhaps her details on the database had been altered, and the money siphoned off. Part of the answer may lie in SASSA’s review process. The agency says payments for beneficiaries whose grants are under review will be made later, this month the date falls next week, on Tuesday 5 November.

That date sits apart from the main schedule, under which the Older Persons Grant was paid on Friday 30 October 2026. With the Disability Grant scheduled for Monday 2 November 2026, and Children’s Grants on Tuesday 03 November 2026. The South African Social Security Agency urges all beneficiaries undergoing reviews to respond to official communication and attend appointments when requested.

But also, not to respond to elaborate scam communications asking the same thing of recipients. Likewise, the agency warns that beneficiaries may be scammed by third-party insurance/funeral policy providers. These companies authorise a small deduction from your bank account each month.

WHEN SASSA GRANT MONEY DIFFERS BY TYPE

If you suspect your SASSA profile has been compromised, they only thing to do is change your banking details, which is a timely process. Image: File

As ever, different SASSA grant money payments reflect different categories. SASSA Older Persons and Disability are both set at R2 400. While War Veterans comes in slightly higher at R2 420, along with Older Persons (over 75). Foster Child grant sits at R1 300, and Child Support and Grant-in-Aid recipients each receive R580.

SASSA advises beneficiaries to always keep their bank details current and active ahead of each payment cycle, as outdated information can delay payments. Beneficiaries who have not been paid are encouraged to check whether they have received any communication that their grant is under review before visiting an office.



If you suspect your SASSA grant money is being siphoned off illegally. You will have to go through the process of changing your banking details with the agency. Which, sadly, is a time-intensive process.

But what do you think? Are you missing SASSA grant money from your monthly stipend? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: ‘Tried pushing my car’: Rachel Kolisi on running out of petrol, recieveing help
World.content:
Author and director Rachel Kolisi revealed that she ran out of petrol earlier this week and there was only one person who stopped to help her, via an Instagram Story on Friday 30 October.

RACHEL KOLISI RUNS OUT OF PETROL, RECIEVES HELP

Rachel Kolisi, the ex-wife of Springboks captain Siya Kolisi, revealed that she ran out of petrol earlier this week. She explained that she tried pushing her car off the road but her shoulder was not allowing her to. Then a Woolworths Dash driver stepped in to help her, who she described as an “absolute angel.” Take a look…

“I also ran out of petrol in prem traffic this week. I tried pushing my car off the road but shoulder was like sorry sis, not happening. This man on the bike was the only person to stop and help me. He works for @woolworths_sa and my goodness an absolute angel,” she wrote.



RACHEL KOLISI TO HOST FALLING FORWARD EVENT IN LONDON

Falling Forward is Rachel’s personal project exploring healing, self-discovery and rebuilding life after difficult experiences. Through a documentary, memoir and screening roadshow, she shared her journey of navigating major life changes, rediscovering her identity and learning to move forward on her own terms.

She has visited many cities in South Africa with her events and now she’s taking it to London. She teased the type of coversations to expect via a video. Take a look…

“Being a woman shouldn’t mean carrying everything and making it look easy. We’re told to be strong, to be resilient and to keep going. But it’s also okay if that weight feels too heavy sometimes. You don’t have to carry it alone,” she wrote.



“London, you’re in for a treat. These are the kinds of honest conversations you can look forward to at Falling Forward on the 19th of November 🤍,” she continued.

World.title: FF Plus councillor candidate arrested for removing ANC election posters
World.content:
Two people were arrested for allegedly destroying the ANC's election materials in KZN. Image: Facebook/ANC eThekwini

The African National Congress (ANC) in KwaZulu-Natal has welcomed the arrest of a Freedom Front Plus (FF Plus) councillor candidate accused of removing the ANC’s election posters in the Ray Nkonyeni sub-region.

Michelle Wright was arrested on Thursday, 29 October, alongside another individual after a video allegedly showing the two removing ANC election posters circulated widely on social media.

The pair were detained at Margate Police Station and appeared before the Port Shepstone Regional Court on Friday, 30 October.



The ANC said the arrests marked an important step towards establishing the facts and ensuring accountability through due legal process.

The party said it would not tolerate electoral lawlessness disguised as political competition and this is a violation of the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) electoral code of conduct.

“The alleged removal of our campaign materials strikes at the heart of democratic participation, undermining the right of political organisations to campaign freely and the right of voters to make informed choices without interference.

“Elections must be contested through ideas, policies and service delivery records, not through intimidation, sabotage or the unlawful interference with opponents’ campaigns,” ANC KZN spokesperson Sifiiso Sonjica said.

CAMPAIGN BANNERS VANDALISED ON THE M4 IN DURBAN

In a similar incident in September, the ANC’s election posters and street-pole banners were allegedly destroyed along the M4 in Durban in KwaZulu-Natal.

The ANC eThekwini Region said the campaign material was removed from street poles in the early hours of Thursday, 3 September.



The party said all political parties have the right to campaign and advertise across the country and called on members of the public to report incidents that could undermine the electoral process.

“The vandalising of the ANC’s posters and street pole banners is the highest form of provocation and should be condemned by all peace and democracy loving people,” the party said.

World.title: Eight best neighbourhoods for young professionals in Durban
World.content:
If you’re looking to start a new chapter, move out of your city or move closer to work, choosing the right neighbourhood to live in can be overwhelming. Here is a look at eight of the best neighbourhoods for young professionals in and around Durban.

From the far North in Ballito to the South in Amanzimtoti, each area will depend on where you work and the kind of lifestyle you are looking for.

EIGHT BEST NEIGHBOURHOODS FOR YOUNG PROFESSIONALS IN DURBAN

UMHLANGA RIDGE



Umhlanga Ridge is an attractive option for young professionals who are looking for contemporary apartments, shopping centres, restaurants and proximity to major business hubs. Umhlanga Ride is located near Gateway Theatre of Shopping and the N2. This also makes the commute easier if you work in the North of Durban.

However, Umhlanga is an expensive area with rent reportedly starting at around R9500. There are other areas within and around Umhlanga that you could also look at.

Take a look at seven neighbourhoods in Cape Town to rent for young professionals here.



BALLITO

Located along KwaZulu-Natal’s North Coast, Ballito is popular with professionals seeking a coastal lifestyle, modern apartment complexes and access to beaches, restaurants and shopping facilities. Ballito is further North than Umhlanga and will therefore involved a lenghty commute to work.

This would be the ideal location if you work in the North or if you are a remote worker.



DURBAN NORTH

Not too far away from Umhlanga is Durban North. Durban North offers a balance between residential tranquillity and ease of access to Durban northern business and retail districts. It is worth considering for professionals who want more space, quieter surroundings and access to major routes connecting them to Umhlanga and central Durban.

Starting rent in Durban North is reportedly between R6000 – R7000.



MORNINGSIDE

A more central option is Morningside. Morningside is ideal for young professionals who want a lively social life without living directly on the beachfront. The popular Florida Road precinct which features restaurants, cafés and bars is just a stone throw away. The surrounding residential streets offer apartments and character-filled homes.

Starting rent in Morningside is much lower than Umhlanga and Durban North, cited as starting from R4250 for a bachelor flat.



MUSGRAVE

Musgrave is also a more central option and not too far away from Morningside. So, you could enjoy both the lively social scene and living near the Durban CBD. This works well if you will be working in or around the CBD.

Starting rent reportedly also starts at around R5000 a month.

POINT WATERFRONT

Point Waterfront appeals to professionals who enjoy being close to the ocean, the promenade and leisure attractions such as uShaka Marine World. Its apartment developments and waterfront setting offer a different lifestyle from Durban’s traditional inland suburbs. Point Waterfront offers waterfront views, apartment living and access to coastal attraction.



Rent is a bit more expensive in this area, reportedly starting at around R8000.

ESSENWOOD

Essenwood is worth considering if you prefer a leafy, residential environment while remaining within reach of Musgrave and the wider Berea area. The suburb has a mix of apartments and houses, making it an option for professionals looking for a more settled atmosphere.



Starting prices for rent are reportedly around R5500.

AMANZIMTOTI

Amanzimtoti is located South of Durban. This is the perfect option if you’re looking for scenic beach views and a quiet area to live in. Amanzimtoti is a “sleepy town” with convenience. There are several malls, restarunts, cafes and many apartments are located right on the beach.



However, Amanzimtoti is further south so there is quite a commute. This would be an ideal location if you are working in the South or remotely. The views are definitely worth it.

Rent prices start at around R6000.

COMPARING COST OF LIVING

To compare Umhlanga Ridge, Ballito, Durban North, Morningside, Musgrave, Point Waterfront, Essenwood and Amanzimtoti, you would need to look monthly cost of living for a young professional renting alone in each area. The living expenses will include rent, fuel, groceries, utilities and other living expenses, instead of the rent as a standalone expense.



A cheaper apartment further away from work can easily cost you more due to the fuel price. This would also take away your time as your commute is longer.

TIPS FOR SETTLING IN TO YOUR MOVE IN DURBAN

Choose your neighbourhood carefully – Before signing a lease, consider how close you will be to work, supermarkets, gyms, restaurants and public transport. Umhlanga Ridge may suit someone working in the northern business districts, while Morningside, Musgrave and Essenwood offer access to central Durban. Ballito and Amanzimtoti may be better suited to people working locally or remotely.

Set a realistic monthly budget – Moving involves more than paying rent. Remember to budget for your deposit, moving costs, electricity, water, internet, groceries, fuel, car insurance and unexpected expenses. Also, try to build an emergency fund. The rule of thumb is to have three times your salary in an emergency fund.

Learn your commute and transport options – Spend time learning the main routes to work and identifying alternative roads for busy periods. Durban’s N2, N3 and M13 routes can become congested during peak commuting times. If you do not plan on driving to work research transport options near your home and workplace before choosing a property.

Take in the beauty of Durban – One of the biggest attractions of living in Durban is its coastal lifestyle. Make time to explore the promenade, discover local restaurants and enjoy outdoor activities on weekends.

Prepare yourself for the humidity in Durban – Durban’s warm, humid climate can require a little adjustment, especially if you’re moving from Johannesburg or Cape Town. Keep rooms ventilated, make sure clothes and bedding are dry before storing them, and pay attention to mould and moisture in your home. Get familiar with your neighbourhood’s safety precautions, too, and use well-lit routes and reputable transport services when travelling at night.

Is there anything else you’d like to know about moving? Drop your questions in the comments section below…

World.title: New system to detect leaks and chlorine levels
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A technology-driven water management system is up and running in Mogale City.

It's part of Gauteng government's intervention to address the water crisis.

Gauteng Cooperative Governance launched the project to monitor chlorine levels and detect leaks in municipal reservoirs.

The CSIR is the implementing agency for the pilot project.

Theo Nkonki, Cogta MEC's spokesperson said the system is live in Mogale City.

"It's live in Johannesburg and Crown Gardens. We are able to read a lot of information from that system. We don't have to wait for us to get data that tells us what is the quality of the water that is being supplied. But also if there are problems, if we see that, this reservoir is dropping quite quickly. So we don't have to wait for weeks and weeks for us to get manual reports from individuals or people.

"These systems, they help us to manage actively what is happening with the water system so that a place like Ekurhuleni doesn't have to be really hard done by the fact that it's in a higher lying area. So we can actively look at the system, watch what is happening with the system."

World.title: DA and MKP likely to emerge victorious - political analyst
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Political parties are making the final push to ensure the electorate favours them on Wednesday.

Political analyst Brutus Malada said the DA and MKP are likely to come out on top in KZN, Gauteng and the Western Cape.

He said other parties should prepare strategies to deal with them.

"The biggest winner in this election will be the DA. I think the DA is likely to take three metros to emerge as the largest party in the three metros. That is Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni. The DA is likely to emerge as the largest. The fourth one will be Cape Town, which is obvious. They are already a leading party there.

"But with these three metros, it would mean that the DA now has its hands in the levers of power. So they will determine the kind of coalition that would emerge out of that as the largest party. The other key player, which I think will be a game changer, it's MKP. MKP will be a game changer in two areas. One in KZN in the eThekwini municipality, it's likely to emerge as the leading party and it might actually be able to form a government there. So you'll have an MK party led government in eThekwini. The other place where MKP is going to be a game changer is in Joburg. So I think those who are imagining coalitions in Johannesburg, they need to start thinking about how they will engage with MKP.

World.content:
