World.title: Government to strengthen monitoring in Ministries-Nalumango
World.content:
Vice President, Mutale Nalumango, says the government will strengthen monitoring in Ministries and government agencies to prevent the misappropriation and misapplication of public funds.

Mrs Nalumango says the government is committed to ensuring that recommendations arising from the Auditor General’s reports are followed up and appropriate action taken against those found wanting.

She said this in Parliament today during the Vice President’s Question Time when responding to Bahati Member of Parliament (MP), Sydney Kaweme, who wanted to know the measures the government is implementing to address the rampant misappropriation of public funds highlighted in the 2024 Auditor General’s report.

Mrs Nalumango stated the National Assembly has an important role to play in ensuring that government acts on recommendations contained in the reports, as part of its oversight and accountability responsibilities.

She assured that the government takes appropriate action against individuals involved in financial irregularities, with some cases referred to the courts for prosecution and those found guilty of misappropriating public funds are sent to jail in line with the law.

Mrs Nalumango, however, acknowledged the need to strengthen existing mechanisms to ensure that public resources are used for their intended purposes.

She further called on lawmakers in the country to work with the government in identifying measures that could help prevent the abuse of public funds and strengthen accountability in public institutions.

The Vice President emphasised that the government will continue to operate within the law while taking appropriate action against selfish individuals who deliberately embezzle funds meant for national development.

World.title: Government recommits to promoting sustainable agriculture
World.content:
Seed Control and Certification Institute (SCCI) Senior Seed Officer, Zombe Sikazwe, says Government reaffirmed its commitment to promoting sustainable agriculture, crop diversification and the empowerment of women farmers as part of efforts to strengthen Zambia’s food security and agricultural resilience.

Speaking during the Zambia Traditional Seed and Food Festival, Mrs Sikazwe said the government is shifting its agricultural agenda from focusing mainly on production to promoting sustainable, resilient and inclusive agricultural practices.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government had identified agroecology, agricultural diversification and women empowerment as key priorities in transforming the agricultural sector.

She said the Eighth National Development Plan and the National Agriculture Policy prioritised agroecology as a pathway towards sustainable agriculture.

Mrs Sikazwe said the Ministry of Agriculture is promoting farming practices that restore soil health, conserve water, encourage the use of indigenous seed varieties and reduce dependence on expensive external inputs.

She said SCCI will continue ensuring that farmers have access to certified, diverse and climate-resilient seeds, including traditional and improved varieties suitable for agro ecological farming systems.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government is moving away from overdependence on maize production by promoting crops such as soybeans, sunflower, groundnuts, cowpeas, sorghum, cassava and high-value horticultural crops.

She said the diversification agenda also included integrating livestock and aquaculture into farming systems to create additional income opportunities, employment and resilience against climate-related shocks.

Mrs Sikazwe said the Comprehensive Agriculture Transformation Support Programme (CASP) has placed crop diversification at the centre of its implementation strategy.

She further said the government recognised women as key players in the agricultural sector, noting that they contributed more than 60 percent of farm labour and played a central role in household food security.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government is prioritising support for women-headed households through the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP), improved access to finance and land, women-focused agricultural extension services and training.

She said deliberate efforts are also being made to ensure women are included in seed systems and agricultural value chains.

Mrs Sikazwe added that sustainable agriculture could only be achieved through the combined efforts of government, farmers, the private sector, non-governmental organisations and cooperating partners.

Meanwhile, Gabriel Mapulanga who was representing a Consortium of Civil Society Organizations has called for increased investment in traditional seed systems, saying indigenous seeds are critical to strengthening Zambia’s food security, improving nutrition and building resilience to climate change.

Father Mapulanga said traditional seeds such as sorghum, millet and cowpeas had the potential to help communities withstand drought and other climate-related challenges.

He said the loss of indigenous seed varieties is gradually threatening Zambia’s agricultural heritage, as some traditional crops are becoming less common in farming communities.

Father Mapulanga noted that the disappearance of traditional seeds also meant losing indigenous knowledge on how to grow, preserve, store and prepare traditional foods.

He said women play a critical role in preserving indigenous seeds and traditional food knowledge, describing them as key custodians of the country’s food systems.

Father Mapulanga said traditional foods such as sorghum, millet, cowpeas, bondwe and wild fruits such as masuku are important sources of nutrition but are increasingly being marginalised due to changing food consumption patterns.

He observed that the growing consumption of highly processed foods has contributed to reduced dietary diversity and increased nutrition-related health challenges.

Father Mapulanga said traditional seeds should not be viewed as outdated, but rather as practical solutions to climate change and food security challenges because of their ability to withstand harsh weather conditions and their nutritional value.

He, however, said farmers continued to face challenges such as the high cost of irrigation equipment, limited access to affordable processing technologies, inadequate agricultural extension services and restricted access to seed markets.

He called for increased investment in farmer-managed seed enterprises, affordable agricultural technologies for rural women and policies that protect farmers’ rights to save, exchange and sell traditional seeds.

Father Mapulanga said farmers should be given the freedom to preserve and use their own seeds, adding that seed sovereignty is important to achieving national food sovereignty.

He urged policymakers to integrate gender-inclusive agroecological approaches into national agricultural strategies and support farmer-led seed systems alongside conventional agricultural methods.

He has also called on the private sector, academic and research institutions to work with women-led cooperatives in developing markets and affordable processing technologies that would help retain economic value within local communities.

Women farmers have called for greater recognition and support for traditional seed systems, saying indigenous crops are essential to strengthening food security, preserving agricultural knowledge and building resilience to climate change.

The women farmers’ representative Esther Mumba said women are not merely beneficiaries of agricultural development but key leaders, innovators and custodians of traditional seed and food knowledge.

Mrs Mumba said women play a critical role in selecting, preserving and exchanging seeds, as well as passing indigenous farming knowledge from one generation to another.

She said women farmers remained central to household food security through the production of vegetables, legumes, small grains and other traditional crops.

She however, noted that farming had become increasingly challenging due to unpredictable rainfall patterns, declining soil fertility, rising input costs, increased pest attacks and limited access to reliable markets.

Mrs Mumba said the severe drought experienced during the 2023/2024 agricultural season had exposed the vulnerability of the country’s food system when it depended heavily on a limited number of crops.

She also highlighted indigenous vegetables such as bondwe, chiwawa, kalembula and katapa, saying they contributed to dietary diversity and represented an important part of Zambia’s food heritage.

Mrs Mumba said traditional seeds carried valuable knowledge and biodiversity, adding that some indigenous crop varieties had characteristics that made them suitable for different local growing conditions, including dry environments.

Mrs Mumba said increased support for farmer-managed seed systems, community seed banks, seed conservation and the exchange of traditional seeds among farming communities and young people.

She further urged stakeholders to recognise and protect farmers’ rights while ensuring that women’s knowledge and experiences are represented in agricultural policies and programmes.

Mrs Mumba said women farmers are also adopting agro ecological practices such as compost making, crop rotation, intercropping, mulching, tree planting and water harvesting to improve soil fertility and protect the environment.

She said combining traditional farming knowledge with modern technologies and scientific research will help farmers improve productivity, conserve biodiversity and reduce dependence on expensive external inputs.

Mrs Mumba has since called for stronger support for traditional seeds and farmer-managed seed systems through policies and programmes that recognise community seed banks, indigenous seed varieties and farmers’ knowledge.

She has also urged the government to increase investment in agro ecology and climate-resilient agriculture through practical extension services, water harvesting technologies, small-scale irrigation, soil restoration initiatives and affordable farming equipment.

Mrs Mumba further called for improved access to land, finance, training, technology and decision-making opportunities for women farmers, including young women entering the agricultural sector.

World.title: Africa: From Commonwealth Connections to Economic Opportunity - Expanding Africa-Caribbean Trade Linkages
World.content:
guest column

When Commonwealth leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda this November, they will confront rising trade tensions, geopolitical shocks and supply chain disruption alongside longstanding challenges, such as high debt, limited affordable finance, climate exposure and poor connectivity.

Across Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean, these pressures make diversifying markets, attracting productive investment and building resilience through trade even more urgent. They also increase the importance of regional and cross-regional value chains that can withstand disruptions to established trade relationships.

One opportunity lies in plain sight: stronger Africa-Caribbean economic connections. Shared history, culture and diaspora relationships provide a foundation, as do common ambitions to diversify exports, add value locally and create opportunities for small businesses, including those led by women and young entrepreneurs.

The institutional landscape is also changing. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is building a framework for trade including goods, services, investment and digital commerce, while the Caribbean is deepening the CARICOM Single Market and Economy.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Connecting these integration efforts across the Atlantic could help firms aggregate supply and demand, build scale, and develop regional value chains. and access larger markets. A bigger, more integrated market can improve the commercial case for investment and the economics of cross-regional trade.

Forthcoming analysis by the International Trade Centre (ITC), undertaken with the support of Afreximbank, points to considerable unrealised trade potential between Africa and the Caribbean. But the numbers tell only part of the story.

In a survey of 1,175 businesses and business support organisations only 10% of African companies and 12% of Caribbean companies reported trading with the other region. Yet among those that did, 79% of African firms and 82% of Caribbean firms described their experience positively or very positively. The challenge is less about potential than removing barriers to scale.

Businesses struggle to access reliable market information, trusted partners and appropriate finance, as well as to navigate standards and move goods efficiently.

These constraints are not new. Low trade volumes weaken direct transport links; poor connectivity raises costs; limited commercial relationships restrict information; and smaller transactions are harder to finance.

The priority is to tackle these challenges in a comprehensive way.

Physical distance remains particularly costly. ITC estimates freight costs on African exports to the Caribbean at almost 20% of shipment value, compared with just over 8% for African exports globally. Caribbean exports to Africa face costs approaching 22%. Limited routes and fragmented networks continue to undermine viable trade. Scheduled direct air services between Lagos and Barbados, launched in 2026, illustrate how improved connections can support business travel, tourism and wider services.

Access to finance depends not only on the availability of capital, but on whether viable opportunities can be connected to appropriate financing. Businesses need guidance on available funding and lender requirements, and financial institutions need appropriate instruments and ways to manage risk. Trade finance, working-capital facilities, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms can all bridge these gaps.

Payments also matter, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Slow, costly or uncertain transfers can derail transactions. More efficient cross-border payment systems would reduce both transaction costs and risks. Africa's Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) offers useful lessons for simplifying payments as financial links with the Caribbean deepen.

Beyond trade volumes, value creation extends beyond goods. Services, digital solutions and the creative industries can generate more value within both regions. Africa and the Caribbean have globally recognised cultural assets and extensive diasporas, yet much of the creative value is captured elsewhere. Creators and firms need finance, workable payments, intellectual property expertise, distribution channels and direct access to buyers and investors. Supporting creative businesses, rather than only promoting cultural exchange, would generate more revenue and help jobs remain in local economies.

Governments and institutions can create the enabling environment, but businesses will ultimately determine whether a new chapter in Africa–Caribbean economic relations succeed, especially for SMEs.

Commonwealth trade and investment platforms can connect policymakers, investors, entrepreneurs and business leaders. They offer a way to identify obstacles that no single firm or government can resolve alone. Success, however, means introductions becoming contracts, investment reaching viable enterprises and businesses entering new markets.

The Commonwealth brings an existing economic advantage to this endeavour. The opportunity is to make that advantage work more deliberately for Africa–Caribbean commerce, where physical distance, limited market information and still-thin commercial networks continue to constrain trade.

Through its Working Group on Trade and Investment, member countries are developing a workplan to expand intra-Commonwealth commerce. Cooperation on compatible regulations, mutual recognition of standards and qualifications, and simpler border procedures can help realise these gains.

Close 

ITC's work on investment promotion and digital trade to women's economic empowerment, small-state resilience and emerging Africa–Caribbean business linkages can advance this agenda. Afreximbank's Global Africa vision brings the finance, investment and commercial infrastructure required to turn diaspora ties into sustainable economic relationships.

These capabilities are complementary. Trade policy can open markets; finance helps businesses act; and enterprises sustain commercial relationships.

The practical test is clear: identify viable opportunities, mobilise investment, resolve logistics, finance and payment barriers, connect SMEs to customers and investors, use digital trade to overcome distance and retain more value within regions. Progress should then be measured in transactions, market access and sustainable business relationships.

As leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda, they can demonstrate how a connected Commonwealth can convert partnerships into investment, enterprise and shared prosperity.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Police Inspector, 11 Others in Kebbi
World.content:
Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities.

The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse.

A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said, "the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities," he said.

Though the police said five people were killed in an attack on October 26, while seven others died in attacks on October 28 in the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi area of the state, bringing the total to 12, including a police inspector, locals who spoke under condition of anonymity said over 23 people actually lost their lives in the Lakurawa/Mamudawa attacks on the communities of Koko Besse and Shanga areas of Kebbi.

A source said, "They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted."

He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026.

A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, "I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities. Some of them who fled for safety during the attack are just returning on the assurance by the security agents and government that measures are being put in place to ensure our safety."

He called on the government to come to their aid as some of the residents have nowhere to stay.

Another resident, Aliyu Tailor Besse, said the attack was carried out by the Lakurawa terrorists group.

"What happened was that after attacking communities in Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government, they started moving along the River Niger up to Koko Besse area.They were attacking communities along the River Niger as they moved towards Besse community. Many people were killed in the attacks. Prior to the attacks, those who saw them moving along the River Niger banks had raised an alarm calling on residents of the communities along the area to vacate. Some left, but many others stayed behind," he said.

Daily Trust gathered that a few days before the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi attacks, suspected members of the Lakurawa group also attacked Lafagu and other communities in Boya area of Kaoje, killing the village head, Alhaji Saidu Mujeli, and six others before leaving the area through the River Niger bank to attack other communities in Besse and Shanga.

It was gathered that despite the establishment of an army battalion in Kaoje to curtail the activities of terrorists, attacks have continued.

Police confirm attacks

Speaking to our correspondent, the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, said "it's true that the attack happened but it did not happen in one day and not in one community. It started from the 22nd of this month. The casualties recorded was not in a single attack. They attacked many of the communities in the riverine area and that's why the figure of those killed rose to 12. A police inspector and 11 others were killed in the attacks."

He said members of the Lakurawa terrorists group had earlier attacked communities along the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi axis on 22nd of October, but security operatives repelled them. He said they later carried out attacks on the communities of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi on October 26 and 28.

"Although the joint security teams repelled the attacks, seven people unfortunately lost their lives, including a police inspector," he said.

He added that earlier, members of the Yan Sakai, had invaded Samanaji Market and killed Fulani traders.

"Our police tactical teams deployed by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Besse, responded promptly to restore peace and prevent further carnage. However, three Fulani people lost their lives, while a police inspector sustained injuries in the line of duty," he said.

The state police spokesman said a tactical team of the police had been deployed to the troubled communities and normalcy is gradually returning to the area.

"The police have launched investigation into the attack and is following up on the attackers," he said.

'Attacks sign of frustration'

A security expert, who retired as a Captain in the Nigerian Army, Shehu Abubakar, told our correspondent that the attacks carried out by suspected members of the Lakurawa group in some communities of Kebbi, is a sign of frustration.

"You should understand that a battalion of the Nigerian Army was recently established at Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government to curtail activities of the bandits and Lakurawa, operating in the area. The Lakurawa must leave the area to find a convenient place as base to carry out their attacks. They carried out their attack on the communities along the River Niger bank while migrating to another area to avenge the presence of the army base at Kaoje.

"They can no longer stay close to the area where the battalion is located. They migrated from Kaoje, through the bank of the River Niger, moving through communities of Samanaji, Dutsinmari, Zaria Kalakala, to where they started their attacks at Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi. Now that they seem to have been displaced, the security agencies operating in the state should follow them up in every move they make so that they don't get a convenient place to settle. That way, they may be frustrated to move out of the state," he said.

Military bases in Kebbi

In the last two years, six Forward Operation Bases were established in Sakaba,Zuru,Yauri, Augie and Kaoje. The Battalion in Birnin Kebbi was upgraded to an Armoured Brigade, just as there is a battalion in Zuru.There are also army units in parts of Kaoje and other areas to strengthen military operations in the troubled communities of Augie, Danko Wasagu, Mahuta, Argungu, Arewa, Bagudo and Dandi, but the spate of killings occasioned by bandits and Lakurawa attacks remain a growing concern among residents.

Close 

Kebbi's killing fields

On Wednesday of last week, a large number of bandits invaded Dirin -Daji in Sakara Local Government Area of the state. It took the combined efforts of the security agencies in the area to disperse the attackers.

A week before the Kaoje district attack, three people were killed at Kasabo, a community in Saminaka, Yauri Local Government Area of the state. The community was attacked by the bandits in the early hours of the day when people were preparing to go about their daily activities. A resident, Aminu Usman, said their attackers came in large number to invade the community and that they killed three people while many others escaped through the bush.

A few days before the attack at Kasabo, suspected members of the Lakurawa terrorists group attacked the site of the construction company handling the Badagry-Ilela Supper Highway project at Gubba in Maiyama Local Government Area of the state, killing two soldiers and a Chinese national. The attackers were said to have crossed into Kebbi from Kebbe area of Sokoto, to carry out the attack, it was gathered.

Efforts to get comments from the state government proved abortive, but a top government official who does not want his name in print told our corespondent that the state government was working closely with security agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attacks.

He said, "Governor Nasir Idris has been up and doing on issues of security on the state. No fewer than 109 armoured vehicles and other logistics have been procured for security agencies to fight insecurity in the state."

World.title: Africa: AFCON Every Two Years Again As CAF Reverses Decision
World.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle.

The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation's Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026.

The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition.

CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable.



In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation's 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent.

"The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa," he said.

Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition.

He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future.

Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament.

The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year.

Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries' ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027.

He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa's cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together.

"The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa's rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa's 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world," he said.

"The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa," he added.

World.title: South Africa: African Horse Sickness Confirmed in Western Cape's Cederberg
World.content:
The Department of Agriculture has confirmed a case of African horse sickness (AHS) in a single horse on a property in the Cederberg Local Municipality in the Western Cape, prompting movement restrictions and intensified surveillance to contain the disease.

Laboratory tests conducted by the University of Pretoria's Veterinary Genetics Laboratory confirmed the presence of AHS virus serotype 7 on the property, which is located within South Africa's established AHS Protection Zone.

Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp said the case was detected through the country's veterinary surveillance systems, enabling authorities to respond swiftly and implement containment measures.

"The swift detection of this case in the Cederberg Local Municipality is a good example of how South Africa's veterinary surveillance system works. As a result, the authorities were able to move quickly to the affected area and take the required stringent actions as stipulated in the Animal Diseases Act and deploy containment protocols," Aucamp said.



In accordance with the Animal Diseases Act, 1984 (Act 35 of 1984), and the Western Cape Department of Agriculture's AHS contingency plan, an outbreak containment area has been established and movement controls implemented.

Horse movements within the controlled area ordinarily require a permit issued by the State Veterinarian: Boland. However, the department has advised that no permits will be issued for moving horses out of the affected area, while investigations and surveillance continue.

Veterinary Services, working with authorised veterinarians and industry partners, have also commenced intensive surveillance, tracing and census activities to determine the extent of the outbreak and identify any additional cases.

The department has urged equine owners in the controlled area to cooperate with Veterinary Services and report any animals showing signs consistent with AHS, including unexplained fever, swelling of the head or neck, breathing difficulties or sudden death.

Horse owners are also encouraged to take precautions against Culicoides midges, which transmit the disease. Recommended measures include stabling horses, where possible, from two hours before sunset until two hours after sunrise, avoiding low-lying and wet areas, and appropriately using registered insect repellents and insecticides.

The department has strongly discouraged AHS vaccination at this time, explaining that the currently registered vaccine is live-attenuated and that vaccination during periods of vector activity could result in the vaccine strain being spread by midges, potentially worsening the situation.

Close 

"While there is no proof of large-scale disease activity outside the said property, the department is focused on total vigilance and calls on all horse owners to refrain from AHS vaccination during this period. Veterinary Services will continue to monitor the situation closely and will provide updates as additional information becomes available," Aucamp said.

The department said international trade partners will be notified of the outbreak, with further information on the implications for international trade to be provided in due course.

Updates on containment measures, movement restrictions and permits will be issued by the Western Cape Department of Agriculture. Further information is available from Veterinary Services and at www.myhorse.org.za

World.title: Kenya: No, Kenyan Pastor Victor Kanyari Was Not Killed in a Road Accident
World.content:
No, Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari was not killed in a road accident

IN SHORT: A fake Citizen Digital news graphic claims Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari died in a road accident. But the image is fabricated and uses an old photograph of a separate crash.

Social media posts circulating in Kenya feature what appears to be a Citizen Digital breaking news alert, dated 5 October 2026. It claims that pastor Victor Kanyari has died in a road accident along Kangundo Road in the capital, Nairobi.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The graphic shows Kanyari alongside a badly damaged white vehicle surrounded by onlookers.

Collectively, the posts we sampled received more than 162,000 views and 2,000 likes.

Who is Kanyari?

Kanyari is a Kenyan preacher who heads the Salvation Healing Ministry in Nairobi. He made headlines in 2014 after a KTN investigation exposed staged miracles at his ministry and his controversial KSh310 donation scheme, which he later acknowledged was intended to lift him out of poverty.

Kanyari was previously married to gospel singer Beatrice Wairimu Mbugua, popularly known as Betty Bayo. They had two children. Bayo died of leukaemia on 10 November 2025, prompting a custody dispute between Kanyari and the children's stepfather, Hiram Gitau, popularly known as Tash.

On 26 October 2026, a court awarded Kanyari legal custody but ordered a gradual transition, allowing the children to remain temporarily with Tash.

The dispute, along with his active social media presence, has kept Kanyari in the public eye. He has also announced plans to contest the Kasarani parliamentary seat in Kenya's 2027 general election.

Citizen Digital is the online news platform of Citizen TV, owned by Royal Media Services.

But did the broadcaster report Kanyari's death in a road accident? We checked.

Old accident photo used in fake graphic

We found no credible news reports confirming Kanyari's alleged death or a corresponding report on Citizen Digital or Citizen TV's social media accounts.

In contrast, Kanyari's social media accounts feature recent photos and videos of him going about his usual activities.

A reverse image search revealed that the photo of the wrecked vehicle had been shared on Facebook on 27 June 2024, more than two years before the supposed news alert.

Close 

The earlier post was captioned: "Bad accident on Ngong road joining on to Karen road. Multiple casualties."

The vehicle and onlookers match those in the circulating graphic, confirming the photograph predates the alleged October 2026 crash.

The graphic is fabricated. It uses an old accident photo to support a false claim about Kanyari's death. His recent public activities also contradict the rumour.

World.title: Troubling discovery on state voter rolls sparks action days before midterms: ‘Should have been fixed’
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A conservative legal group filed an election complaint in Maine Tuesday, alleging that more than 3,000 potentially dead people and hundreds of duplicate registrations were discovered on the state’s voter rolls just days before the pivotal midterm elections.

The Public Interest Legal Foundation (PILF) identified 3,181 potentially dead voters and 693 duplicate registrations, urging the state to take action as Mainers prepare to cast their ballots Tuesday.

"Now we know why they were hiding them because there were problems on them," Adams told Fox News Digital. "They have dead people, they have lots of duplicates and they have general problems. It's something that should have been fixed a long time ago."

The complaint, which was filed with Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows, argues election officials have not made a "reasonable effort" to remove ineligible voters from the official list.

TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN IN ELECTION INTEGRITY FIGHT AS STATES GAIN NEW VOTER ROLL TOOL

Adams said the state should have discovered the information, not his group.

"Why does it take a third-party group like the Public Interest Legal Foundation to find these duplicates?" Adams said.

The group is asking the state to take "additional corrective action," warning it "may have no other recourse" but to appeal through the complaint process under the Help America Vote Act (HAVA), a 2002 election reform law, if nothing is done.

The group compared those findings with its previous investigation in 2025, which found 18,453 potentially dead voters and 1,498 duplicate or triplicate registration records in Maine. The state addressed many of the records identified that year, but PILF said some errors remain while "new problems have arisen."

Several searches were used in the analysis to identify records that shared the same address, first and last names and birth year, as well as typos, punctuation errors, common nicknames and birth-year discrepancies.

DOJ GIVES CALIFORNIA 48 HOURS TO REVIEW LIST OF POSSIBLE NONCITIZENS ON VOTER ROLLS

The complaint requests that Maine review the group’s analysis, immediately remove ineligible voters and implement a plan to ensure the state complies with HAVA "now and in the future."

"I hope she gets the job done and removes all these duplicates," Adams said.

Adams said his group has been embroiled in an ongoing legal battle and Bellows has a history of trying to "criminalize" PILF for revealing what they found. PILF sued Maine roughly six years ago over access to the state’s voter rolls and won a federal appeals court case in 2024 that required the state to make the records public.

"There's a history here of Secretary Bellows not wanting the public to know what kind of job she's doing," Adams said.

Adams accused Bellows of focusing on "defending sort of blue theories" rather than keeping Maine's voter lists accurate and up to date.

"Unfortunately, Secretary of State Shenna Bellows is not getting the job done," he said.

MAP IT: DOJ ILLEGAL VOTING CRACKDOWN SWEEPS 17 STATES AS RAZOR-THIN ELECTIONS FACE SCRUTINY

One of Adams' biggest concerns is that someone could use a dead person's registration to illegally vote. He said progressive state officials are reluctant to immediately remove dead voters out of fear they could mistakenly remove eligible voters, potentially leaving the door open for fraud.

"The problem is that sometimes people vote for the dead people," he said.

But Adams said he believes Maine has been trying to keep its problems out of the public eye for a long time.

"Maine has a longstanding problem trying to hide public information about whether or not they're doing a good job," he said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Fox News Digital reached out to Bellows’ office for comment.

The legal filing comes just days before Mainers vote in a critical and tight U.S. Senate race between incumbent Republican Susan Collins and her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson. The winner could determine the balance of power in the Senate.

World.title: Dems' dire warnings about threats to democracy face an uncomfortable reckoning after Alaska election report
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

While prominent Democrats have spent years warning about threats to democracy, dozens of lawmakers and governors who endorsed Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola have declined to respond to Fox News Digital's questions about a reported effort to confuse voters and potentially cost Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan his seat.

The New York Times reported Wednesday that aides to Democratic Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola helped recruit a man named Dan Sullivan to run in an alleged effort to draw votes from Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan – though Peltola's campaign has denied involvement.

Fox News Digital reached out to 42 Democratic lawmakers and governors who endorsed Peltola to ask whether they would denounce the alleged effort to mislead Alaska voters.

As of publication, not a single one has responded.

MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT

'DECOY DAN' SULLIVAN CASE LEADS TOP SENATOR TO BREAK FOUR-YEAR X SILENCE: 'PATTERN OF LIES'

World.title: Federal judge blocks Trump DOJ threats against election workers ahead of 2026 midterms
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A federal judge on Friday temporarily barred the Trump administration from threatening election workers with criminal prosecution over ballots tied to suspected noncitizens.

U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson found that the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security likely violated the Voting Rights Act's prohibition against voter intimidation by threatening election workers with prosecution for processing ballots from voters the administration claims are ineligible, just days before the midterm elections.

"One of the hallmarks of a fair election is the freedom to exercise the right to vote free from threat, fear, or intimidation," Thompson, a Biden-appointed judge, wrote in the eight-page order.

The ruling comes as the Trump administration has sought voter registration information from states ahead of the Nov. 3 elections, arguing that its efforts are aimed at preventing noncitizen voting and protecting election integrity.

BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE BLOCKS VOTER-FRAUD PROBES IN BATTLEGROUND STATES JUST DAYS BEFORE MIDTERMS

The temporary restraining order prohibits federal officials from threatening, intimidating or coercing state and local election workers into halting ballot processing solely because the administration alleges certain registered voters are ineligible.

The order also bars the administration from demanding that election officials remove registered voters from voter rolls, refuse to issue them ballots or segregate or decline to count their ballots based solely on those allegations.

The lawsuit was brought by labor unions and civil rights organizations, including the Service Employees International Union and the NAACP.

"Because the public has a paramount interest in ensuring that election officials and workers are able to carry out their work in accordance with federal law and election procedure, and the official day of the Elections is only a couple of days away, the balance of the equities and public interest weigh in Plaintiffs' favor," Thompson wrote.

"Ballots have already been issued," Thompson also noted. "Americans have already begun voting."

NINTH CIRCUIT QUESTIONS TRUMP DOJ'S EMERGENCY REQUEST TO SET ASIDE 20,000 CALIFORNIA MAIL BALLOTS

Thompson also ordered the administration to notify state and local governments that received the disputed letters that the demands and threats of prosecution contained in them have been blocked.

Earlier Friday, a federal appeals court separately ruled against the Trump administration's emergency request to require California to set aside mail-in ballots associated with roughly 20,000 voters federal officials identified as likely noncitizens while their citizenship status was verified.

The Ninth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied the Justice Department's request to set aside the disputed mail-in ballots while officials reviewed the voters' citizenship status, handing the administration another setback just four days before Election Day.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Justice Department for comment.

World.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening election officials
World.content:
A federal judge issued a sweeping order Friday night blocking the Trump administration from threatening or intimidating election officials amid pressure tactics used by the administration in the weeks leading up to the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

The eight-page order prohibits any action that may “threaten, intimidate or coerce state or local elections officials or workers to demand that they halt processing the ballots of any registered voter solely on the basis that the ballot belongs to an individual alleged by [the administration] to be ineligible to vote.”

U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson, who’s based in California, wrote, “In the lead-up to the election, high-ranking DOJ and DHS officials have engaged in a campaign to intimidate, threaten, and coerce state and local officials and employees who are engaged in administering the ongoing midterm 2026 election.”

The order comes in the wake of efforts to require states like California and Washington to separate out ballots the administration says could be cast by noncitizens. An appeals court ruled against the administration in California this week; the Washington case is pending.

“Although Defendants claim that their actions are designed to halt unlawful voting by noncitizens, their actions are likely to have the effect of interfering with election administration and disenfranchising lawful voters,” Thompson wrote Friday.

The judge’s order extends through Nov. 16, nearly two weeks after Election Day.

The Justice Department sent letters to election officials in 57 of California’s 58 counties last week, directing them to cooperate with the DOJ’s investigations of illegal voting or face investigations themselves.

“As you’re aware, federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections,” a letter sent to an election official in San Bernardino County on Oct. 22 said. “I write to seek your help to protect the integrity of the ongoing federal election.”

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bilal Essayli wrote in the letter that he was attaching a list of “1133 likely aliens” registered to vote in San Bernardino County.

“Within 48 hours, we ask that you commit to working with DOJ and DHS to identify who on the accompanying list is a citizen and who is not,” Essayli wrote, adding, “That means sending us the nonpublic information associated with each suspected alien’s registration,” including Social Security numbers, state IDs or driver’s licenses.

“For individuals whom citizenship status cannot be confirmed, we request that you immediately instruct the appropriate elections official to segregate—not cancel—those individuals’ vote-by-mail ballots until their citizenship status can be determined,” Essayli wrote.

Essayli asserted that the list of alleged noncitizens was created by a “multilayered, multiagency investigative methodology” by DHS. He urged the election officials to comply, reiterating that “The legal consequences for either facilitating or ignoring federal crimes are significant.”

In a Friday ruling, a federal appeals court rejected the Trump administration’s request to force California election officials to segregate ballots that it says are from noncitizens.

The decision followed a separate ruling from a federal appeals court Monday to also deny the DOJ’s bid to block more than 20,000 ballots from being counted over claims of noncitizens being on the state’s voter rolls.

And Wednesday, a federal judge argued that the Justice Department’s request to segregate the ballots “violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” and questioned the administration’s processes for identifying the alleged noncitizens.

World.title: Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed clash over Israel ad ahead of planned rally together
World.content:
Days before they are set to headline a rally in Detroit, Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., traded critical messages in statements released Friday, escalating tensions between the two in the final stretch of El-Sayed’s campaign for Senate.

Stevens said that she expected El-Sayed, the progressive candidate who defeated her in a bitter Democratic primary in August, to formally condemn an ad from an outside progressive group that she called antisemitic, adding that it’s why she agreed to join El-Sayed on the campaign trail for the first time on Sunday.

“This ad tells Michigan families they cannot afford groceries because their money has to be set aside for ‘killing Palestinians,’ and it blames our close ally Israel for everything Michiganders cannot afford,” Stevens said in a statement.

She sought to tie the ad — which is set in a grocery store and suggests Israel and the war in Gaza are to blame for rising prices in America — to comments El-Sayed has made in his own campaign.

“I therefore expect him to apologize for those statements as well,” Stevens said. “Abdul promises to get money out of politics. He can begin by getting Israel out of his explanation for everything Michigan cannot afford.”

El-Sayed is not affiliated with the group that produced the ad, Rebellion PAC, and his campaign distanced itself from the ad in statements to The New York Times earlier this week.

Stevens also called on El-Sayed to take down one of his own ads that featured right-wing commentator Tucker Carlson “out of the same respect for Michigan’s Black community.”

El-Sayed, a vocal critic of Israel, shot back Friday, saying in a statement that Stevens, a strong supporter of Israel, “seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago” and that his campaign’s focus was on affordability and health care.

“That focus is why our people-powered campaign defeated a historic $70M in outside spending from big corporations and AIPAC on behalf of Congresswoman Stevens,” El-Sayed said, referencing Stevens’ support from the American Israeli Public Affairs Committee, a pro-Israel lobbying group, during the primary.

The exchange comes after the former primary opponents had seemingly reached a reconciliation, agreeing to appear at an event in Detroit alongside senior Democratic leader Rep. Jim Clyburn, D-S.C., on Sunday. The escalation is also playing out four days before voters will choose between El-Sayed and Republican candidate Mike Rogers to be the next Michigan senator in a race the nonpartisan Cook Political Report rates as a toss-up.

It’s unclear whether Stevens’ and El-Sayed’s Friday statements will affect their appearance Sunday. Representatives for Stevens and El-Sayed did not respond when asked for additional comment and whether the two still planned to appear at the event.

On Wednesday, Stevens sat for an interview on CNN in which she signaled she would vote for El-Sayed while also calling on him to denounce the ad from Rebellion PAC. That interview came shortly after Stevens’ fiancé, Jason Turkish, told The Detroit News that he was voting for Rogers.

“Of course I’m voting for our Democratic nominee for Senate,” Stevens said. “I’m voting for the Democratic ticket. But I want to encourage this campaign to shut out the hate and to call it out and to make people who are in my coalition, make them feel comfortable about coming to the polls.”

The tensions between El-Sayed and Stevens have drawn in other Michigan Democrats as the party hopes to secure a critical Senate seat in the race to control Congress.

“First of all, I have no idea what the hell Haley Stevens is doing,” Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow said Friday on CNN. “This is a moment where we have to recognize the stakes.”

Democratic Rep. Debbie Dingell, a senior member of Michigan’s delegation, sought to downplay the conflict on NBC News’ “Meet the Press NOW,” saying Friday that she helped broker the event Sunday with Clyburn, who is close with Stevens.

“I think that, quite frankly, a lot of people are trying to create more controversy here, when I think the real discussion should be about what’s been happening in Washington and how we’ve got to stand up to what we’ve seen in the last two years,” Dingell said.

World.title: Manhunt launched after California Spirit Halloween shooting leaves 1 dead, 6 injured
World.content:
A manhunt is underway for a shooter who killed one person and injured six in a Spirit Halloween store on Friday night, police in Fairfield, California said.

At least three victims are “currently in critical condition,” Fairfield Police Department Chief Dan Marshall told a news conference about the incident at the Solano Town Center mall, which took place at around 8:30 p.m. local time (5:30 p.m. ET)

“Our thoughts and prayers are with the families of the victims of this heartbreaking incident,” he said, adding that all of the victims had been taken to a nearby hospital. No further information was provided about those shot.

Detectives were “diligently working to identify the suspect or suspects responsible for this horrific shooting,” Marshall said.

David Bernal told NBC News affiliate KCRA that his wife was in the store when the shooter opened fire but she had managed to escape with several other people through an emergency exit.

“She’s at home right now, still in shock,” he said, adding that she told him she heard “five big bangs, big ones, like loud.”

He added that she started running and made her way “out from the one of the exits on the other side of the mall.”

The incident came hours after another person was shot dead inside a Spirit Halloween store in Madison Heights, Michigan.

“A 21-year-old Detroit resident sustained serious injuries and was transported to a local hospital,” the Madison Heights Police Department said in a news release.

They later “succumbed to those injuries,” the release said.

The alleged shooter, a 21-year-old man, “sustained non life threatening after being assaulted by several bystanders as officers took him into custody,” police said, adding that he was taken to hospital.

“Based on the evidence gained thus far, investigators anticipate seeking criminal charges in this case,” the release said.

The incidents do not appear to be connected.
