NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday invited people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday before reaching Ramlila Maidan, where the INDIA bloc is scheduled to hold a mega rally on November 1.

However, Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI that no permission had been sought for the proposed march from Connaught Place.

In a post on X, Rahul shared the route and schedule of the march, saying, "See you tomorrow, let's walk together."

According to his post, the march will begin at the Minto Road junction near Connaught Place at noon on Sunday. Participants will proceed towards Ajmeri Gate before concluding at Ramlila Maidan.

Responding to Rahul's announcement, Delhi Police sources told ANI that no application had been received seeking permission for a march from Connaught Place. They added that MPs and political leaders were free to travel in their private vehicles to the Constitution Club, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence or any other location of their choice.

The sources also pointed out that Jantar Mantar, traditionally a designated venue for protests in the capital, has been de-notified as a protest site.





They said Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts assemblies and gatherings, is currently in force across the New Delhi area, including the vicinity of the Election Commission.

Police said elaborate security arrangements would be made at Ramlila Maidan for Sunday's rally. Personnel from multiple Delhi Police districts, including the Central District, will be deployed along with paramilitary forces.

Meanwhile, INDIA bloc leaders are scheduled to hold a public programme on the proposed impeachment of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday at 3.30 pm at 10, Rajaji Marg, the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.

The programme was postponed from Friday due to rain in the national capital. Announcing the decision, Gandhi said the leaders had agreed to reschedule it to avoid inconvenience to senior members.

Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Friday, Rahul said, "By consensus, we have decided to postpone today's program (public impeachment programme against CEC) to tomorrow at the same time because of rain. We felt that it would be uncomfortable for seniors to sit in the rain, and we will hold the same program tomorrow."

He also urged political parties, civil society members, journalists and other citizens to join the INDIA bloc's November 1 march to Ramlila Maidan.

Both the programs are about the demolition of Indian democracy by Narendra Modi, by Amit Shah, by Gyanesh Kumar and his crew in the Election Commission," he said.

World.title: Karnataka Congress expels former general secretary Kripa Alva for six years over alleged sting operation

NEW DELHI: The Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) on Saturday expelled former party general secretary Kripa Alva for six years over her alleged involvement in a sting operation targeting Congress leaders in the state. The expulsion takes immediate effect, according to an order issued by KPCC vice-president M Narayanaswamy.The order said the controversy had caused embarrassment to the party because of negative publicity and media reactions. It also cited alleged anti-party activities as the reason for the disciplinary action."As your name has figured in this sting operation case and your conduct in the matter amounts to anti-party activities, on the instructions of the Hon'ble KPCC President, you are hereby expelled from the party for a period of six years with immediate effect," the order stated.According to the KPCC, a show-cause notice had previously been issued to Alva seeking her explanation over the allegations. However, the party said she had not submitted any response so far.The action comes amid an ongoing police investigation into a video allegedly targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah.Siddaramaiah had named her behind the 'defamatory video'. The Bengaluru police said on Thursday that the sexual abuse allegation featured in the video was part of a "fabricated and deliberately constructed narrative"."The evidence gathered so far prima facie indicates that the allegations of sexual abuse portrayed in the video are part of a fabricated and deliberately constructed narrative," the police said in a statement.The police further said that statements recorded from individuals appearing in the video and the evidence collected so far did not substantiate the allegations."Their statements and the evidence collected so far, prima facie, with regard to the allegations made or implied in the recording about any individuals mentioned in the video, is false and concocted," the statement said.Investigators said the original mobile phone allegedly used to record the video had been traced, recovered and seized. It has been sent for forensic examination, with the report awaited.According to the police, the video was allegedly recorded in 2023 and purportedly concerned an incident dating back to 2011. Investigators are examining whether the recording was staged, fabricated or manipulated and are tracing its circulation before it appeared on social media in September-October 2026.The police also said the video was uploaded through anonymous accounts using VPNs, masked IP addresses and spoofed phone numbers. A mobile phone allegedly linked to the YouTube upload was traced to a shop dealing in used and refurbished devices in Delhi.One person connected with the procurement of the device was arrested from the National Capital Region on October 24. Police said preliminary findings suggested that he worked as a freelance social media content creator and may have links with politically connected individuals in New Delhi. These associations are being investigated.Alva had earlier appeared before the Central Crime Branch (CCB) on October 26, where she was questioned and her statement recorded. Police sources quoted by news agency ANI said she had also been questioned on previous occasions.Siddaramaiah had named Alva in connection with the alleged sting operation and obtained a court injunction restraining media organisations from airing or publishing the video. His son and minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah had also alleged the involvement of some Congress leaders.The investigation remains ongoing, with police examining the video's creation, ownership, circulation and the identities and possible motives of those involved.

World.title: PM Modi pays tribute to Sardar Patel at Statue of Unity on 151st birth anniversary

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the

in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, on the occasion of the former deputy prime minister's 151st birth anniversary. The day is observed across the country as

(

Patel had played a pivotal role in bringing hundreds of princely states into the Indian Union.

PM Modi calls Patel architect of Akhand Bharat

"On the occasion of his birth anniversary, heartfelt salutations to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the architect of Akhand Bharat and the Iron Man of the nation.

He dedicated his life to the creation of a strong, prosperous, and capable India," PM Modi said.

He further said Patel's "sacrifice and dedication in the service of Mother India" continued to serve as an inspiration for building a developed and self-reliant India.

The Prime Minister also emphasised Patel's enduring contribution to nation-building, saying his commitment to the country remained a source of inspiration for future generations.





Union home minister Amit Shah also paid tribute to Patel and extended greetings to citizens on National Unity Day.

In a post on X, Shah described Patel as the "architect of modern India" and "the symbol of national unity and integrity".

"On the birth anniversary of the architect of modern India, the symbol of national unity and integrity, the Iron Man Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel ji, we offer him millions of salutations and extend our heartfelt greetings to all fellow citizens on âNational Unity Dayâ," Shah said.

Crediting Patel's courage and foresight with India's political integration, Shah said the leader had brought together a nation fragmented into princely states.

"With his indomitable courage and foresight, Sardar Sahab wove together a nation fragmented into princely states into a single thread, laying the foundation of a strong India," he said.

World.title: ‘Distorians’ cannot erase the profound respect Indira Gandhi had for Vallabhbhai Patel: Jairam Ramesh

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Saturday (October 31, 2026) shared a rare photograph from 1947 featuring a young Indira Gandhi greeting Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who was then Deputy Prime Minister, and said “distorians” cannot erase the profound respect and admiration that Indira Gandhi had for the Congress stalwart.

Mr. Ramesh hailed Patel on his birth anniversary and Indira Gandhi on her death anniversary, saying both shaped subcontinental geography and history.

“Two Indians, both indomitable and resolute. Both shaped subcontinental geography and history,” he said on X.

“Today, we celebrate the 151st birth anniversary of a key architect of India’s freedom and who made India’s unity a living reality. He was also to inspire the White Revolution that came decades later,” Mr. Ramesh said of Patel.

Two Indians both indomitable and resolute. Both shaped sub-continental geography and history. Today, we celebrate the 151st birth anniversary of a key architect of India's freedom and who, made India's unity a living reality. He was also to inspire the White Revolution that came decades later. Today, we also mark the 42nd death anniversary of a most courageous and consequential personality who made a free India strong as a nuclear and space power and catalysed the Green Revolution during her lifetime. This picture taken in early November 1947 in New Delhi during a function hosted by the Prime Minister for delegates to the Asian Regional Conference of the International Labour Organisation shows a 30-year old Indira Gandhi greeting the 72-year old Deputy Prime Minister. Distorians cannot erase the profound respect and admiration that Indira Gandhi had for Sardar Patel and she spoke from her heart on the occasion of his birth centenary. And Sardar Patel's was the only statue of a living person that Nehru himself unveiled in Godhra on Feb 13, 1949. — Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) October 31, 2026

“Today, we also mark the 42nd death anniversary of a most courageous and consequential personality who made a free India strong as a nuclear and space power and catalysed the Green Revolution during her lifetime,” he said of Indira Gandhi.

Sharing the picture in which Indira Gandhi is seen greeting Patel as Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru looks on, Mr. Ramesh said it was taken in early November 1947 in New Delhi, during a function hosted by the Prime Minister for delegates to the Asian Regional Conference of the International Labour Organisation.

The picture shows a 30-year-old Indira Gandhi greeting the 72-year-old Deputy Prime Minister, he said.

“Distorians cannot erase the profound respect and admiration that Indira Gandhi had for Sardar Patel, and she spoke from her heart on the occasion of his birth centenary. And Sardar Patel’s was the only statue of a living person that Nehru himself unveiled in Godhra on February 13, 1949,” Mr. Ramesh said.

Patel was born on October 31, 1875, in Nadiad, Gujarat. He passed away on December 15, 1950.

Following India’s independence in 1947, Patel became the country’s first Home Minister and was credited with the integration of over 560 princely states into the Indian Union.

Indira Gandhi, India’s first and only woman Prime Minister, was assassinated by her bodyguards in New Delhi on October 31, 1984. She was born on November 19, 1917.

World.title: Why Sri Lanka’s tourism is thriving amid crises while Keralam struggles to regain lost ground despite its advantages
World.content:
Foreign tourist arrivals in Keralam continue to stagnate, in sharp contrast to Sri Lanka, despite the two destinations offering comparable tourism experiences and products. Even amid adverse global conditions, including the West Asian conflict, Colombo has managed to surpass its pre-COVID foreign tourist arrival figures. Keralam, meanwhile, has struggled to regain momentum, achieving only around 70% of its pre-pandemic arrivals even in 2026, despite offering a more diverse and arguably superior range of tourism products and experience.

Keralam and Sri Lanka share a striking tropical appeal, characterised by sprawling coconut groves, spice-scented landscapes, mist-covered tea plantations and a rich Indian Ocean maritime heritage. However, Keralam enjoys several natural advantages, with its picturesque backwaters nestled between the Arabian Sea to the west and the formidable Western Ghats to the east. The State is also regarded as the cradle of authentic wellness tourism in India, with its rejuvenating Ayurveda therapies.
