World.title: Kyrgyzstan, UNFPA discuss cooperation on demographic policy
World.content:
Photo: Press service of the President of Kyrgyzstan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. The Ministry of Labor, Social Security and Migration of Kyrgyzstan and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) have discussed priority areas of cooperation in demographic development, gender equality, and social protection.

According to the ministry, the meeting was held between First Deputy Minister Arlen Aliyasov and UNFPA Representative for Kazakhstan and Country Director for Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan Chinwe Ogbonna.

The sides discussed prospects for further cooperation in protecting the rights of persons with disabilities, strengthening social protection, and promoting gender equality.

Particular attention was paid to implementing Kyrgyzstan’s Demographic Policy Concept through 2040, which aims to make effective use of the country’s demographic potential, develop human capital, support families and young people, increase employment, and raise living standards.

Following the meeting, the sides confirmed their intention to strengthen their partnership and continue joint initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life in Kyrgyzstan.

UNFPA is a UN agency working on population issues, reproductive health, and gender equality. Its activities include supporting demographic development, promoting equal opportunities, protecting the rights of women and young people, and improving access to healthcare services.

In Kyrgyzstan, UNFPA cooperates with government agencies on demographic policy, human capital development, and social protection, and provides technical and expert support for developing and implementing relevant national programs.

Kyrgyzstan’s demographic policy focuses on addressing changes in population size and age structure, developing the country’s labor potential, supporting families, and creating conditions for higher living standards.

World.title: Film "44" sets audience record at cinema screening
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. The feature film "44," currently screening in cinemas across Azerbaijan, was met with great audience interest from its very first day, quickly recording a record-breaking number of viewers.

Within 15 days, the film has been watched by 122,000 people, a new record for cinema screenings in the history of Azerbaijani cinema.

Screenings of "44" are consistently sold out, and the number of showtimes has been increased to accommodate the high level of audience interest. It’s projected that the total number of viewers will be even higher, provided that further increases in the number of screenings prove possible.

World.title: Uzbek company opens $40M livestock complex in Belarus
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. An Uzbek-owned livestock complex worth $40 million has been inaugurated in Belarus’ Brest region, with capacity to accommodate up to 10,000 head of cattle, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Uzbekistan announced on Saturday.

According to the chamber, the facility was built by Tashkent region-based Maraqand Meat. As of October 27, it was already housing 4,500 breeding cattle.

The project is part of Uzbekistan’s expanding agricultural investment presence in Belarus. Uzbek entrepreneurs have so far launched 13 livestock projects in the country, with a combined capacity to accommodate approximately 8,500 head of cattle.

The initiatives are aimed at strengthening agricultural and industrial cooperation between Uzbekistan and Belarus, expanding the international activities of Uzbek businesses and promoting the exchange of expertise in cattle breeding.

The companies plan to make more effective use of existing facilities, expand their projects and gradually increase the number of cattle.

Agriculture remains an important area of economic cooperation between Uzbekistan and Belarus, with both countries seeking to expand trade, investment and joint production projects. Their cooperation covers livestock breeding, meat and dairy production, agricultural machinery, food processing and the exchange of technologies and expertise. Uzbek businesses have increasingly invested in Belarus’ livestock sector, while the two countries continue to explore opportunities to strengthen agricultural ties and expand supplies of agricultural products to each other's markets.

World.title: Repsol plans €11.5 billion in Spanish projects through 2030
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. Spanish energy company Repsol plans to develop projects worth €11.5 billion in Spain through 2030, the company said on October 29.

Of the total investment, about 60% (approximately €7 billion) will be directed to initiatives in or around Repsol’s major industrial complexes, which rank among Europe’s most advanced refining assets. Key projects include new renewable hydrogen plants and a third facility producing fuels from 100% renewable feedstocks, complementing existing plants in Cartagena and Puertollano.

In the first nine months of 2026, Repsol reported net income of €5.006 billion, including a positive inventory effect of €943 million driven by higher crude prices. Adjusted net income reached €5.419 billion. The company allocated nearly €3.7 billion to boosting crude and refined product inventories, helping secure supplies of diesel and jet fuel in a tight market.

Repsol has also extended customer discounts at its service stations for an additional month, having already spent close to €100 million on the programme since late March. The company’s tax contribution so far this year totals €10.5 billion, of which 72% (€7.5 billion) was generated in Spain.

CEO Josu Jon Imaz said the investment plan underscores the company’s confidence in Spain.

“In a highly volatile environment, Repsol once again demonstrates that its commitment to Spain translates into action: we are strengthening security of supply, protecting our industrial capacity, and supporting families and businesses. The €11.5 billion for projects through 2030 reflects our confidence in the country and our determination to continue generating industrial activity, jobs, investment, and value for society,” he said.

Repsol also announced a third share buyback programme of up to €950 million. Combined with earlier programmes, total shareholder distributions for 2026 are expected to reach approximately €3 billion, benefiting around 400,000 shareholders, the majority of them minority investors based in Spain.

World.title: Turkmenistan seeks to become digital bridge between East and West, North and South
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. Turkmenistan is seeking to position itself as a regional digital bridge connecting East and West, as well as North and South, while advancing its digital economy and the use of artificial intelligence across key sectors.

This was reflected in a press release published today by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan. The country's priorities were outlined by Deputy Minister of Communications Berdymyrat Berdyev, who is leading the Turkmen delegation at the international forum Kazan Digital Week 2026, held in Russia's Republic of Tatarstan from October 29 to 31.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Berdyev highlighted Turkmenistan's State Program for the Development of the Digital Economy, noting that the country was actively shaping its own digital agenda and seeking to strengthen its role at the intersection of major international transit routes.

He also outlined the application of artificial intelligence solutions in the public and social sectors. In education and healthcare, adaptive learning systems and algorithms for early disease diagnosis are being introduced, while the economy is seeing the development of crop yield forecasting systems and intelligent transport flow management.

Particular attention was given to the city of Arkadag, which Berdyev described as a model of a smart and environmentally sustainable city. Its infrastructure is based on advanced information and communication technologies and green solutions, with Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence technologies integrated into a unified urban management and security platform.

World.title: Uzbekistan’s TMK, Germany’s CRONIMET discuss critical metals cooperation
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. Uzbekistan’s Technological Metals Complex (TMK) and Germany’s CRONIMET Holding GmbH have discussed expanding cooperation in critical metals processing, developing new production facilities and strengthening international trade ties at a meeting on Saturday in Tashkent.

According to TMK, the discussions covered five priority areas for potential cooperation with CRONIMET, which operates more than 70 production, processing and trading sites across six continents.

The parties focused on recovering valuable metals from industrial waste, establishing ferroalloy production in Uzbekistan, manufacturing higher-value-added products and expanding international trade.

Following the talks, the sides outlined further steps to advance cooperation. CRONIMET expressed readiness to prepare a technical proposal for ferroalloy production, explore opportunities to supply rhenium raw materials and consider joint initiatives in metals processing.

The proposed cooperation is part of TMK’s efforts to expand the deep processing of critical minerals, develop domestic production of higher-value-added goods and strengthen Uzbekistan’s position in global value chains.

CRONIMET Holding GmbH is a Germany-based international group specializing in the trading, processing and recycling of stainless steel scrap, ferroalloys and other metal-bearing materials. The company operates a global network of production, processing and trading facilities, supplying raw materials and metal products to industrial customers worldwide. Its activities include the recovery and processing of metal-bearing materials, supporting resource efficiency and the recycling of valuable metals.

World.title: Kazakhstan establishes diplomatic relations with all UN member states
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. Kazakhstan has established diplomatic relations with all United Nations member states following the signing of a joint communiqué with Naoero, according to the Kazakh Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The document was signed by Kazakhstan's Permanent Representative to the UN, Kairat Umarov, and Naoero's Permanent Representative to the UN, Lara Erab Daniel.

"Naoero has become the 195th country in the world with which Kazakhstan has established diplomatic relations. Thus, Kazakhstan has completed the process of establishing diplomatic relations with all UN Member States, marking an important milestone in the history of Kazakhstan's diplomacy", the ministry said.

The communiqué provides a basis for developing bilateral cooperation in accordance with the UN Charter and international law. The parties reaffirmed their commitment to mutual respect for state sovereignty and territorial integrity, the equality of states, and non-interference in each other's internal affairs.

During the meeting, the representatives discussed prospects for political dialogue and the development of trade, economic and humanitarian ties. Potential areas of cooperation include trade, sustainable development, digitalization and human capital development.

The sides also emphasized the importance of strengthening cooperation within the UN and other multilateral platforms, maintaining regular dialogue on current international issues, and developing partnerships between Kazakhstan and countries in the Pacific region.

World.title: Locals protest against proposed AI data centre in Adelaide Hills
World.content:
Residents in and around the Adelaide Hills have said they will fight an AI data centre proposed for a block just outside of Mount Torrens.

Quantum DC is proposing a 1,200-megawatt hyperscale data centre along with energy infrastructure on Collins Road in Tungkillo, about 41 kilometres directly east of the Adelaide CBD. The first stage would commence in 2028.

It had scheduled two community consultation sessions this week but postponed them to late November amid safety concerns.

In their absence, locals instead convened their own protest meetings, one in Tungkillo on Thursday, followed by a public rally in the nearby town of Mannum today.

Local organiser Magdalene Lippett said she had communicated with Quantum DC officials in email, but they had declined to attend Saturday's community event.

She said residents were opposed to the construction, having raised concerns about the use of land, water supplies and the impact of noise and light pollution.

"We're not going away," Ms Lippett said.

" We don't want the data centre, we will fight it using every legal means possible. "

Magdalene Lippett says the community will pursue all "legal means" to prevent the construction of the data centre. (Supplied)

She said the community was not opposed to development, citing the Tungkillo Battery Energy Storage System being constructed at the nearby existing substation.

"There just has to be a point where we slow down a little bit and start to question what trade-offs we're giving up to have this AI data centre there and what are the risks for … primary production, the agriculture and the lifestyles of everyone around that area."

Application on hold

No formal application to construct the Tungkillo AI facility has been lodged with state planning authorities by Quantum DC.

Its chief executive Alby Tomassi said about 80 per cent of the project's electricity needs would be met by two on-site substations connecting to existing ElectraNet power lines, with supply via solar and wind contracts.

It would also construct an on-site gas-fired power station to provide firming capacity, with captured and recirculated rainwater used to meet the facility's water needs.

Mr Tomassi said the facility would not utilise water from the nearby River Murray or existing groundwater reserves.

Quantum DC has rescheduled its consultations to November 20 and 21.

"We respect the community's views, and that is why our engagement is taking place before anything is lodged, so that we hear and consider those views first," Mr Tomassi said.

" What we hear will help inform and shape the proposal we lodge, and a summary of what we heard and how we responded will accompany our application. "

At 120 hectares the infrastructure build would cover an area about a third of the size of Adelaide's CBD and would be larger than the current "Colossus" campus operated by Elon Musk's SpaceXSI, which is less than 100 hectares in size.

Crossbench calls for halt to project

Planning Minister Nick Champion said that any application to build a data centre would need to pass through a "rigorous planning system", including meeting power and water requirements.

Mr Champion said an application's assessment would be determined by the government, and could be handed to the State Commission Assessment Panel or to the minister for evaluation.

"Whatever the pathway, the process is rigorous," Mr Champion said.

Government members did not attend Saturday's meeting in Mannum, however representatives from the opposition and crossbench did address protesters.

Members of the local community attended the protest in Mannum. (ABC News: James Wakelin)

Though the Liberal Party, Greens and One Nation support the local push against the project, they differ on how to approach the question of data centres in South Australia.

"We're not against data centres but at the end of the day you've got to take community sentiment into consideration," said Liberal upper house leader Nicola Centofanti.

"This community is saying right from day dot: 'We don't want it here.'"

Greens leader Robert Simms called on the state government "to put a moratorium on any new data centres and to include data centres within their royal commission", while One Nation MLC Carlos Quaremba pointed to the recent move by the three parties to support a Greens motion to block gas fracking in the state's south-east.

Mr Quaremba said his party took "the principled position" of looking "at everything as risk-versus-reward" and suggested a similar tri-party alliance could be forged on the data centre issue.

World.title: Melbourne Cup 2026: Field, barrier draw, form guide and betting
World.content:
The leading chances for Tuesday's Melbourne Cup have enjoyed mixed fortunes at the barrier draw this evening.

Point Of Law retains favouritism after coming up with barrier 9, while a draw of 18 has prompted a slight drift for Irish runner Trustyourinstinct, who'll be partnered by James McDonald fresh off a four-timer on Derby Day.

Explore our interactive form guide to all the horses set to line up in the 166th Melbourne Cup.

You can also download and print our sweep.

1. Sons And Lovers $21 | Barrier 3 | 57.5kg Read more Read more 6yo gelding (Great Britain)

Jockey: Dylan Browne McMonagle

Trainer: Joseph O'Brien Sons And Lovers kicked off the year with success in Saudi Arabia. (Reuters/Action Images) The honour of topweight this year goes to Sons And Lovers, one of five horses in the race for Irish trainer Joseph O'Brien who won the Cup with Rekindling in 2017. A consistent stayer across his 19-start career, Sons And Lovers began 2026 with a narrow victory over 3,000 metres in Saudi Arabia, and in July claimed the Prix Maurice de Nieuil (2,800m) in Paris where he took the lead from the start and refused to be passed. The six-year-old rounded off his Cup preparations with a second in the Kilternan Stakes (2,414m) in Ireland; behind him that day were stablemates and fellow Cup rivals James J Braddock and Goodie Two Shoes. Sons And Lovers has the services of Dylan Browne McMonagle, whose initial Cup mount Defiantly was withdrawn by stewards on Saturday after failing a vet inspection. 2. Trustyourinstinct $8 | Barrier 18 | 57kg Read more Read more 7yo gelding (Ireland)

Jockey: James McDonald

Trainer: Joseph O'Brien Trustyourinstinct is among the leading chances for the international raiders. (PA Images via Getty Images: Niall Carson) Trustyourinstinct is a winner of two races this year in his native Ireland, including the Curragh Cup (2,816m) where he defeated one-time 2025 Cup favourite Al Riffa. His final run before heading Down Under was a well-held fourth when no match for star stayer Scandinavia in the Irish St Leger (2,816m) in September. Trustyourinstinct seems to produce his best when he's held up for a final sprint, and he'll have no better jockey than James McDonald to present him at the right time on Tuesday. McDonald, a winner aboard Verry Elleegant in 2020, will be sporting the famous green and yellow silks of JP McManus, whose major victories include the Cheltenham Gold Cup and Grand National. 3. Knight's Choice $34 | Barrier 2 | 56.5kg Read more Read more 7yo gelding (Australia)

Jockey: Robbie Dolan

Trainer: John Symons & Sheila Laxon Knight's Choice is out to repeat his narrow victory in 2024. (AAP: James Ross) Knight's Choice and his singing jockey Robbie Dolan landed a shock victory at $91 in 2024 and they're back for an encore; note that only the great Peter Pan (1932, 1934) has won non-consecutive Cups. The now seven-year-old had been sidelined by injury after his famous Cup triumph, but he looked to be getting back into form with a close third behind the well-rated Pinhole in the Herbert Power Stakes (2,400m) on October 10. However he was never a factor in an incident-packed Caulfield Cup (2,400m) a week later, finishing 14th behind Kingswood beaten 10 lengths. Improvement is expected back to Flemington but once again Knight's Choice will be an outsider — anyone else sensing some déjà vu? 4. Middle Earth $13 | Barrier 1 | 56.5kg Read more Read more 7yo gelding (Great Britain)

Jockey: Mark Zahra

Trainer: Ciaron Maher Middle Earth ridden by Mark Zahra wins the Australian Cup Prelude at Flemington racecourse on March 8, 2025. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Scott Barbour) Middle Earth (insert Tolkien reference here) finished third for Ciaron Maher last year and has been building towards a second Cup tilt with five unplaced runs this campaign. The seven-year-old made ground from well back in the Caulfield Cup (2,400m) to finish ninth, beaten 5.4 lengths behind Kingswood, Saint George and Enfjaar. A week later he had his final Cup lead-up with a seven-length eight behind Cosmic Crusader in the Cox Plate (2,040m). Middle Earth wasn't suited by the race shape on that occasion and is much better preferred back to a 3,200-metre handicap in the hands of two-time Cup winner Mark Zahra (Gold Trip 2022, Without A Fight 2023). 5. Vauban $51 | Barrier 22 | 56.5kg Read more Read more 9yo gelding (France)

Jockey: Jordan Childs

Trainer: Gai Waterhouse & Adrian Bott Tim Clark riding Vauban wins the Sky High Stakes at Rosehill Gardens on March 15, 2025. (Getty Images: Jeremy Ng) Punters know this former Irish-trained galloper well, as he's helped them part with their money in the past three Melbourne Cups (14th 2023, 11th 2024, sixth 2025). Gai Waterhouse and Adrian Bott have given Vauban a more European preparation for this year's race, having just the one run since his third in the Doomben Cup (2,000m) in May. Just under a fortnight ago Vauban was only fair when ninth, beaten 6.2 lengths, behind Point Of Law in the Geelong Cup (2,400m). He'll derive extra fitness from that run and appreciate any give in the surface on Tuesday as he attempts to become the first nine-year-old to win the Cup. 6. Enfjaar $21 | Barrier 8 | 56kg Read more Read more 7yo gelding (Ireland)

Jockey: Ray Dawson

Trainer: Roger Varian Enfjaar's biggest success to date came in the Glorious Stakes at Goodwood. (PA Images via Getty Images: Andrew Matthews) The winner of five from 17 starts, the English-trained Enfjaar only had his first test over a staying trip in August, reaching a career peak when leading all the way in the Glorious Stakes (2,412m) at Goodwood. One runner behind him that day, Opportunity, has formlines through Cup contender Hopewell Rock, who has form tied to Small Fry, who ran a strong second to Cup favourite Point Of Law in the Geelong Cup (2,400m) — still with me? At his first Australian appearance Enfjaar took up a handy position and fought bravely in the straight to finish third behind Kingswood in the Caulfield Cup (2,400m) and ahead of eventual Cox Plate winner Cosmic Crusader. Provided he can see out the extra distance on Tuesday, Enfjaar should give a good showing for trainer Roger Varian, whose previous Cup runner My Ambivalent finished 17th in 2014. 7. Royal Supremacy $51 | Barrier 21 | 56kg Read more Read more 6yo gelding (Ireland)

Jockey: Ben Allen

Trainer: Ciaron Maher Royal Supremacy is out to make amends for a below-par effort last start. (Getty Images: Jeremy Ng) Royal Supremacy will certainly appreciate any rain to soften the track in his bid to improve on a 15th-place finish in last year's Cup. The six-year-old ended his last campaign with a dominant all-the-way win in Brisbane's rich Q22 (2,200m) ahead of Melbourne Cup winners Half Yours and Knight's Choice. The signs were good when he again led from start to finish in the JRA Cup (2,000m) in September, but he blotted his copybook using the same tactics in Caulfield Cup (2,400m) when he weakened noticeably to finish 15th, beaten 17 lengths by Kingswood. Punters rate Royal Supremacy the outsider of trainer Ciaron Maher's seven runners, and he'll be a second Melbourne Cup ride for Ben Allen, who finished sixth aboard Thomas Hobson in 2017. 8. Wine Dark Sea $61 | Barrier 23 | 56kg Read more Read more 5yo gelding (Great Britain)

Jockey: Damian Lane

Trainer: Harry Charlton Wine Dark Sea will be hard to miss on Tuesday. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: George Sal) The prize for the most eye-catching jockey silks certainly goes to Wine Dark Sea, the design of which is the brainchild of his majority owner, Brisbane roofer Sonny Glebe. Wine Dark Sea won three of four starts in England this year, including the Geoffrey Freer Stakes (2,671m) when he made all from the front and lowered the colours of the highly regarded Dubai Honour, a regular visitor (and winner) Down Under. At his first Australian appearance in the Caulfield Cup (2,400m), Wine Dark Sea was forced to race wide early and hit the front rounding the turn but weakened in the closing stages to finish 11th, beaten 6.6 lengths, behind Kingswood and Cup rival Enfjaar. The lightly raced five-year-old will likely derive a fitness benefit from the outing and has the services of Damian Lane, who is searching for his first Cup win. 9. Asterix $101 | Barrier 6 | 55kg Read more Read more 8yo gelding (New Zealand)

Jockey: Jye McNeil

Trainer: Chris Waller Not many eight-year-olds like Asterix have won the Cup. (Getty Images: Jeremy Ng) Asterix's only start over 3,200 metres was a fourth in the 2024 Auckland Cup before he crossed the Tasman to join the stable of 2021 Cup winner Chris Waller. Fast-forward to 2026 and Asterix scored three victories at Group and Listed level last campaign, but so far this spring his best performance was a third behind Cup rival Zahrann in the Naturalism Stakes (2,000m). Asterix was a distant last on a heavy track behind Cosmic Crusader in the Turnbull Stakes (2,000m), and then made minor headway from the back of the field when 12th, beaten 7.1 lengths, behind Kingswood in the Caulfield Cup (2,400m). The punters aren't giving this veteran much of a chance, and history looms against him as only three eight-year-olds (Toryboy 1865, Catalogue 1938 and Twilight Payment 2020) have won the great race. 10. Goodie Two Shoes $31 | Barrier 19 | 55kg Read more Read more 8yo mare (Ireland)

Jockey: Wayne Lordan

Trainer: Joseph O'Brien Goodie Two Shoes is hoping to go one better than last year. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: George Sal) Goodie Two Shoes has only had four runs since her brave second behind Half Yours in last year's Cup when a $41 chance for Irish trainer Joseph O'Brien. Racing in the famous green and yellow silks of JP McManus, she scored a narrow victory in the Lillie Langtry Stakes (2,816m) at Goodwood in August. But the eight-year-old then raced well below her best and trailed the field behind Cup rivals Sons And Lovers and James J Braddock in the Kilternan Stakes (2,414m). Nevertheless she has made the trip Down Under. Goodie Two Shoes is being asked to carry 3.5kg more than last year, and to her credit, of the 50 mares to run in the Cup since 2005, she is one of only three — High Emocean (2022) and Verry Elleegant (2021) being the others — to have finished top three. 11. Juja Kibo $11 | Barrier 14 | 55kg Read more Read more 6yo gelding (Ireland)

Jockey: Sam Clipperton

Trainer: Ciaron Maher Juja Kibo stormed into Cup contention with victory in the Moonee Valley Cup. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Brett Holburt) Juja Kibo is one of the leading hopes for trainer Ciaron Maher who has seven lining up this year to emulate his success with Gold Trip in 2022. The six-year-old comes into Tuesday's race on the back of successive wins, the first of which was a dominant victory in The Metropolitan (2,400m) where he defeated the likes of Cup rival Soul Of Spain. He then finished over the top of Cup rivals Mr Monaco and Strictly Business to claim the Moonee Valley Cup (2,500m) and punch his golden ticket into the Cup. Juja Kibo is being kept safe in the market and will be partnered again by Sam Clipperton, whose only Cup ride to date was eighth aboard Stockman in 2022.

12. Hopewell Rock $9 | Barrier 15 | 54.5kg Read more Read more 5yo gelding (Ireland)

Jockey: Zac Lloyd

Trainer: George Boughey There's been a good amount of betting interest in Hopewell Rock in recent days. (Getty Images: Sam Mellish) This lightly raced five-year-old worked his way through lower-level staying races in England before winning a handicap over 2,816 metres at Goodwood, defeating one-time Cup contender Small Fry. Small Fry would go on to frank that form when runner-up to Cup favourite Point Of Law in the Geelong Cup (2,400m). Hopewell Rock's form also lines up well out of his close second in the time-honoured Ebor Handicap (2,786m) at York; alongside him that day was Opportunity, which finished behind Enfjaar at Goodwood. Enfjaar would later run a strong third in the Caulfield Cup (2,400m). While he is yet to be tested over the 3,200 metres, Hopewell Rock can handle rain-affected ground and there's plenty of money to suggest he'll give a forward showing with young gun Zac Lloyd in the saddle. 13. Onesmoothoperator $101 | Barrier 13 | 54.5kg Read more Read more 9yo gelding (United States)

Jockey: Declan Bates

Trainer: Tim Fitzsimmons Onesmoothoperator is out to recapture the form that saw him win the Geelong Cup in 2024. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Pat Scala) This former English-trained galloper is making his third attempt at the Cup after finishing 12th in 2024 and 16th last year. A previous winner of the Geelong Cup (2024) and Moonee Valley Cup (2025), Onesmoothoperator's jockey could offer no excuses when he finished 11th, 9.4 lengths behind Point Of Law in the Geelong Cup (2,400m) almost a fortnight ago. It didn't appear to be the run of a coming Melbourne Cup winner, and Onesmoothoperator will need to create history as no nine-year-old has won the race in its 166-year history. But win, lose or draw, it'll be a memorable first Cup runner for Bendigo-based trainer Tim Fitzsimmons, who took over the training of Onesmoothoperator less than a year ago. 14. Soul Of Spain $41 | Barrier 5 | 54.5kg Read more Read more 6yo gelding (Ireland)

Jockey: Tommy Berry

Trainer: Chris Waller Soul Of Spain is one of two runners for champion trainer Chris Waller. (Getty Images: Vince Caligiuri) This Chris Waller-trained galloper finished second in the Sydney Cup in the autumn at his only attempt at 3,200 metres, but his form this campaign doesn't seem to be quite at the same level. Soul Of Spain finished seventh, beaten 6.5 lengths, behind Juja Kibo in The Metropolitan (2,400m) in Sydney before running eighth in the Caulfield Cup (2,400m). He settled well back in a slowly run race that day, and made a bold mid-race move to sit outside the leaders before tiring in the straight to finish 4.7 lengths behind Kingswood. Soul Of Spain's connections will be hoping the likelihood of a wet track will help his chances, but he remains an outsider as top Sydney jockey Tommy Berry continues to search for his first Cup victory. 15. Zahrann $23 | Barrier 11 | 54.5kg Read more Read more 5yo stallion (Ireland)

Jockey: Ben Melham

Trainer: Ciaron Maher Zahrann has drifted in Cup betting following his past two starts. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Reg Ryan) Zahrann was highly rated in Ireland when purchased by Australian interests and shipped to the Ciaron Maher stable as a potential Cups horse. The five-year-old looked on track to justify that aim when scoring a dominant win over one-time Cup contender Saint George in the Naturalism Stakes (2,000m). And despite a well-beaten 11th on a bog track behind Cosmic Crusader in the Turnbull Stakes (2,000m), Zahrann was sent out as second favourite in the Caulfield Cup (2,400m) and settled well back before making steady ground without threatening to finish 3.9 lengths behind Kingswood in fourth. Ben Melham takes the ride, hoping to go one better than his second aboard Johannes Vermeer in 2017. 16. So You Are $19 | Barrier 7 | 54kg Read more Read more 5yo gelding (Australia)

Jockey: Rachel King

Trainer: Bjorn Baker So You Are made it four in a row in the Bendigo Cup. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Brett Holburt) There will be few fitter horses on Tuesday than this grinding stayer, who comes into the Cup after four wins on the bounce. So You Are's winning streak began in the Tatts Cup (2,400m) at Randwick and was followed by victory in the Colin Stephen Quality (2,400m) at Rosehill. Then the step up to 2,600 metres of the ATC St Leger proved no issue, before a perfect ride from Rachel King helped him salute in the Bendigo Cup (2,400m) last Wednesday. While So You Are hasn't been racing against the elite level, expect King to have him positioned up near the lead where he won't go down without a fight — and he won't be afraid of a wet track either. 17. Future History $71 | Barrier 12 | 53.5kg Read more Read more 9yo gelding (Great Britain)

Jockey: Jamie Melham

Trainer: Gregory Hickman Future History makes a second Cup appearance as a veteran nine-year-old. (Getty Images: Vince Caligiuri) Future History squeaked into the field after other runners were forced to withdraw due to fitness concerns; their loss is Jamie Melham's gain as she now has a chance to emulate her victory last year aboard Half Yours. Future History has been running OK without winning since joining the Greg Hickman stable at the start of the year, with his best result a second to Cup rival Royal Supremacy in the JRA Plate (2,000m) in September. Since then he's finished fourth behind Pinhole in the Herbert Power Stakes (2,400m) and ninth, beaten 3.6 lengths, behind Cup rivals Juja Kibo and Mr Monaco in the Moonee Valley Cup (2,500m). One of three nine-year-olds in this year's race, Future History finished 15th behind Without A Fight in the 2023 Cup at his only attempt at 3,200 metres. 18. James J Braddock $13 | Barrier 24 | 53.5kg Read more Read more 4yo gelding (Great Britain)

Jockey: Craig Williams

Trainer: Joseph O'Brien James J Braddock runs in the Cup at only his eighth career appearance. (PA Images via Getty Images: Damien Eagers) Named after the world heavyweight boxing champion of the 1930s (and inspiration for the Russell Crowe movie Cinderella Man), plenty of punters feel James J Braddock and jockey Craig Williams can deliver a knockout blow on Tuesday. A third in the English Derby (2,420m) reflected trainer Joseph O'Brien's high opinion of James J Braddock, but he then disappointed when a distanced sixth in the Irish Derby (2,414m). His latest performance showed a glimpse that he might appreciate the 3,200 metres, staying on strongly before not seeing much room in the closing stages of the Kilternan Stakes (2,414m) in Ireland. The formula of bringing well-performed Northern Hemisphere three-year-olds to Australia for the Cup has proven successful, evidenced by the likes of Rekindling (1st, 2017), Cross Counter (1st, 2018), Il Paradiso (3rd, 2019) and Tiger Moth (2nd, 2020). 19. Kizlyar $41 | Barrier 20 | 53.5kg Read more Read more 5yo gelding (Ireland)

Jockey: Beau Mertens

Trainer: Joseph O'Brien Kizlyar scored a thrilling Royal Ascot victory back in June. (Action Images via Reuters: Andrew Boyers) Kizlyar was a late inclusion in the Cup field at the expense of his well-fancied stablemate Defiantly, who failed to pass a vet inspection and was withdrawn by the stewards on Saturday. He actually lowered Defiantly's colours after a stirring battle down the straight at Royal Ascot over 4,013 metres, and then finished second in the Irish St Leger Trial (2,816m) in August. But Kizlyar raced well below expectations at his Australian debut when beaten almost four lengths behind Cup rivals Juja Kibo and Mr Monaco in the Moonee Valley Cup (2,500m) a week ago. His record shows that Tuesday's distance is of no concern, but he'll need to improve sharply to reverse the disappointment of last start. 20. Point Of Law $6 fav | Barrier 9 | 53kg Read more Read more 4yo stallion (Great Britain)

Jockey: Ethan Brown

Trainer: Ciaron Maher Point Of Law showed sustained speed for an impressive win at Geelong. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Pat Scala) The second of two Northern Hemisphere three-year-olds in this year's Cup, Point Of Law surged to the top of betting following a victory in the Geelong Cup (2,400m) that impressed ratings experts. It was his Australian debut for trainer Ciaron Maher after being purchased in August from King Charles who bred and raced him to a fourth at Royal Ascot over 2,846 metres and a victory in the Bahrain Trophy (2,615m) at Newmarket. European three-year-olds on an upward trajectory have featured prominently in the past decade, namely Rekindling (1st, 2017), Cross Counter (1st, 2018), Il Paradiso (3rd, 2019) and Tiger Moth (2nd, 2020). Ethan Brown stays on board, and many people think he's a great chance to at least emulate his third place aboard Middle Earth last year in his only Cup ride to date. 21. Strictly Business $101 | Barrier 4 | 53kg Read more Read more 4yo mare (Australia)

Jockey: Michael Dee

Trainer: Thomas Carberry The career highlight for Strictly Business was her Oaks victory a year ago. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Reg Ryan) Strictly Business has won two races in her career, and none since her famous Victoria Oaks (2,500m) triumph at Flemington almost a year ago. In the autumn she added a second place in the South Australian Derby (2,518m) to her resume, but the mare has struggled racing against open-class horses this spring. The four-year-old struggled to make ground when 12th, beaten 10 lengths, behind Pinhole in the Herbert Power Stakes (2,400m), and then finished last of 16 behind Juja Kibo in the Moonee Valley Cup (2,500m) a week ago. A sharp turnaround in form will be needed for Strictly Business to figure on Tuesday. It's worth noting that of the 50 mares to run in the Cup since 2005, only three — Goodie Two Shoes (2025), High Emocean (2022) and Verry Elleegant (2021) — have finished top three. 22. Mr Monaco $26 | Barrier 16 | 52.5kg Read more Read more 6yo gelding (Great Britain)

Jockey: Jabez Johnstone

Trainer: Ciaron Maher Mr Monaco booked his spot in the field by winning the Bart Cummings in early October. (Getty Images: Vince Caligiuri) The possibility of a rain-affected track won't bother this former English-trained gelding, who's another of Ciaron Maher's seven-strong attack on the Cup. Mr Monaco won his way into the great race with victory in the Bart Cummings (2,500m) in early October, and then was far from disgraced when a close third to stablemate and Cup rival Juja Kibo in the Moonee Valley Cup (2,500m). He'll get a 2kg weight advantage on Juja Kibo on Tuesday in his bid to improve on his only previous run at 3,200 metres, which was a disappointing 11th behind Changingoftheguard and Soul Of Spain in the Sydney Cup. Mr Monaco will be a first Cup ride for 20-year-old Jabez Johnstone, who's looking to become the first apprentice jockey to win the Cup since 15-year-old Ray Neville saluted aboard Rimfire in 1948. 23. Zakouma $34 | Barrier 10 | 52kg Read more Read more 6yo gelding (Australia)

Jockey: William Pike

Trainer: Grahame Begg The Andrew Ramsden back in May was Zakouma's golden ticket into the Cup. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: Scott Barbour) This stoutly bred six-year-old secured his spot in the Cup with victory in the Andrew Ramsden (2,800m) at Flemington in May. Zakouma's spring campaign has therefore been designed for him to peak on Tuesday; he closed off strongly for sixth behind Zahrann in the Naturalism Stakes (2,000m) and was fifth behind Pinhole in the Herbert Power Stakes (2,400m). Ignore his last of 11 behind Surfin' Bird in the Crystal Mile a week ago over 1,600 metres; that's well below his best distance and the run was nothing more than a maintenance gallop to have him primed for his grand final. Trainer Grahame Begg has engaged the services of West Australian wizard William Pike, who is riding high after his Cox Plate victory aboard Cosmic Crusader a week ago. 24. Shockletz $11 | Barrier 17 | 51kg Read more Read more 5yo mare (New Zealand)

Jockey: Harry Coffey

Trainer: Ciaron Maher Shockletz is out to match her sire and win a Melbourne Cup. (Racing Photos via Getty Images: George Sal) Shockletz's dominant victory in the Archer Stakes (2,500m) in September booked her place in the Cup field, one of seven runners for trainer Ciaron Maher. Her two runs since then have been about having her primed to peak on Tuesday; she recorded good closing sectionals when sixth behind Pinhole in the Herbert Power Stakes (2,400m), and then a fast-finishing second to Soverato in the Tesio Stakes (2,040m) cemented her place among the leading contenders. Shockletz will have to buck history to a degree; of the 50 mares to run in the Cup since 2005, only three — Goodie Two Shoes (2025), High Emocean (2022) and Verry Elleegant (2021) — have finished top three. But she will have the benefit of the low weight of 51kg, which her sire Shocking also carried to Cup glory in 2009 in the same colours of owner Laurence Eales.

Odds at 4.20pm AEDT Saturday

Credits

World.title: Roos make AFLW history with three straight minor premierships
World.content:
Jasmine Garner has spearheaded North Melbourne to a third consecutive AFLW minor premiership in a rousing 68-point victory over Richmond.

Knowing a win would make the Kangaroos the first team to top the ladder three straight times, the captain sparkled in her team's 15.11 (101) to 5.3 (33) thumping at Windy Hill on Saturday.

Her 28 disposals and one goal contribution firmed her position for the league's best and fairest award, the star midfielder playing an integral role in helping North finish its campaign 11-1.

The Roos will certainly be the team to beat in the finals series as they've won their games by an average of 43.2 points and thrashed the second-placed Geelong by 73 points earlier in the year.

Richmond did provide a scare when it kicked two of the first three goals, but the visitors found a new gear, booting the next seven majors to put them in the box seat for victory.

Midfielder Ash Riddell (32 disposals) was typically inspirational, along with forward Tahlia Randall (three goals), while Monique Conti (33 disposals) was busy for the Tigers.

St Kilda's horror season ends with 11th loss

St Kilda was left devastated after its wooden spoon finish was virtually cemented in a weather-affected 7.9 (51) to 7.3 (45) loss to Port Adelaide.

The Saints (1-11) end their season having won just one game and will need either Collingwood or Essendon to suffer a massive loss in order for them to avoid last place.

The loss finishes a tumultuous campaign for the team whose coach, Nick Dal Santo, stepped down midway through the campaign, and the club is independently reviewing the program.

But the Power won't celebrate the result too wildly either, as they needed a huge victory to put themselves in finals contention.

Although they are equal on points with the eighth-placed Hawthorn (24), they have a significantly lower percentage, meaning 2022 All Australian Kirsty Lamb and captain Justine Mules-Robinson won't get to end their glittering careers with a finals appearance.

AAP

World.title: Live: Australia reeling as Rabada nips out three wickets in opening spell
World.content:
Over the wicket to Green, part of a plan I am sure. Good ball, outside off across Green's face, the Australian tall all rounder leaving the delivery from Proteas's tall all rounder.

EDGED! Close! Short leg in place and in the game, making a good stop as Green gets an inside edge that falls short of catching height.

EDGED! And again! Jansen is fast and accurate and Green is getting an examination. Short leg is in the game here.

Solid defence this time from Green.

Well played, Green rides the high bounce and the ball falls into short cover, where he takes off for a single.

Solid defence from Inglis to end the over.

That's drinks, and a big first hour for South Africa.

Chris de Silva will take you through to lunch.

World.title: Joanna Wietrzyk wins first HYROX race after incontinence controversy
World.content:
Australian athlete Joanna Wietrzyk has made a triumphant return to HYROX competition in Germany after taking a six-week break following a controversial incident at a race in Beijing last month.

The 24-year-old from Melbourne faced widespread criticism after continuing to compete despite suffering severe diarrhoea during the race.

Videos showing Wietrzyk running with faecal matter streaming down her legs were widely shared on social media.

Although she crossed the finish line first, Wietrzyk subsequently withdrew from the event, forfeited her points and issued a public apology.

The backlash took a heavy emotional toll, with Wietrzyk saying she considered quitting the sport altogether.

Loading Instagram content

But after stepping away from competition and social media, she returned in emphatic fashion, cruising to victory over Lauren Weeks at HYROX Hamburg in Germany.

The event marked the opening round of the 2026-27 HYROX Elite 15 Series and Wietrzyk's first competition since the Beijing controversy.

The women's solo professional HYROX world record holder said she relied heavily on family support during what she described as a mentally and emotionally taxing period.

Joanna Wietrzyk shared an apology online on Thursday, withdrawing and handing back points from the race she won. (Instagram: @joannawietrzyk)

In an earlier interview with the BBC, Wietrzyk acknowledged she had made "the wrong decision" by continuing to race in Beijing but said she was shocked by the scale of the online abuse.

"To personally experience that was very eye-opening to me, seeing the effect of social media for someone who's 24 and out there racing," she said.

" Yes, I did make the wrong decision but I don't believe I should have received such backlash and such scrutiny online. "

Joanna Wietrzyk (middle in black top) holds the HYROX Women's Solo Pro world record. (Instagram: joannawietrzyk)

"I didn't really think about those around me, which looking back in hindsight, was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry to everyone I did affect in that situation."

Wietrzyk also revealed how close she came to walking away from the sport.

"I've gone through moments and weeks of 'maybe we should just stop' and just go back to doing a normal job and just remove myself from social media entirely," she said.

"I went through a very, very low period mentally and emotionally. It was great that I had my family with me and I could kind of isolate myself from the world but I can't do that forever."

Wietrzyk's next major event is the HYROX Elite Series in London, scheduled for December 3-6.

HYROX is a global fitness race combining 8 kilometres of running with eight functional work-out stations, testing strength and endurance.

World.title: Horses pulled from Derby Day after trainer allegedly has syringes in car
World.content:
Flemington trainer Nick Ryan had two runners withdrawn from today's meeting after Racing Victoria (RV) stewards charged him with alleged possession of a prohibited substance.

Ryan was charged after a stable inspection this morning by RV's Compliance Assurance Team, which resulted in the forced scratchings of Anglaise (Wakeful Stakes) and Doubt Time (Coolmore Stud Stakes).

"Mr Ryan was found to have in his possession, in the glove box of his motor vehicle, two syringes of Darbepoetin Alfa which is a prohibited substance under Prohibited List A of the Australian Rules of Racing," RV stewards reported.

Ryan, a former champion jockey, reserved his plea and the hearing was adjourned until Monday.

Zahra overcomes fall to claim first Group 1 of Melbourne Cup Carnival

Mark Zahra has bounced back from his nasty fall to pilot The Next Episode to a brilliant victory in the stallion-making Coolmore Stud Stakes (1,200m) at Flemington.

Mark Zahra riding The Next Episode wins the Coolmore Stud Stakes. (Getty Images: Vince Caligiuri)

The Ciaron Maher-trained colt stamped himself as the nation's premier three-year-old sprinter, finishing a long neck clear of Chris Waller's St Gotthard in the $2 million Group 1 sprint.

Mbube was third, with Under Focus fourth.

Zahra returned to action today just two weeks after a horror Caulfield Cup fall on Half Yours.

His win in the first Group 1 event of this year's Melbourne Cup carnival comes after his dominant showing with four victories on Victoria Derby day 12 months ago.

It was Zahra's third Coolmore Stud Stakes victory and second in as many years after his win aboard Tentyris last year.

"They're very similar horses. He's a real dude now, this horse," Zahra said.

"He's so relaxed, but when you want him he just goes 'bang'. It's great to be on two magnificent colts within two years."

Zahra took a week off under doctors' orders after his Caulfield Cup fall and missed Cox Plate day, but would not be denied another shot at Flemington glory.

Loading...

"Any other time of year I'm probably having a holiday in Byron or Ibiza, but this time of year you just can't do it," Zahra said.

"I just had to suck it up. It's been a tough two weeks, but this time of year is what I live for and ride for.

"Great help by the doctors and with a few Nurofen today we're bang on song."

It was Maher's first Coolmore Stud Stakes victory. The master trainer paid tribute to close friend Zahra.

"He's a super jock, Mark," Maher said.

"He had the fall the other day, and to get up and be riding at the top of his game, they're marvellous, the jocks.

"Mark's a great mate and I'm sure we'll be popping the top off a couple of champagnes tomorrow."

Earlier, Waller had success in the first race of the Melbourne Cup carnival, when Damian Lane steered The Roaring Sun to victory in the Group 3 Carbine Club Stakes.

Waller had the quinella with Unhinged, ridden by James McDonald, finishing second ahead of Conquer The World in third.

It is the sixth time Waller has won the traditional carnival opener, and third in succession after triumphs by Aeliana (2024) and Panova (2025).

Waller also claimed the Group 2 Wakeful Stakes with De Armas, ridden by Blake Shinn.

J-Mac, Waller combine for Victoria Derby win

James "J-Mac" McDonald and Waller combined for another major victory as Stormy Marco surged home to claim the $3 million Victoria Derby (2500m) at Flemington.

The three-year-old colt charged to the lead in the straight and raced away from second-placed Cold Shower for a stunning victory under McDonald in Australia's oldest classic.

Quick Finish was third as the first filly in the race since 1990, with Murshidi fourth.

It was a fourth Derby triumph for Waller and second for McDonald.

World.title: Two sent off after high shot and punch as Kiwis humiliate Fiji 78-0
World.content:
New Zealand has marched itself into the semifinals of the Rugby League World Cup with a 78-0 thrashing of Fiji, with two players being sent off from the fiery clash on the Gold Coast.

New Zealand was ruthless from the opening whistle, scoring 13 tries in a one-sided contest.

The Kiwis had scored eight tries in the first half and with the result beyond doubt, before the match was thrown into turmoil when each team had a player marched from the field after an ugly episode.

New Zealand winger Ronaldo Mulitalo, who scored one of the Kiwis' eight first-half tries, rushed out of the defensive line and hit Fiji's Ronald Philitoga flush in the head with his shoulder.

That high-shot had the Fiji Bati players seeing red, with halfback Brandon Wakeham hitting Mulitalo with a punch to the head while he was still on the ground.

Referee Grant Atkins sent both players from the field, with each player certain to be on the charge sheet when it is released tomorrow.

Wakeham will play no further part in the World Cup with the Bati failing to make the semifinals, but Mulitalo's hopes of playing in the semifinals appear to be in serious doubt.

One week after giving Australia a huge scare at Lang Park, the Fijian Bati were hoping to pull off a huge upset in Saturday's de facto semifinal.

But the Kiwis were ruthless from the start, scoring four tries in the opening 12 minutes to end any hope of the Bati knocking them out of the competition like they did in 2017.

The Kiwis scored its first try in the second minute through Jahrome Hughes, then crossed again three minutes later when fullback Keano Kini used his speed to slice through the defensive line.

Centre Casey McLean scored the Kiwis' third in the ninth minute, then Bati captain Apisai Koroisau suffered a head knock which ruled him out of the remaining 70 minutes.

When Dane Gagai picked up a loose ball that was dropped by the Bati on their goal-line to score in the 12th minute, the score was 24-0 and the match was all but over.

The Kiwis would score another four tries to round out a spirit-breaking 48-0 first half.

The tension at the Gold Coast did not cool after the two send-offs, with several big shots and a pair of flare-ups between the two sides.

Kiwi lock Joseph Tapine was put on report for a high tackle, while Bati interchange player Jordan Miller was sent to the sin bin late for an alleged headbutt.

The Kiwis would score five more tries in the second half, with McLean ending the day with four.

Jamayne Isaako was perfect off the kicking tee, converting all 13 shots at goal.

The Kiwis will likely face either Tonga or Samoa in the semifinals, while England still has a mathematical chance of qualifying for the knock-out phase.

World.title: Rugby League World Cup LIVE: Kangaroos in control after early scare from Cook Islands
World.content:
This Kangaroos side hasn’t hit top gear yet in this World Cup and have been decidedly clunky again tonight, giving away two errors and three penalties to gift the Cook Islands the bulk of attacking territory in the early stages of this game.

But the Roos do have a ton of talent and don’t need to control possession to score tries, and now Harry Grant goes to the line and links up with Tom Dearden, who breaks a tackle and draws the last defender before sending Tom Trbojevic over for a try in the right corner.

Reece Walsh lands this conversion and normal service has resumed for now.

Australia 10, Cook Islands 6 after 19 minutes

World.title: Chris Waller and James McDonald dominated Derby Day, but Waller wasn’t even there to enjoy it
World.content:
Master trainer Chris Waller came tantalisingly close to making it a clean sweep of Derby Day’s three group 1 races but, in a sign of the times, was not even at Flemington as star jockey James McDonald dominated the start of the Melbourne Cup carnival.

McDonald had a day out with four winners, including the Victoria Derby and Empire Rose Stakes aboard Waller’s duo Stormy Marco and Lady Shenandoah respectively, but they were nosed out by Ciaron Maher’s glamour colt, The Next Episode, in the Coolmore Stud Stakes.

Loading

Instead of basking in the glory at Flemington, Waller was at Randwick for Sydney’s lucrative Golden Eagle meeting, which, along with The Everest, has reshaped the Australian racing calendar.

World.title: Australia v South Africa LIVE: Aussies on the ropes as Rabada blows away top three
World.content:
It’s do-or-die for Marnus Labuschagne.

He secretly would have been happy that the Proteas batted the day yesterday because it’s given him a chance to save his Test career.

There’s already been calls for Josh Inglis to move to No.3 in the order to start the Australian summer in place for Labuschagne. But he can have his say on that matter today.

After falling for a five-ball duck in the first innings, the pressure will be firmly on the Australian No.3 to deliver, with the Aussies needing 288 runs for victory on the final day.

It means the 32-year-old failed to score a Test century for the 48th time in a row - a record for the number of consecutive innings a batter in Australia’s top four has waited to raise his bat at three figures. He hasn’t scored a Test century since July 2023.

World.content:

Former NSW One Nation leader Mark Latham’s day at the horse races has ended in a potential loss of almost $180,000 after the MP was served with bankruptcy papers while at the Royal Randwick racecourse. The bankruptcy notice stems from independent Sydney MP Alex Greenwich’s successful defamation lawsuit against Latham over a “vile, homophobic” Twitter post from March 2023. Mark Latham departs the Royal Randwick racecourse last year. Sam Mooy Latham was spotted being served with papers by a representative of Greenwich, while attending The Golden Eagle racing event on Saturday. When approached by a News Corp journalist who witnessed the serving, Latham refused to comment, calling the reporter a “nosy dickhead”.



Latham is being pursued for about $180,000 in court-ordered damages and interest. When factoring in unpaid legal costs, his total bill exceeds $500,000. Speaking to the Herald, Latham complained he was targeted by the server and media. “When the left say, ‘Lower the temperature in politics,’ I was followed today for hours at the races (of all places) by some server (to deliver documents my lawyer already had) plus the Tele journalist and photographer,” he said. The Federal Court upheld the original finding that Latham’s post, which was highly graphic and referred to Greenwich’s sexuality, defamed the MP. Greenwich declined to comment on the serving, pointing instead to a statement he made earlier this month after the High Court dismissed Latham’s final appeal.



“Mr Latham defamed me in a sexually aggressive social media post that subjected me to an avalanche of homophobic hate,” Greenwich said. “Mr Latham has repeatedly refused to take responsibility for his actions, instead pursuing appeals through the courts,” he said. Latham has 21 days to pay the outstanding debt. If he cannot, or does not pay, he can then apply for a court to declare himself officially bankrupt. Under the NSW Constitution Act 1902, any member of parliament who “becomes bankrupt or takes the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors” must have their seat declared vacant. In June, Latham quietly listed his sprawling five-bedroom family home for $2.4 million, but he says it had nothing to do with mounting legal bills and damages owed in his feud with Greenwich. World.title: How a ghost story from 200 years ago inspired a Sydney tradition
World.content:
NationalNSWCity life How a ghost story from 200 years ago inspired a Sydney tradition Ellie Busby October 31, 2026 — 7:30pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. The local legend starts like all good ghost stories do: with a mysterious disappearance, suspicious townspeople and the unnerving appearance of an apparition with a message. However, it’s how the ghost story is remembered and celebrated 200 years later that sets Campbelltown in south-west Sydney apart from any other Halloween tradition in Sydney. The Fisher’s Ghost Festival parade through Campbelltown. James Brickwood The parade was reinstated after demands from residents. James Brickwood The Festival of Fisher’s Ghost, an event that runs for two weeks until November 8 and features a range of ghost-themed community celebrations, is held in honour of Frederick Fisher and the story of his death.



Colourful floats and performers took over the town centre on Saturday in a “ghost parade” – an event residents have been wanting to return for six years. Campbelltown City Council Mayor Darcy Lound said there was still great interest in the ghost of Fred Fisher. “There’s still people who say today [that] you can still hear noises in our historic Campbelltown Theatre because that’s where his house basically used to sit, where the old Town Hall Theatre is now,” he said. “There’s a thing there when they lock up, they say ‘goodnight, Fred’, and it’s a tradition that still goes today.” Campbelltown City Council’s record of Fisher shows he was a farmer who mysteriously disappeared in 1826 after giving his neighbour, George Worrall, power of attorney over his farm while he served a short prison sentence.



Despite Worrall saying Fisher had sailed for England after being released from jail, the townspeople were suspicious, especially after he sold Fisher’s horse and belongings. Fisher’s disappearance remained unsolved for a few months, the case reopening only after new information appeared in an unexpected way: through a ghost sighting. Related Article Prisons Celebrity murderers, disembodied voices and huge expense: A Sydney landmark’s uncertain future “A bloke by the name of John Farley was in the pub having a couple of beers, and ... he was walking home and came across the bridge, and says he’d seen this ghostly figure sitting on the bridge, pointing to an area of the paddock,” Lound said. “So John Farley, in a panic, ran back into the pub and said he’s seen a ghost, it’s pointing to the paddock. It could be where a body is.” As the story goes, Farley was right and Fisher’s body was found in the paddock. Worrall was arrested and found guilty of his murder, and later hanged.



The first annual Halloween Express picnic trains from Central Station left on Saturday with hundreds of passengers in fancy dress. Audrey Richardson Photo: Audrey Richardson Photo: Audrey Richardson It’s a tale Lound says residents are still fascinated by, describing it as Campbelltown “through and through”, and the reason why the tradition of the Fisher’s Ghost Festival has continued for 70 years. For the believers, the ghost of Fisher is set to make an appearance throughout the festival – although this version is depicted as a smiling costumed ghost wearing sneakers.

World.title: The $1b Powerhouse Parramatta just got its first test run. Here’s how it measured up
World.content:
Exclusive CultureArt & designCity life The $1b Powerhouse Parramatta just got its first test run. Here’s how it measured up Linda Morris October 31, 2026 — 7:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

The Herald charts the ups and downs of the creation of Sydney’s newest cultural institution. See all stories .

Curatorial and installation crews race against the clock inside the colossal, column-free exhibition halls of the Moreau Kusunoki and Genton–designed Powerhouse Parramatta. Amid the tangle of loose cabling, bare walls, empty vitrines and objects under dust covers, it is difficult to imagine that any of the five main galleries will be ready in time for the ribbon-cutting on November 7. Out on the terrace, an array of cutouts depicting endangered birds sits clustered beside an egg-shaped sound shell, where a tradesman works from a basket on a long crane arm. Ground-floor kitchen staff at the upcoming restaurant, Simara, review freshly printed menus before their first service, while 300 front-of-house recruits move through the corridors for final orientation. Matthew Beadle, Natalya Mandelberg and their children, Arabella Beadle, 8, and Baxter Beadle, 6, inside the mirror room. George Chan Four days later, the hard hats and hi-vis have vanished. The sound stage backdrop is fully assembled, and members of the choir and dancers are arriving on Saturday for rehearsals. The ladders and scissor lifts are pulled back, though the construction fencing will remain in place for another week.



Guest services’ hosts dressed in coordinated grey uniforms and necklaced with hot pink “how can I help” lanyards wait to greet the first visitors as a digital commission plays on a 24-metre-long screen in an empty lobby. Some 3000 arrivals are expected over the next several hours; the families and friends of 3000 workers, subcontractors and staff invited for the first dry run of western Sydney’s only designated state-significant cultural institution. A decade of bitter political acrimony that has shadowed the billion-dollar project is all but forgotten in a rush of civic and professional pride by those who have most sweated the outcome. “A dress rehearsal is critical,” says interim CEO Abbie Galvin. “It allows us the time to put the building through its paces, and weed out all about problem. If anything is going to go wrong, we want it to happen now so we can troubleshoot and resolve it and have it ready for the public.” At Saturday’s walk-through, the Beadle-Mandelberg family from Belrose get their first taste of the museum’s marquee aerospace showcase, Task Eternal, an exhibition in four acts which houses the museum’s biggest item a 8400-kilogram F1 rocket from Woomera. The sound stage on the terrace of the new Powerhouse Parramatta this week. Sitthixay Ditthavong



Baxter, 6, gives the rocket-ship playground slide a couple of tries. He’s taken with the stack of planes showing the evolution of flight and the 20 spacesuits and screen-used costumes from Alien, The Martian and Star Trek detailing how our obsession with space and flight has influenced so much in contemporary culture. He and sister Arabella, 8, linger in the room featuring Thai artist Torlarp Larpjaroensook ’s kinetic sculpture inspired by the Voyager 1 space probe. The distortions of reflecting ceiling and floor mirrors fascinate the siblings. The glass-encased Burramattagal Boomerang, an object created in Parramatta, held by the British Museum in London and returned to Parramatta for this exhibition, is the first and last object visitors will see. The 10 larrakitj (hollow-log coffins) drawn from the Powerhouse Collection , also draws admiration of mum Natalya Mandelberg, whose father was a photographer at the Ultimo museum before it was shuttered in 2024 for rebuilding. A spacesuit collection drawn from industry, science fiction and pop culture on display as part of the Task Eternal exhibition. Sitthixay Ditthavong Another space object as part of the flagship Task Eternal aerospace exhibit. Sitthixay Ditthavong



“The scale of it is just impressive,” Matthew Beadle said. “It’s beautifully designed. There are no boring bits. No matter where you look there is an interesting shadow or reflection, or you see an exhibit you’ve just walked through from a different perspective, like the jet engines where you get to see the whole ‘under the hood’, so to speak.” Spectacle is one thing, says Galvin. The success of these exhibitions will be their resonance. “That will be what makes people return.” Inside James Turrell’s Shangri La (Over the Hump), a light installation accessed via Task Eternal. Sitthixay Ditthavong Upstairs of Task Eternal is The Mall, a deep-dive into the phenomenon of the shopping centre and Frank Lowy’s invention of Westfield which is more likely to divide opinions. In the western wing, children venture through tunnels of glowing minerals inside a mock giant meteorite into a recreated childhood bedroom before clambering across a mock windowsill into an indoor Christmas pine forest. Visitors are asked to surrender their smartphones into pouches upon entry – a strict condition of admission designed to preserve a sense of mystery and purely sensory engagement. The Dark, which turns the idea of darkness as a place of nightmares upside down, is made specifically for children aged four to 12 but will engage young teens.



The major outdoor sculpture commissioned for the Powerhouse Parramatta is Tree of Life by British Indian contemporary artist Bharti Kher. Sitthixay Ditthavong In the First Nations exhibition Overflow, adults and children are welcome to shuck shoes and socks to paddle through a shallow sandstone pond. Set within the only gallery offering direct vistas over the Parramatta River and close-up views of the building’s muscular lattice exoskeleton, the space provides rare stillness. Filmmaker Ivan Sen documented seven communities across NSW as they care for water country, the screen images reflected in pond water with its levels shifting subtlety with the river tides. The drop from a viewing platform to the floor of Overflow will be closely watched as well as any trails of wet footprints and discarded shoes in case they raise trip or slip hazards. The exhibition’s design versus function has recently been a point of reflection inside the museum, as has the number of collection objects on display.



Ivan Sen in front of the LCD screen showing images from the exhibition Overflow at Parramatta Powerhouse. Nadir Tolj-Kinani From the moment of its 2015 announcement 11 years ago, the idea to headquarter the Powerhouse in Parramatta has been squeezed by two opposing forces: the ambitions and cultural claims of Sydney’s second CBD versus the wisdom and expense of splitting it from its repurposed home at Ultimo. More than 400 museum staff have worked over the past three years developing and delivering the five opening exhibitions. Staff have acutely felt the intense scrutiny. It’s a relief for many to see the finish line so close, but there are nerves, too. Except for the families’ look and see, no media is permitted inside for the dry run which is a practical test of audio visuals and interactives, installation of labels, signage and way finding. Given the headlines, and like the new Sydney Metro line, the museum says it wants space to deal with any teething troubles and the staff to enjoy the product of their efforts without scrutiny. The Beadle-Mandelburgs say they haven’t followed the controversies anyway.



Related Article City life Powerhouse Parramatta’s $4.5 million opening festival revealed The guiding hand behind all this crisp aesthetic and concept – former chief executive Lisa Havilah, who stepped aside from her position on August 27, pending a departmental investigation into “governance and procurement practices” – remains a palpable presence throughout in the intimate, tailored enclosures carved out of cavernous volumes with its high-end industrial finishes. Only after they open can the public judge if she has found the right balance between embedding western Sydney into the museum and taking its focus international, and in the museum’s delivery of its core charter as a museum of applied arts and sciences and its dedication to its 500,000-strong collection. British-born artist Es Devlin’s labyrinth of mirrors and light-filled maze will be kept under wraps until opening. Devlin has designed large-scale shows for artists including Beyoncé, Dr Dre, Kendrick Lamar, Eminem and U2. Her commissions replace original plans for a Planetarium, still a sensitive topic for supporters of a dedicated science museum. “It’s absolutely Lisa’s vision,” Galvin says. “What’s clear, though, is that an entire team helped shape, develop and deliver it – and that’s what really matters. Any great leader builds a strong team, and any great leader is replaceable.”



The museum expects two million visitors in its inaugural year– a figure that once sounded ambitious to Galvin until crowds swarmed the recent four-day Parramatta Lanes festival. More than 20,000 people have registered for opening weekend, with more than 3245 reservations booked across opening program. Tickets for Task Eternal are still available – an entry point to the museum. The Beadle-Mandelburgs agree that the complex is far too vast to absorb in a single visit. It took them 40 minutes to travel by car, and they easily found street parking, putting to bed early public anxieties around access. They’d be back in a heart-beat, even if they had to travel twice the distance. Related Article Exclusive

Arts Powerhouse slammed over Kylie Kwong’s new $440,000 ambassador role Come Monday, staff will be back working up to the last hour to ready the museum for its big ribbon-cutting. It’s director of program, Clare Holland, said the to-do list was getting shorter but was not yet complete. “All the teams are focused on making sure every part is perfect for opening. I love watching people’s faces as they see parts of the building, or exhibitions for the first time.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

Master trainer Chris Waller came tantalisingly close to making it a clean sweep of Derby Day’s three group 1 races but, in a sign of the times, was not even at Flemington as star jockey James McDonald dominated the start of the Melbourne Cup carnival.

McDonald had a day out with four winners, including the Victoria Derby and Empire Rose Stakes aboard Waller’s duo Stormy Marco and Lady Shenandoah respectively, but they were nosed out by Ciaron Maher’s glamour colt, The Next Episode, in the Coolmore Stud Stakes.
